verses.devanagari: পীড়াভির্নবকালকূটকটুতা-গর্বস্য নির্বাসনো\\nনিঃস্যন্দেন মুদাং সুধা-মধুরিমাহঙ্কর-সঙ্কোচনঃ ।\\nপ্রেমা সুন্দরি নন্দনন্দনপরো জাগর্তি যস্যান্তরে\\nজ্ঞায়ন্তে স্ফুটমস্য বক্রমধুরাস্তেনৈব বিক্রান্তয়ঃ ॥১৪৮॥
verses.transliteration: pīḍābhir nava-kāla-kūṭa-kaṭutā-garvasya nirvāsano\\nnisyandena mudāṁ sudhā-madhurimāhaṅkāra-saṅkocanaḥ\\npremā sundari nanda-nandana-paro jāgarti yasyāntare\\njñāyante sphuṭam asya vakra-madhurās tenaiva vikrāntayaḥ
verses.translation: 'My dear beautiful friend, if one develops love of Godhead, love of Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda Mahārāja, all the bitter and sweet influences of this love will manifest in one's heart. Such love of Godhead acts in two ways. The poisonous effects of love of Godhead defeat the severe and fresh poison of the serpent. Yet there is simultaneously transcendental bliss, which pours down and defeats the poisonous effects of a snake, as well as the happiness derived from pouring nectar on one's head. It is perceived as doubly effective, simultaneously poisonous and nectarean.' "
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse is from the
Vidagdha-mādhava
(2.18). It also appears in
Madhya-līlā,
Chapter Two, verse 52. It is spoken by Paurṇamāsī.

verses.devanagari: রায় কহে, — “কহ সহজ-প্রেমের লক্ষণ” ।\\nরূপ-গোসাঞি কহে, “সাহজিক প্রেমধর্ম” ॥১৪৯॥
verses.transliteration: rāya kahe,—"kaha sahaja-premera lakṣaṇa"\\nrūpa-gosāñi kahe,—"sāhajika prema-dharma"
verses.translation: Rāmānanda Rāya further inquired, "What are the natural characteristics of awakening love of Godhead?" Rūpa Gosvāmī replied, "These are the natural characteristics of love of God.

verses.devanagari: স্তোত্রং যত্র তটস্থতাং প্রকটয়চ্চিত্তস্য ধত্তে ব্যথাং\\nনিন্দাপি প্রমদং প্রযচ্ছতি পরীহাসশ্রিয়ং বিভ্রতী ।\\nদোষেণ ক্ষয়িতাং গুণেন গুরুতাং কেনাপ্যনাতন্বতী\\nপ্রেম্ণঃ স্বারসিকস্য কস্যচিদিয়ং বিক্রীড়তি প্রক্রিয়া ॥১৫০॥
verses.transliteration: stotraṁ yatra taṭa-sthatāṁ prakaṭayac cittasya dhatte vyathāṁ\\nnindāpi pramadaṁ prayacchati parīhāsa-śriyaṁ bibhratī\\ndoṣeṇa kṣayitām guṇena gurutāṁ kenāpy anātanvatī\\npremṇaḥ svārasikasya kasyacid iyaṁ vikrīḍati prakriyā
verses.translation: 'When one hears praise from his beloved, he outwardIy remains neutral but feels pain within his heart. When he hears his beloved making accusations about him, he takes them to be jokes and enjoys pleasure. When he finds faults in his beloved, they do not diminish his love, nor do the beloved's good qualities increase his spontaneous affection. Thus spontaneous love continues under all circumstances. That is how spontaneous love of Godhead acts within the heart.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse from
Vidagdha-mādhava
(5.4) is spoken by Paurṇamāsī, the grandmother of Rādhārāṇī and mother of Sāndīpani Muni.

verses.devanagari: শ্রুত্বা নিষ্ঠুরতাং মমেন্দুবদনা প্রেমাঙ্কুরং ভিন্ধতী\\nস্বান্তে শান্তিধুরাং বিধায় বিধুরে প্রায়ঃ পরাঞ্চিষ্যতি ।\\nকিংবা পামর-কাম-কার্মুকপরিত্রস্তা বিমোক্ষ্যত্যসূন্\\nহা মৌগ্ধ্যাৎ ফলিনী মনোরথলতা মৃদ্বী ময়োন্মূলিতা ॥১৫১॥
verses.transliteration: śrutvā niṣṭhuratāṁ mamendu-vadanā premāṅkuraṁ bhindatī\\nsvānte śānti-dhurāṁ vidhāya vidhure prāyaḥ parāñciṣyati\\nkiṁvā pāmara-kāma-kārmuka-paritrastā vimokṣyaty asūn\\nhā maugdhyāt phalinī manoratha-latā mṛdvī mayonmūlitā
verses.translation: 'Upon hearing of My cruelty, moon-faced Rādhārāṇī may establish some kind of tolerance in Her aggrieved heart. But then She might turn against Me. Or, indeed, being fearful of the lusty desires invoked by the bow of formidable Cupid, She might even give up Her life. Alas! I have foolishly uprooted the soft creeper of Her desire just when it was ready to bear fruit.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Having been very cruel to Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, Kṛṣṇa is repenting in this way (
Vidagdha-mādhava
2.40).

verses.devanagari: যস্যোৎসঙ্গসুখাশয়া শিথিলিতা গুর্বী গুরুভ্যস্ত্রপা\\nপ্রাণেভ্যোঽপি সুহৃত্তমাঃ সখি তথা যূয়ং পরিক্লেশিতাঃ ।\\nধর্মঃ সোঽপি মহান্ময়া ন গণিতঃ সাধ্বীভিরধ্যাসিতো\\nধিগ্ধৈর্যং তদুপেক্ষিতাপি যদহং জীবামি পাপীয়সী ॥১৫২॥
verses.transliteration: yasyotsaṅga-sukhāśayā śithilitā gurvī gurubhyas trapā\\nprāṇebhyo 'pi suhṛt-tamāḥ sakhi tathā yūyaṁ parikleśitāḥ\\ndharmaḥ so 'pi mahān mayā na gaṇitaḥ sādhvībhir adhyāsito\\ndhig dhairyaṁ tad-upekṣitāpi yad ahaṁ jīvāmi pāpīyasī
verses.translation: 'Desiring the happiness of His association and embraces, My dear friend, I disregarded even My superiors and relaxed My shyness and gravity before them. Furthermore, although you are My best friend, more dear to Me than My own life, I have given you so much trouble. Indeed, I even put aside the vow of dedication to My husband, a vow kept by the most elevated women. Oh, alas! Although He is now neglecting Me, I am so sinful that I am still living. Therefore I must condemn My so-called patience.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is speaking this verse (
Vidagdha-mādhava
2.41) to Her intimate friend Viśākhādevī.

verses.devanagari: গৃহান্তঃখেলন্ত্যো নিজসহজবাল্যস্য বলনা-\\nদভদ্রং ভদ্রং বা কিমপি হি ন জানীমহি মনাক্ ।\\nবয়ং নেতুং যুক্তাঃ কথমশরণাং কামপি দশাং\\nকথং বা ন্যায্যা তে প্রথয়িতুমুদাসীনপদবী ॥১৫৩॥
verses.transliteration: gṛhāntaḥ-khelantyo nija-sahaja-bālyasya balanād\\nabhadraṁ bhadraṁ vā kim api hi na jānīmahi manāk\\nvayaṁ netuṁ yuktāḥ katham aśaraṇāṁ kā api daśāṁ\\nkathaṁ vā nyāyyā te prathayitum udāsīna-padavī
verses.translation: 'I was engaged in My own playful activities in My home, and because of My childish innocence I did not know right from wrong. Therefore, is it good for You to have forced us into being so much attracted to You and then to have neglected us? Now You are indifferent to us. Do You think that is right?'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse (
Vidagdha-mādhava
2.46) is spoken to Kṛṣṇa by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.

verses.devanagari: অন্তঃক্লেশকলঙ্কিতাঃ কিল বয়ং যামোঽদ্য যাম্যাং পুরীং\\nনায়ং বঞ্চনসঞ্চয়প্রণয়িনং হাসং তথাপ্যুজ্ঝতি ।\\nঅস্মিন্ সম্পুটিতে গভীরকপটৈরাভীরপল্লীবিটে\\nহা মেধাবিনি রাধিকে তব কথং প্রেমা গরীয়ানভূৎ ॥১৫৪॥
verses.transliteration: antaḥ-kleśa-kalaṅkitāḥ kila vayaṁ yāmo 'dya yāmyāṁ purīṁ\\nnāyaṁ vañcana-sañcaya-praṇayinaṁ hāsaṁ tathāpy ujjhati\\nasmin sampuṭite gabhīra-kapaṭair ābhīra-pallī-viṭe\\nhā medhāvini rādhike tava kathaṁ premā garīyān abhūt
verses.translation: 'Our hearts are so polluted by miserable conditions that we are certainly going to Pluto's kingdom. Nevertheless, Kṛṣṇa does not give up His beautiful loving smiling, which is full of cheating tricks. O Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, You are very intelligent. How could You have developed such great loving affection for this deceitful debauchee from the neighborhood of the cowherds?'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse (
Vidagdha-mādhava
2.37) is spoken to Rādhārāṇī by Lalitā-sakhī, another confidential friend.

verses.devanagari: হিত্বা দূরে পথি ধবতরোরন্তিকং ধর্মসেতো-\\nর্ভঙ্গোদগ্রা গুরুশিখরিণং রংহসা লঙ্ঘয়ন্তী ।\\nলেভে কৃষ্ণার্ণব নবরসা রাধিকা-বাহিনী ত্বাং\\nবাগ্বীচীভিঃ কিমিব বিমুখীভাবমস্যাস্তনোষি ॥১৫৫॥
verses.transliteration: hitvā dūre pathi dhava-taror antikaṁ dharā-setor\\nbhaṅgodagrā guru-śikhariṇaṁ raṁhasā laṅghayantī\\nlebhe kṛṣṇārṇava nava-rasā rādhikā-vāhinī tvāṁ\\nvāg-vīcibhiḥ kim iva vimukhī-bhāvam asyās tanoṣi
verses.translation: 'O Lord Kṛṣṇa, You are just like an ocean. The river of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī has reached You from a long distance-leaving far behind the tree of Her husband, breaking through the bridge of social convention, and forcibly crossing the hills of elder relatives. Coming here because of fresh feelings of love for You, that river has now received Your shelter, but now You are trying to turn Her back by the waves of unfavorable words. How is it that You are spreading this attitude?' "
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse from
Vidagdha-mādhava
(3.9) is spoken to Lord Kṛṣṇa by paurṇamāsī, the grandmother of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.

verses.devanagari: রায় কহে, — “বৃন্দাবন, মুরলী-নিঃস্বন ।\\nকৃষ্ণ, রাধিকার কৈছে করিয়াছে বর্ণন ? ॥ ১৫৬ ॥
verses.transliteration: rāya kahe,—"vṛndāvana, muralī-niḥsvana\\nkṛṣṇa, rādhikāra kaiche kariyācha varṇana
verses.translation: Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya further inquired: "How have you described Vṛndāvana, the vibration of the transcendental flute, and the relationship between Kṛṣṇa and Rādhikā?

verses.devanagari: কহ, তোমার কবিত্ব শুনি’ হয় চমৎকার ।”\\nক্রমে রূপ-গোসাঞি কহে করি’ নমস্কার ॥১৫৭॥
verses.transliteration: kaha, tomāra kavitva śuni' haya camatkāra"\\nkrame rūpa-gosāñi kahe kari' namaskāra
verses.translation: "Please tell me all this, for your poetic ability is wonderful." After offering obeisances to Rāmānanda Rāya, Rūpa Gosvāmī gradually began answering his inquiries.

verses.devanagari: সুগন্ধৌ মাকন্দপ্রকরমকরন্দস্য মধুরে\\nবিনিস্যন্দে বন্দীকৃতমধুপবৃন্দং মুহুরিদম্ ।\\nকৃতান্দোলং মন্দোন্নতিভিরনিলৈশ্চন্দনগিরে-\\nর্মমানন্দং বৃন্দা-বিপিনমতুলং তুন্দিলয়তি ॥১৫৮॥
verses.transliteration: sugandhau mākanda-prakara-makarandasya madhure\\nvinisyande vandī-kṛta-madhupa-vṛndaṁ muhur idam\\nkṛtāndolaṁ mandonnatibhir anilaiś candana-girer\\nmamānandaṁ vṛndā-vipinam atulaṁ tundilayati
verses.translation: 'The sweet, fragrant honey oozing from newly grown mango buds is again and again attracting groups of bumblebees, and this forest is trembling in the softly moving breezes from the Malaya Hills, which are full of sandalwood trees. Thus the forest of Vṛndāvana is increasing My transcendental pleasure.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse from
Vidagdha-mādhava
(1.23) is spoken by Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself.

verses.devanagari: বৃন্দাবনং দিব্যলতা-পরীতং\\nলতাশ্চ পুষ্পস্ফুরিতাগ্রভাজঃ ।\\nপুষ্পাণি চ স্ফীতমধুব্রতানি\\nমধুব্রতাশ্চ শ্রুতিহারিগীতাঃ ॥১৫৯॥
verses.transliteration: vṛndāvanaṁ divya-latā-parītaṁ\\nlatāś ca puṣpa-sphuritāgra-bhājaḥ\\npuṣpāṇi ca sphīta-madhu-vratāni\\nmadhu-vratāś ca śruti-hāri-gītāḥ
verses.translation: 'My dear friend, see how this forest of Vṛndāvana is full of transcendental creepers and trees. The tops of the creepers are full of flowers, and intoxicated bumblebees are buzzing around them, humming songs that please the ear and surpass even the Vedic hymns.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse from
Vidagdha-mādhava
(1.24) is spoken by Lord Balarāma to His friend Śrīdāmā.

verses.devanagari: ক্বচিদ্ভৃঙ্গীগীতং ক্বচিদনিলভঙ্গী-শিশিরতা\\nক্বচিদ্বল্লীলাস্যং ক্বচিদমলমল্লীপরিমলঃ ।\\nক্বচিদ্ধারাশালী করকফলপালী-রসভরো\\nহৃষীকাণাং বৃন্দং প্রমদয়তি বৃন্দাবনমিদম্ ॥১৬০॥
verses.transliteration: kvacid bhṛṅgī-gītaṁ kvacid anila-bhaṅgī-śiśiratā\\nkvacid vallī-lāsyaṁ kvacid amala-mallī-parimalaḥ\\nkvacid dhārā-śālī karaka-phala-pālī-rasa-bharo\\nhṛṣīkāṇāṁ vṛndaṁ pramadayati vṛndāvanam idam
verses.translation: 'My dear friend, this forest of Vṛndāvana is giving great pleasure to our senses in various ways. Somewhere bumblebees are singing in groups, and in some places mild breezes are cooling the entire atmosphere. Somewhere the creepers and tree twigs are dancing, the mallikā flowers are expanding their fragrance, and an overabundance of juice is constantly flowing in showers from pomegranate fruits.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse from
Vidagdha-mādhava
(1.31) is spoken by Lord Kṛṣṇa to His cowherd friend Madhumaṅgala.

verses.devanagari: পরামৃষ্টাঙ্গুষ্ঠত্রয়মসিতরত্নৈরুভয়তো\\nবহন্তী সংকীর্ণৌ মণিভিররুণৈস্তৎপরিসরৌ ।\\nতয়োর্মধ্যে হীরোজ্জ্বলবিমল-জাম্বূনদময়ী\\nকরে কল্যাণীয়ং বিহরতি হরেঃ কেলিমুরলী ॥১৬১॥
verses.transliteration: parāmṛṣṭāṅguṣṭha-trayam asita-ratnair ubhayato\\nvahantī saṅkīrṇau maṇibhir aruṇais tat-parisarau\\ntayor madhye hīrojjvala-vimala-jāmbūnada-mayī\\nkare kalyāṇīyaṁ viharati hareḥ keli-muralī
verses.translation: The flute of Kṛṣṇa's pastimes measures three fingers in length, and it is bedecked with indra-nīla gems. At the ends of the flute are aruṇa gems [rubies], glittering beautifully, and in between the flute is plated with gold, set ablaze by diamonds. This auspicious flute, pleasing to Kṛṣṇa, is glittering in His hand with transcendental brilliance.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse from
Vidagdha-mādhava
(3.1) is spoken to Lalitādevī by Paurṇamāsī, the grandmother of Rādhārāṇī.

verses.devanagari: সদ্বংশতস্তব জনিঃ পুরুষোত্তমস্য\\nপাণৌ স্থিতির্মুরলিকে সরলাসি জাত্যা ।\\nকস্মাত্ত্বয়া সখি গুরোর্বিষমা গৃহীতা\\nগোপাঙ্গনাগণবিমোহনমন্ত্রদীক্ষা ॥১৬২॥
verses.transliteration: sad-vaṁśatas tava janiḥ puruṣottamasya\\npāṇau sthitir muralike saralāsi jātyā\\nkasmāt tvayā sakhi guror viṣamā gṛhītā\\ngopāṅganā-gaṇa-vimohana-man tra-dīkṣā
verses.translation: My dear friend the flute, it appears that you have been born of a very good family, for your residence is in the hands of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. By birth you are simple and are not at all crooked. Why then have you taken initiation into this dangerous mantra that enchants the assembled gopīs?'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse (
Vidagdha-mādhava
5.17) is spoken by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.

verses.devanagari: সখি মুরলি বিশালচ্ছিদ্রজালেন পূর্ণা\\nলঘুরতিকঠিনা ত্বং গ্রন্থিলা নীরসাসি ।\\nতদপি ভজসি শশ্বচ্চুম্বনানন্দসান্দ্রং\\nহরিকরপরিরম্ভং কেন পুণ্যোদয়েন ॥১৬৩॥
verses.transliteration: sakhi murali viśāla-cchidra-jalena pūrṇā\\nlaghur atikaṭhinā tvaṁ granthilā nīrasāsi\\ntad api bhajasi śvaśvac cumbanānanda-sāndraṁ\\nhari-kara-parirambhaṁ kena puṇyodayena
verses.translation: My dear friend the flute, you are actually full of many holes or faults. You are light, hard, juiceless and full of knots. But what kind of pious activities have engaged you in the service of being kissed by the Lord and embraced by His hands?'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse (
Vidagdha-mādhava
4.7) is spoken by Candrāvalī-sakhī, the
gopī
competitor of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.

verses.devanagari: রুন্ধন্নম্বুভৃতশ্চমৎকৃতিপরং কুর্বন্মুহুস্তুম্বুরুং\\nধ্যানাদন্তরয়ন্ সনন্দনমুখান্ বিস্মাপয়ন্ বেধসম্ ।\\nঔৎসুক্যাবলিভির্বলিং চটুলয়ন্ ভোগীন্দ্রমাঘূর্ণয়ন্\\nভিন্দন্নণ্ডকটাহভিত্তিমভিতো বভ্রাম বংশীধ্বনিঃ ॥১৬৪॥
verses.transliteration: rundhann ambu-bhṛtaś camatkṛti-paraṁ kurvan muhus tumburuṁ\\ndhyānād antarayan sanandana-mukhān vismāpayan vedhasam\\nautsukyāvalibhir baliṁ caṭulayan bhogīndram āghūrṇayan\\nbhindann aṇḍa-kaṭāha-bhittim abhito babhrāma vaṁśī-dhvaniḥ
verses.translation: 'The transcendental vibration of Kṛṣṇa's flute blocked the movements of the rain clouds, struck the Gandharvas full of wonder, and agitated the meditation of great saintly persons like Sanaka and Sanandana. It created wonder in Lord Brahmā, wrought intense curiosity that agitated the mind of Bali Mahārāja, who was otherwise firmly fixed, made Mahārāja Ananta, the carrier of the planets, whirl around, and penetrated the strong coverings of the universe. Thus the sound of the flute in the hands of Kṛṣṇa created a wonderful situation.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse (
Vidagdha-mādhava
1.27) is spoken by Madhumaṅgala, a cowherd friend of Kṛṣṇa's.

verses.devanagari: অয়ং নয়নদণ্ডিতপ্রবরপুণ্ডরীকপ্রভঃ\\nপ্রভাতি নবজাগুড়-দ্যুতিবিড়ম্বি-পীতাম্বরঃ ।\\nঅরণ্যজপরিষ্ক্রিয়া-দমিতদিব্যবেশাদরো\\nহরিন্মণিমনোহরদ্যুতিভিরুজ্জ্বলাঙ্গো হরিঃ ॥১৬৫॥
verses.transliteration: ayaṁ nayana-daṇḍita-pra vara-puṇḍarīka-prabhaḥ\\nprabhāti nava-jāguḍa-dyuti-viḍambi-pītāmbaraḥ\\naraṇyaja-pariṣkriyā-damita-divya-veśādaro\\nharin-maṇi-manohara-dyutibhir ujjvalāṅgo hariḥ
verses.translation: 'The beauty of Kṛṣṇa's eyes surpasses the beauty of white lotus flowers, His yellow garments surpass the brilliance of fresh decorations of kuṅkuma, His ornaments of selected forest flowers surpass the hankering for the best of garments, and His bodily beauty possesses mind-attracting splendor greater than the jewels known as marakata-maṇi [emeralds].'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse from
Vidagdha-mādhava
(1.17) is spoken by paurṇamāsī.

verses.devanagari: জঙ্ঘাধস্তটসঙ্গিদক্ষিণপদং কিঞ্চিদ্বিভুগ্নত্রিকং\\nসাচিস্তম্ভিতকন্ধরং সখি তিরঃসঞ্চারিনেত্রাঞ্চলম্ ।\\nবংশীং কুট্মলিতে দধানমধরে লোলাঙ্গুলীসঙ্গতাং\\nরিঙ্গদ্ভ্রূভ্রমরং বরাঙ্গি পরমানন্দং পুরঃ স্বীকুরু ॥১৬৬॥
verses.transliteration: jaṅghādhas-taṭa-saṅgi-dakṣiṇa-padaṁ kiñcid vibhugna-trikam-\\nsāci-stambhita-kandharaṁ sakhi tiraḥ-sañcāri-netrāñcalam\\nvaṁśīṁ kuṭmalite dadhānam adhare lolāṅgulī-saṅgatāṁ\\nriṅgad-bhrū-bhramaraṁ varāṅgi paramānandaṁ puraḥ svīkuru
verses.translation: 'O most beautiful friend, please accept the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is standing before you full of transcendental bliss. The borders of His eyes roam from side to side, and His eyebrows move slowly like bumblebees on His lotuslike face. Standing with His right foot placed below the knee of His left leg, the middle of His body curved in three places, and His neck gracefully tilted to the side, He takes His flute to His pursed lips and moves His fingers upon it here and there.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse is from the
Lalita-mādhava-nāṭaka
(4.27), a ten-act play by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. The speaker here is Lalitādevī.

verses.devanagari: কুলবরতনুধর্মগ্রাববৃন্দানি ভিন্দন্\\nসুমুখি নিশিতদীর্ঘাপাঙ্গটঙ্কচ্ছটাভিঃ ।\\nযুগপদয়মপূর্বঃ কঃ পুরো বিশ্বকর্মা\\nমরকতমণিলক্ষৈর্গোষ্ঠকক্ষাং চিনোতি ॥১৬৭॥
verses.transliteration: kula-varatanu-dharma-grāva-vṛndāni bhindan\\nsumukhi niśita-dīrghāpāṅga-ṭaṅka-cchaṭābhiḥ\\nyugapad ayam apūrvaḥ kaḥ puro viśva-karmā\\nmarakata-maṇi-lakṣair goṣṭha-kakṣāṁ cinoti
verses.translation: 'O beautiful-faced one, who is this creative person standing before us? With the sharp chisels of His loving glances, He is splitting the hard stones of many women's devotion to their husbands. And with the luster of His body, surpassing the brilliance of countless emeralds, He is simultaneously constructing private meeting places for His pastimes.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse (
Lalita-mādhava
1.52) is spoken by Rādhārāṇī to Lalitādevī.

verses.devanagari: মহেন্দ্রমণিমণ্ডলীমদবিড়ম্বিদেহদ্যুতি-\\nর্ব্রজেন্দ্রকুলচন্দ্রমাঃ স্ফুরতি কোঽপি নব্যো যুবা ।\\nসখি স্থিরকুলাঙ্গনা-নিকর-নীবি-বন্ধার্গল-\\nচ্ছিদাকরণ-কৌতুকী জয়তি যস্য বংশীধ্বনিঃ ॥১৬৮॥
verses.transliteration: mahendra-maṇi-maṇḍalī-mada-viḍambi-deha-dyutir\\nvrajendra-kula-candramāḥ sphurati ko 'pi navyo yuvā\\nsakhi sthira-kulāṅganā-nikara-nīvi-bandhārgala-\\ncchidākaraṇa-kautukī jayati yasya vaṁśī-dhvaniḥ
verses.translation: My dear friend, this newly youthful Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the moon in the family of Nanda Mahārāja, is so beautiful that He defies the beauty of clusters of valuable jewels. All glories to the vibration of His flute, for it is cunningly breaking the patience of chaste ladies by loosening their belts and tight dresses.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse from
Lalita-mādhava
(1.49) is spoken by Lalitādevī to Rādhārāṇī.

verses.devanagari: বলাদক্ষ্ণোর্লক্ষ্মীঃ কবলয়তি নব্যং কুবলয়ং\\nমুখোল্লাসঃ ফুল্লং কমলবনমুল্লঙ্ঘয়তি চ ।\\nদশাং কষ্টামষ্টাপদমপি নয়ত্যাঙ্গিকরুচি-\\nর্বিচিত্রং রাধায়াঃ কিমপি কিল রূপং বিলসতি ॥১৬৯॥
verses.transliteration: balād akṣṇor lakṣmīḥ kavalayati navyaṁ kuvalayaṁ\\nmukhollāsaḥ phullaṁ kamala-vanam ullaṅghayati ca\\ndaśāṁ kaṣṭām aṣṭā-padam api nayaty āṅgika-rucir\\nvicitraṁ rādhāyāḥ kim api kila rūpaṁ vilasati
verses.translation: The beauty of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's eyes forcibly devours the beauty of newly grown blue lotus flowers, and the beauty of Her face surpasses that of an entire forest of fully blossomed lotuses. Her bodily luster seems to place even gold in a painful situation. Thus the wonderful, unprecedented beauty of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is awakening in Vṛndāvana.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse is from
Vidagdha-mādhava
(1.32). It is spoken by Paurṇamāsī.

verses.devanagari: বিধুরেতি দিবা বিরূপতাং\\nশতপত্রং বত শর্বরীমুখে ।\\nইতি কেন সদাশ্রিয়োজ্জ্বলং\\nতুলনামর্হতি মৎপ্রিয়াননম্ ॥১৭০॥
verses.transliteration: vidhur eti divā virūpatāṁ\\nśata-patraṁ bata śarvarī-mukhe\\niti kena sadā śriyojjvalaṁ\\ntulanām arhati mat-priyānanam
verses.translation: Although the effulgence of the moon is brilliant initially at night, in the daytime it fades away. Similarly, although the lotus is beautiful during the daytime, at night it closes. But, O My friend, the face of My most dear Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is always bright and beautiful, both day and night. Therefore, to what can Her face be compared?'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse (
Vidagdha-mādhava
5.20) is spoken by Śrī Kṛṣṇa to Madhumaṅgala.

verses.devanagari: প্রমদরসতরঙ্গস্মেরগণ্ডস্থলায়াঃ\\nস্মরধনুরনুবন্ধিভ্রূলতা-লাস্যভাজঃ ।\\nমদকলচলভৃঙ্গীভ্রান্তিভঙ্গীং দধানো\\nহৃদয়মিদমদাঙক্ষীৎ পক্ষ্মলাক্ষ্যাঃ কটাক্ষঃ ॥১৭১॥
verses.transliteration: pramada-rasa-taraṅga-smera-gaṇḍa-sthalāyāḥ\\nsmara-dhanur anubandhi-bhrū-latā-lāsya-bhājaḥ\\nmada-kala-cala-bhṛṅgī-bhrānti-bhaṅgīṁ dadhāno\\nhṛdayam idam adāṅkṣīt pakṣmalākṣyāḥ kaṭākṣaḥ
verses.translation: When Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī smiles, waves of joy overtake Her cheeks, and Her arched eyebrows dance like the bow of Cupid. Her glance is so enchanting that it is like a dancing bumblebee, moving unsteadily due to intoxication. That bee has bitten the whorl of My heart.' "
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse from
Vidagdha-mādhava
(2.51) is also spoken by Lord Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: রায় কহে, — “তোমার কবিত্ব অমৃতের ধার ।\\nদ্বিতীয় নাটকের কহ নান্দী-ব্যবহার ।।” ॥ ১৭২ ॥
verses.transliteration: rāya kahe,—"tomāra kavitva amṛtera dhāra\\ndvitīya nāṭakera kaha nāndī-vyavahāra"
verses.translation: Having heard these verses recited by Rūpa Gosvāmī, Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya said, "Your poetic expressions are like continuous showers of nectar. Kindly let me hear the introductory portion of the second drama."

verses.devanagari: রূপ কহে, — “কাহাঁ তুমি সূর্যোপম ভাস  ।\\nমুঞি কোন্ ক্ষুদ্র, — যেন খদ্যোত-প্রকাশ ॥১৭৩॥
verses.transliteration: rūpa kahe,—"kāhāṅ tumi sūryopama bhāsa\\nmuñi kon kṣudra,—yena khadyota-prakāśa
verses.translation: Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī said, "In your presence, which is just like brilliant sunshine, I am as insignificant as the light of a glowworm.

verses.devanagari: তোমার আগে ধার্ষ্ট্য এই মুখ-ব্যাদান ।” এত বলি’ নান্দী-শ্লোক করিলা ব্যাখ্যান ॥১৭৪॥
verses.transliteration: tomāra āge dhārṣṭya ei mukha-vyādāna"\\neta bali' nāndī-śloka karilā vyākhyāna
verses.translation: It is even impudent for me to open my mouth before you." Then, having said this, he recited the introductory verse of Lalita-mādhava.

verses.devanagari: সুররিপুসুদৃশামুরোজকোকা-\\nন্মুখকমলানি চ খেদয়ন্নখণ্ডঃ ।\\nচিরমখিলসুহৃচ্চকোরনন্দী\\nদিশতু মুকুন্দযশঃশশী মুদং বঃ ॥১৭৫॥
verses.transliteration: sura-ripu-sudṛśām uroja-kokān\\nmukha-kamalāni ca khedayann akhaṇḍaḥ\\nciram akhila-suhṛc-cakora-nandī\\ndiśatu mukunda-yaśaḥ-śaśī mudaṁ vaḥ
verses.translation: The beautiful moonlike glories of Mukunda give distress to the lotuslike faces of the wives of the demons and to their raised breasts, which are like gleaming cakravāka birds. Those glories, however, are pleasing to all His devotees, who are like cakora birds. May those glories forever give pleasure to you all.' "
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThis is the first verse of Act One of\nLalita-mādhava.

verses.devanagari: ‘দ্বিতীয় নান্দী কহ দেখি?’ — রায় পুছিলা ।\\nসঙ্কোচ পাঞা রূপ পড়িতে লাগিলা ॥১৭৬॥
verses.transliteration: 'dvitīya nāndī kaha dekhi?'—rāya puchilā\\nsaṅkoca pāñā rūpa paḍite lāgilā
verses.translation: When Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya further inquired about the second introductory verse, Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī was somewhat hesitant, but nevertheless he began to read.

verses.devanagari: নিজপ্রণয়িতাং সুধামুদয়মাপ্নুবন্ যঃ ক্ষিতৌ\\nকিরত্যলমুরীকৃতদ্বিজকুলাধিরাজস্থিতিঃ ।\\nস লুঞ্চিত-তমস্ততির্মম শচীসুতাখ্যঃ শশী\\nবশীকৃতজগন্মনাঃ কিমপি শর্ম বিন্যস্যতু ॥১৭৭॥
verses.transliteration: nija-praṇayitāṁ sudhām udayam āpnuvan yaḥ kṣitau\\nkiraty alam urīkṛta-dvija-kulādhirāja-sthitiḥ\\nsa luñcita-tamas-tatir mama śacī-sutākhyaḥ śaśī\\nvaśīkṛta-jagan-manāḥ kim api śarma vinyasyatu
verses.translation: The moonlike Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is known as the son of mother Śacī, has now appeared on earth to spread devotional love of Himself. He is emperor of the brāhmaṇa community. He can drive away all the darkness of ignorance and control the mind of everyone in the world. May that rising moon bestow upon us all good fortune.' "
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThis is the third verse of Act One of\nVidagdha-mādhava.

verses.devanagari: শুনিয়া প্রভুর যদি অন্তরে উল্লাস  ।\\nবাহিরে কহেন কিছু করি’ রোষাভাস ॥১৭৮॥
verses.transliteration: śuniyā prabhura yadi antare ullāsa\\nbāhire kahena kichu kari' roṣābhāsa
verses.translation: Although Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was inwardly greatly pleased when He heard this verse, externally He spoke as if angry.

verses.devanagari: “কাঁহা তোমার কৃষ্ণরসকাব্য-সুধাসিন্ধু  ।\\nতার মধ্যে মিথ্যা কেনে স্তুতি-ক্ষারবিন্দু” ॥১৭৯॥
verses.transliteration: kāṅhā tomāra kṛṣṇa-rasa-kāvya-sudhā-sindhu\\ntāra madhye mithyā kene stuti-kṣāra-bindu
verses.translation: Your exalted poetic descriptions of the mellows of Lord Kṛṣṇa's pastimes are like an ocean of nectar. But why have you put in a false prayer about Me? It is like a drop of detestful alkali."

verses.devanagari: রায় কহে, — “রূপের কাব্য অমৃতের পূর ।\\nতার মধ্যে এক বিন্দু দিয়াছে কর্পূর ।।” ॥ ১৮০ ॥
verses.transliteration: rāya kahe,—"rūpera kāvya amṛtera pūra\\ntāra madhye eka bindu diyāche karpūra"
verses.translation: Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya objected, "It is not alkali at all. It is a particle of camphor he has put into the nectar of his exalted poetic expression."

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহে, — “রায়, তোমার ইহাতে উল্লাস ।\\nশুনিতেই লজ্জা, লোকে করে উপহাস ।।” ॥ ১৮১ ॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahe,—"rāya, tomāra ihāte ullāsa\\nśunitei lajjā, loke kare upahāsa"
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "My dear Rāmānanda Rāya, you are jubilant at hearing these poetic expressions, but I am ashamed to hear them, for people in general will joke about the subject of this verse."

verses.devanagari: রায় কহে, — “লোকের সুখ ইহার শ্রবণে ।\\nঅভীষ্ট-দেবের স্মৃতি মঙ্গলাচরণে ।।” ॥ ১৮২ ॥
verses.transliteration: rāya kahe,—"lokera sukha ihāra śravaṇe\\nabhīṣṭa-devera smṛti maṅgalācaraṇe"
verses.translation: Rāmānanda Rāya said, "Instead of joking, people in general will feel great pleasure in hearing such poetry, for the initial remembrance of the worshipable Deity invokes good fortune."

verses.devanagari: রায় কহে, — “কোন্ অঙ্গে পাত্রের প্রবেশ ?”\\nতবে রূপ-গোসাঞি কহে তাহার বিশেষ ॥১৮৩॥
verses.transliteration: rāya kahe,—"kon aṅge pātrera praveśa?"\\ntabe rūpa-gosāñi kahe tāhāra viśeṣa
verses.translation: Rāmānanda Rāya inquired, "By which subdivision of style do the players enter?" Rūpa Gosvāmī then began to speak specifically about this subject.

verses.devanagari: নটতা কিরাতরাজং নিহত্য রঙ্গস্থলে কলানিধিনা ।\\nসময়ে তেন বিধেয়ং গুণবতি তারাকরগ্রহণম্ ॥১৮৪॥
verses.transliteration: naṭatā kirāta-rājaṁ\\nnihatya raṅga-sthale kalā-nidhinā\\nsamaye tena vidheyaṁ\\nguṇavati tārā-kara-grahaṇam
verses.translation: “ 'While dancing on the stage after having killed the ruler of uncivilized men [Kaṁsa], Lord Kṛṣṇa, master of all arts, will at the proper time accept the hand of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, who is qualified with all transcendental attributes.'  (Lalita-mādhava 1.11)

verses.devanagari: ‘উদ্ঘাত্যক’ নাম এই ‘আমুখ’ — ‘বীথী’ অঙ্গ ।\\nতোমার আগে কহি — ইহা ধার্ষ্ট্যের তরঙ্গ\\nউদ্ঘাত্যকঃ কথোদ্ঘাতঃ প্রয়োগাতিশয়স্তথা ।\\nপ্রবর্তকাবলগিতে পঞ্চ প্রস্তাবনা-ভিদাঃ ।। ॥১৮৫॥
verses.transliteration: 'udghātyaka' nāma ei 'āmukha'—'vīthī' aṅga\\ntomāra āge kahi—ihā dhārṣṭyera taraṅga
verses.translation: "This introduction is technically called udghātyaka, and the whole scene is called vīthī. You are so expert in dramatic expression that each of my statements before you is like a wave from an ocean of impudence.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
In this connection Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura again quotes the following verse from the
Sāhitya-darpaṇa
(6.288):
udghātyakaḥ kathodghātaḥ
prayogātiśayas tathā
pravartakāvalagite
pañca prastāvanā-bhidāḥ
Thus the technical names for the five kinds of introductory scenes of the drama are listed as
udghātyaka, kathodghāta, prayogātiśaya, pravartaka
and
avalagita.
When Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya inquired which of these five Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī had used to accomplish the technical introduction to his drama
Lalita-mādhava,
Rūpa Gosvāmī replied that he had used the introduction technically called
udghātyaka.
According to
Bhāratī-vṛtti,
three technical terms used are
prarocanā, vīthī
and
prahasanā.
Thus Rūpa Gosvāmī also mentioned
vīthī,
which is a technical term for a certain type of expression. According to the
Sāhitya-darpaṇa
(6.520):
vīthyām eko bhaved aṅkaḥ
kaścid eko 'tra kalpyate
ākāśa-bhāṣitair uktaiś
citrāṁ pratyuktim āśritaḥ
The
vīthī
beginning of a drama consists of only one scene. In that scene, one of the heroes enters the stage, and by means of opposing statements uttered by a voice from the sky (offstage), he introduces the abundant conjugal mellow and other mellows to some degree. In the course of the introduction, all the seeds of the play are planted. This introduction is called
udghātyaka
because the player dances on the stage. This term also indicates that the full moon enters the stage. In this case, when the word
naṭatā
("dancing on the stage") is linked with the moon, its meaning is obscure, but because the meaning becomes very clear when the word
naṭatā
is linked with Kṛṣṇa, this type of introduction is called
udghātyaka.
Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya used highly technical terms when he discussed this with Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. Rūpa Gosvāmī admitted that Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya was a greatly learned scholar of bona fide dramatic composition. Thus although Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī was quite fit to answer Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya's questions, due to his Vaiṣṇava humility he admitted that his words were impudent. Actually both Rūpa Gosvāmī and Rāmānanda Rāya were scholarly experts in composing poetry and presenting it strictly according to the
Sāhitya-darpaṇa
and other Vedic literatures.

verses.devanagari: “পদানি ত্বগতার্থানি তদর্থগতয়ে নরাঃ ।\\nযোজয়ন্তি পদৈরন্যৈঃ স উদঘাত্যক উচ্যতে ।।” ॥ ১৮৬ ॥
verses.transliteration: padāni tv agatārthāni\\ntad-artha-gataye narāḥ\\nyojayanti padair anyaiḥ\\nsa udghātyaka ucyate
verses.translation: To explain an unclear word, men generally join it with other words. Such an attempt is called udghātyaka.' "
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse is quoted from the
Sāhitya-darpaṇa
(6.289).

verses.devanagari: রায় কহে, — “কহ আগে অঙ্গের বিশেষ” ।\\nশ্রীরূপ কহেন কিছু সংক্ষেপ-উদ্দেশ ॥১৮৭॥
verses.transliteration: rāya kahe,—"kaha āge aṅgera viśeṣa"\\nśrī-rūpa kahena kichu saṅkṣepa-uddeśa
verses.translation: When Rāmānanda Rāya requested Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī to speak further about various portions of the play, Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī briefly quoted his Lalita-mādhava.

verses.devanagari: হরিমুদ্দিশতে রজোভরঃ, পুরতঃ সঙ্গময়ত্যমুং তমঃ ।\\nব্রজবামদৃশাং ন পদ্ধতিঃ, প্রকটা সর্বদৃশঃ শ্রুতেরপি ॥১৮৮॥
verses.transliteration: harim uddiśate rajo-bharaḥ\\npurataḥ saṅgamayaty amuṁ tamaḥ\\nvrajavāma-dṛśāṁ na paddhatiḥ\\nprakaṭā sarva-dṛśaḥ śruter api
verses.translation: The dust from cows and calves on the road creates a kind of darkness indicating that Kṛṣṇa is returning home from the pasture. Also, the darkness of evening provokes the gopīs to meet Kṛṣṇa. Thus the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs are covered by a kind of transcendental darkness and are therefore impossible for ordinary scholars of the Vedas to see.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse from the
Lalita-mādhava
(1.23) is spoken by Paurṇamāsī in a conversation with Gārgī.
Kṛṣṇa stated in
Bhagavad-gītā, traiguṇya-viṣayā vedā nistraiguṇyo bhavārjuna.
Thus He advised Arjuna to rise above the modes of material nature, for the entire Vedic system is filled with descriptions involving
sattva-guṇa, rajo-guṇa
and
tamo-guṇa.
People are generally covered by the quality of
rajo-guṇa
and are therefore unable to understand the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa with the
gopīs
of Vraja. Moreover, the quality of
tamo-guṇa
further disturbs their understanding. In Vṛndāvana, however, although Kṛṣṇa is covered by the hazy darkness of the dust, the
gopīs
can nevertheless understand that within the dust storm is Kṛṣṇa. Because they are His topmost devotees, they can perceive His hand in everything. Thus even in the dark or in a hazy storm of dust, devotees can understand what Kṛṣṇa is doing. The purport of this verse is that Kṛṣṇa is never lost, under any circumstances, to the vision of exalted devotees like the
gopīs.

verses.devanagari: হ্রিয়মবগৃহ্য গৃহেভ্যঃ কর্ষতি রাধাং বনায় যা নিপুণা ।\\nসা জয়তি নিসৃষ্টার্থা বরবংশজকাকলী দূতী ॥১৮৯॥
verses.transliteration: hriyam avagṛhya gṛhebhyaḥ karṣati\\nrādhāṁ vanāya yā nipuṇā\\nsā jayati nisṛṣṭārthā\\nvara-vaṁśaja-kākalī dūtī
verses.translation: May the sweet sound of Lord Kṛṣṇa's flute, His authorized messenger, be glorified, for it expertly releases Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī from Her shyness and attracts Her from Her home to the forest.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse from
Lalita-mādhava
(1.24) is spoken by Gārgī, the daughter of Gargamuni.

verses.devanagari: সহচরি নিরাতঙ্কঃ কোঽয়ং যুবা মুদিরদ্যুতি-\\nর্ব্রজভুবি কুতঃ প্রাপ্তো মাদ্যন্মতঙ্গজবিভ্রমঃ ।\\nঅহহ চটুলৈরুৎসর্পদ্ভির্দৃগঞ্চলতস্করৈ-\\nর্মম ধৃতিধনং চেতঃকোষাদ্বিলুণ্ঠয়তীহ যঃ ॥১৯০॥
verses.transliteration: sahacari nirātaṅkaḥ ko 'yaṁ yuvā mudira-dyutir\\nvraja-bhuvi kutaḥ prāpto mādyan mataṅgaja-vibhramaḥ\\nahaha caṭulair utsarpadbhir dṛg-añcala-taskarair\\nmama dhṛti-dhanaṁ cetaḥ-koṣād viluṇṭhayatīha yaḥ
verses.translation: My dear friend, who is this fearless young man? He is as bright as a lightning cloud, and He wanders in His pastimes like a maddened elephant. From where has He come to Vṛndāvana? Alas, by His restless movements and attractive glances He is plundering from the vault of My heart the treasure of My patience.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse (
Lalita-mādhava
2.11) is spoken by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī to Her friend Lalitādevī.

verses.devanagari: বিহারসুরদীর্ঘিকা মম মনঃকরীন্দ্রস্য যা\\nবিলোচন-চকোরয়োঃ শরদমন্দচন্দ্রপ্রভা ।\\nউরোঽম্বরতটস্য চাভরণচারুতারাবলী\\nময়োন্নতমনোরথৈরিয়মলম্ভি সা রাধিকা ।।” ॥ ১৯১ ॥
verses.transliteration: vihāra-sura-dīrghikā mama manaḥ-karīndrasya yā\\nvilocana-cakorayoḥ śarad-amanda-candra-prabhā\\nuro 'mbara-taṭasya cābharaṇa-cāru-tārāvalī\\nmayonnata-manorathair iyam alambhi sā rādhikā
verses.translation: Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is the Ganges in which the elephant of My mind enjoys pastimes. She is the shining of the full autumn moon for the cakora birds of My eyes. She is the dazzling ornament, the bright and beautiful arrangement of stars, on the border of the sky of My chest. Now today I have gained Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī because of the highly elevated state of My mind.' "
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse from
Lalita-mādhava
(2.10) expresses the thoughts of Lord Kṛṣṇa in relation with Rādhārāṇī.

verses.devanagari: এত শুনি’ রায় কহে প্রভুর চরণে  ।\\nরূপের কবিত্ব প্রশংসি’ সহস্র-বদনে ॥১৯২॥
verses.transliteration: eta śuni' rāya kahe prabhura caraṇe\\nrūpera kavitva praśaṁsi' sahasra-vadane
verses.translation: After hearing this, Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya submitted at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu the superexcellence of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī's poetic expression and began to praise it as if he had thousands of mouths.

verses.devanagari: “কবিত্ব না হয় এই অমৃতের ধার  ।\\nনাটক লক্ষণ সব সিদ্ধান্তের সার ॥১৯৩॥
verses.transliteration: "kavitva nā haya ei amṛtera dhāra\\nnāṭaka-lakṣaṇa saba siddhāntera sāra
verses.translation: Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya said, "This is not a poetic presentation; it is a continuous shower of nectar. Indeed, it is the essence of all ultimate realizations, appearing in the form of plays.

verses.devanagari: প্রেম-পরিপাটী এই অদ্ভুত বর্ণন ।\\nশুনি’ চিত্ত-কর্ণের হয় আনন্দ-ঘূর্ণন ॥১৯৪॥
verses.transliteration: prema-paripāṭī ei adbhuta varṇana\\nśuni' citta-karṇera haya ānanda-ghūrṇana
verses.translation: The wonderful descriptions of Rūpa Gosvāmī are superb arrangements to express loving affairs. Hearing them will plunge the heart and ears of everyone into a whirlpool of transcendental bliss.

verses.devanagari: “কিং কাব্যেন কবেস্তস্য কিং কাণ্ডেন ধনুষ্মতঃ ।\\nপরস্য হৃদয়ে লগ্নং ন ঘূর্ণয়তি যচ্ছিরঃ ।।” ॥ ১৯৫ ॥
verses.transliteration: kiṁ kāvyena kaves tasya\\nkiṁ kāṇḍena dhanuṣ-mataḥ\\nparasya hṛdaye lagnaṁ\\nna ghūrṇayati yac chiraḥ
verses.translation: What is the use of a bowman's arrow or a poet's poetry if they penetrate the heart but do not cause the head to spin?'

verses.devanagari: তোমার শক্তি বিনা জীবের নহে এই বাণী ।\\nতুমি শক্তি দিয়া কহাও, — হেন অনুমানি ।।” ॥ ১৯৬ ॥
verses.transliteration: tomāra śakti vinā jīvera nahe ei vāṇī\\ntumi śakti diyā kahāo,—hena anumāni"
verses.translation: Without Your mercy such poetic expressions would be impossible for an ordinary living being to write. My guess is that You have given him the power."

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহে, — “প্রয়াগে ইহার হইল মিলন ।\\nইহার গুণে ইহাতে আমার তুষ্ট হৈল মন ॥১৯৭॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahe,—"prayāge ihāra ha-ila milana\\nihāra guṇe ihāte āmāra tuṣṭa haila mana
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "I met Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī at Prayāga. He attracted and satisfied Me because of his qualities."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The Supreme personality of Godhead is not partial to some and neutral to others. One can actually draw the attention of the Supreme Personality of Godhead by service. Then one is further empowered by the Lord to act in such a way that everyone can appreciate his service. This is confirmed in
Bhagavad-gītā
(Bg. 4.11)/
ye yathā māṁ prapadyante tāṁs tathaiva bhajāmy aham.
Kṛṣṇa is responsive. If one tries to render his best service to the Lord, the Lord gives him the power to do so. Kṛṣṇa also says in the
Bhagavad-gītā
(Bg. 10.10):
teṣāṁ satata-yuktānāṁ
bhajatāṁ prīti-pūrvakam
dadāmi buddhi-yogaṁ taṁ
yena mām upayānti te
"To those who are constantly devoted and worship Me with love, I give the understanding by which they can come to Me." Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bestowed His special favor upon Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī because Rūpa Gosvāmī wanted to serve the Lord to the best of his ability. Such is the reciprocation between the devotee and the Lord in the discharge of devotional duties.

verses.devanagari: মধুর প্রসন্ন ইহার কাব্য সালঙ্কার  ।\\nঐছে কবিত্ব বিনু নহে রসের প্রচার ॥১৯৮॥
verses.transliteration: madhura prasanna ihāra kāvya sālaṅkāra\\naiche kavitva vinu nahe rasera pracāra
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu praised the metaphors and other literary ornaments of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī's transcendental poetry. Without such poetic attributes, He said, there is no possibility of preaching transcendental mellows.

verses.devanagari: সবে কৃপা করি’ ইঁহারে দেহ’ এই বর  ।\\nব্রজলীলা-প্রেমরস যেন বর্ণে নিরন্তর ॥১৯৯॥
verses.transliteration: sabe kṛpā kari' iṅhāre deha' ei vara\\nvraja-līlā-prema-rasa yena varṇe nirantara
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu requested all His personal associates to bless Rūpa Gosvāmī so that he might continuously describe the pastimes of Vṛndāvana, which are full of emotional love of Godhead.

verses.devanagari: ইঁহার যে জ্যেষ্ঠভ্রাতা, নাম — ‘সনাতন’ ।\\nপৃথিবীতে বিজ্ঞবর নাহি তাঁর সম ॥২০০॥
verses.transliteration: iṅhāra ye jyeṣṭha-bhrātā, nāma—'sanātana'\\npṛthivīte vijña-vara nāhi tāṅra sama
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī's elder brother, whose name is Sanātana Gosvāmī, is such a wise and learned scholar that no one is equal to him."

verses.devanagari: তোমার যৈছে বিষয়ত্যাগ, তৈছে তাঁর রীতি ।\\nদৈন্য-বৈরাগ্য-পাণ্ডিত্যের তাঁহাতেই স্থিতি ॥২০১॥
verses.transliteration: tomāra yaiche viṣaya-tyāga, taiche tāṅra rīti\\ndainya-vairāgya-pāṇḍityera tāṅhātei sthiti
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu told Rāmānanda Rāya, "Sanātana Gosvāmī's renunciation of material connections is just like yours. Humility, renunciation and excellent learning exist in him simultaneously.

verses.devanagari: এই দুই ভাইয়ে আমি পাঠাইলুঁ বৃন্দাবনে ।\\nশক্তি দিয়া ভক্তিশাস্ত্র করিতে প্রবর্তনে ॥২০২॥
verses.transliteration: ei dui bhāiye āmi pāṭhāiluṅ vṛndāvane\\nśakti diyā bhakti-śāstra karite pravartane
verses.translation: I empowered both of these brothers to go to Vṛndāvana to expand the literature of bhakti."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu informed Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya that he and Sanātana Gosvāmī had engaged equally in devotional service after giving up all relationships with material activity. Such renunciation is a symptom of an unalloyed devotee engaged in the service of the Lord with no tinge of material contamination. According to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, this is the position of
tṛṇād api sunīcena taror api sahiṣṇunā.
A pure devotee, free from the reactions of the material modes of nature, executes devotional service with tolerance like that of a tree. He also feels humbler than the grass. Such a devotee, who is called
niṣkiñcana
or free from all material possessions, is always absorbed in emotional love of Godhead. He is reluctant to perform any kind of sense gratification. In other words, such a devotee is free from all material bondage, but he engages in Kṛṣṇa conscious activities. Such expert devotional service is performed without hypocrisy. Humility, renunciation and learned scholarship were combined in Sanātana Gosvāmī, the ideal pure devotee, who was on the same level of understanding as Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya. Like Rāmānanda Rāya, Sanātana Gosvāmī was a fully cognizant expert in the conclusions of devotional service and was therefore able to describe such transcendental knowledge.

verses.devanagari: রায় কহে, — “ঈশ্বর তুমি যে চাহ করিতে ।\\nকাষ্ঠের পুতলী তুমি পার নাচাইতে ॥২০৩॥
verses.transliteration: rāya kahe,—"īśvara tumi ye cāha karite\\nkāṣṭhera putalī tumi pāra nācāite
verses.translation: Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya replied to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, "My Lord, You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead. If You like, You can cause even a wooden doll to dance.

verses.devanagari: মোর মুখে যে সব রস করিলা প্রচারণে ।\\nসেই রস দেখি এই ইহার লিখনে ॥২০৪॥
verses.transliteration: mora mukhe ye saba rasa karilā pracāraṇe\\nsei rasa dekhi ei ihāra likhane
verses.translation: "I see that the truths regarding transcendental mellow that You have expounded through my mouth are all explained in the writings of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.

verses.devanagari: ভক্তে কৃপা-হেতু প্রকাশিতে চাহ ব্রজ-রস ।\\nযারে করাও, সেই করিবে জগৎ তোমার বশ ॥২০৫॥
verses.transliteration: bhakte kṛpā-hetu prakāśite cāha vraja-rasa\\nyāre karāo, sei karibe jagat tomāra vaśa
verses.translation: "Because of Your causeless mercy toward Your devotees, You want to describe the transcendental pastimes in Vṛndāvana. Anyone empowered to do this can bring the entire world under Your influence."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This passage parallels the statement k
ṛṣṇa-śakti vinā nahe tāra pravartana,
which means that unless empowered by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, one cannot spread the holy name of the Lord throughout the entire world (Cc. Antya 7.11). Under the protection of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, a pure devotee can preach the holy name of the Lord so that everyone may take advantage of this facility and thus become Kṛṣṇa conscious.

verses.devanagari: তবে মহাপ্রভু কৈলা রূপে আলিঙ্গন ।\\nতাঁরে করাইলা সবার চরণ বন্দন ॥২০৬॥
verses.transliteration: tabe mahāprabhu kailā rūpe āliṅgana\\ntāṅre karāilā sabāra caraṇa vandana
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then embraced Rūpa Gosvāmī and asked him to offer prayers at the lotus feet of all the devotees present.

verses.devanagari: অদ্বৈত-নিত্যানন্দাদি সব ভক্তগণ ।\\nকৃপা করি’ রূপে সবে কৈলা আলিঙ্গন ॥২০৭॥
verses.transliteration: advaita-nityānandādi saba bhakta-gaṇa\\nkṛpā kari' rūpe sabe kailā āliṅgana
verses.translation: Advaita Ācārya, Nityānanda Prabhu and all the other devotees showed their causeless mercy to Rūpa Gosvāmī by embracing him in return.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু-কৃপা রূপে, আর রূপের সদ্গুণ ।\\nদেখি’ চমৎকার হৈল সবাকার মন ॥২০৮॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu-kṛpā rūpe, āra rūpera sad-guṇa\\ndekhi' camatkāra haila sabākāra mana
verses.translation: Seeing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's special mercy toward Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī and seeing his personal qualities, all the devotees were struck with wonder.

verses.devanagari: তবে মহাপ্রভু সব ভক্ত লঞা গেলা ।\\nহরিদাস-ঠাকুর রূপে আলিঙ্গন কৈলা ॥২০৯॥
verses.transliteration: tabe mahāprabhu saba bhakta lañā gelā\\nharidāsa-ṭhākura rūpe āliṅgana kailā
verses.translation: Then, when Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu left with all of His devotees, Haridāsa Ṭhākura also embraced Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.

verses.devanagari: হরিদাস কহে, — “তোমার ভাগ্যের নাহি সীমা ।\\nযে সব বর্ণিলা, ইহার কে জানে মহিমা ?” ॥ ২১০ ॥
verses.transliteration: haridāsa kahe,—"tomāra bhāgyera nāhi sīmā\\nye saba varṇilā, ihāra ke jāne mahimā?"
verses.translation: Haridāsa Ṭhākura told him: "There is no limit to your good fortune. No one can understand the glories of what you have described."

verses.devanagari: শ্রীরূপ কহেন, — “আমি কিছুই না জানি ।\\nযেই মহাপ্রভু কহান, সেই কহি বাণী ।।” ॥ ২১১ ॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-rūpa kahena,—āmi kichui nā jāni\\nyei mahāprabhu kahāna, sei kahi vāṇī
verses.translation: Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī said, "I do not know anything. The only transcendental words I can utter are those which Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu makes me speak.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The poet or writer dealing with transcendental subject matters is not an ordinary writer or translator. Because he is empowered by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, whatever he writes becomes very effective. The principle of being empowered by the Supreme Personality of Godhead is essential. A materialistic poet who describes in his poetry the material activities of man and woman cannot describe the transcendental pastimes of the Lord or the transcendental conclusions of devotional service. Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī has therefore warned all neophyte devotees that one should not hear from the mouth of a non-Vaiṣṇava.
avaiṣṇava-mukhodgīrṇaṁ
pūtaṁ hari-kathāmṛtam
śravaṇaṁ naiva kartavyaṁ
sarpocchiṣṭaṁ yathā payaḥ
(
Padma Purāṇa
)
Unless one is a fully unalloyed devotee of the Lord, one should not try to describe the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa in poetry, for it will be only mundane. There are many descriptions of Kṛṣṇa's
Bhagavad-gītā
written by persons whose consciousness is mundane and who are not qualified by pure devotion. Although they attempted to write transcendental literature, they could not fully engage even a single devotee in Kṛṣṇa's service. Such literature is mundane, and therefore, as warned by Śrī Sanātana Gosvāmī, one should not touch it.

verses.devanagari: হৃদি যস্য প্রেরণয়া প্রবর্তিতোঽহং বরাকরূপোঽপি ।\\nতস্য হরেঃ পদকমলং বন্দে চৈতন্যদেবস্য ॥২১২॥
verses.transliteration: hṛdi yasya preraṇayā\\npravartito 'haṁ varāka-rūpo 'pi\\ntasya hareḥ pada-kamalaṁ\\nvande caitanya-devasya
verses.translation: 'Although I am the lowest of men and have no knowledge, the Lord has mercifully bestowed upon me the inspiration to write transcendental literature about devotional service. Therefore I offer my obeisances at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who has given me the chance to write these books.' "
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse is from
Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu
(1.1.2).

verses.devanagari: এইমত দুইজন কৃষ্ণকথারঙ্গে ।\\nসুখে কাল গোঙায় রূপ হরিদাস-সঙ্গে ॥২১৩॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata dui-jana kṛṣṇa-kathā-raṅge\\nsukhe kāla goṅāya rūpa haridāsa-saṅge
verses.translation: In this way Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī passed his time in close association with Haridāsa Ṭhākura by discussing the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa in great happiness.

verses.devanagari: চারি মাস রহি’ সব প্রভুর ভক্তগণ ।\\nগোসাঞি বিদায় দিলা, গৌড়ে করিলা গমন ॥২১৪॥
verses.transliteration: cāri māsa rahi' saba prabhura bhakta-gaṇa\\ngosāñi vidāya dilā, gauḍe karilā gamana
verses.translation: All the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thus spent four months with Him. Then the Lord bade them farewell, and they returned to Bengal.

verses.devanagari: শ্রীরূপ প্রভুপদে নীলাচলে রহিলা ।\\nদোলযাত্রা প্রভুসঙ্গে আনন্দে দেখিলা ॥২১৫॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-rūpa prabhu-pade nīlācale rahilā\\ndola-yātrā prabhu-saṅge ānande dekhilā
verses.translation: Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, however, stayed at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and when the Dola-yātrā festival took place, he saw it in great happiness with the Lord.

verses.devanagari: দোল অনন্তরে প্রভু রূপে বিদায় দিলা ।\\nঅনেক প্রসাদ করি’ শক্তি সঞ্চারিলা ॥২১৬॥
verses.transliteration: dola anantare prabhu rūpe vidāya dilā\\naneka prasāda kari' śakti sañcārilā
verses.translation: After the Dola-yātrā festival ended, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bade farewell to Rūpa Gosvāmī also. The Lord empowered him and bestowed upon him all kinds of mercy.

verses.devanagari: “বৃন্দাবনে যাহ’ তুমি, রহিহ বৃন্দাবনে ।\\nএকবার ইহাঁ পাঠাইহ সনাতনে ॥২১৭॥
verses.transliteration: "vṛndāvane yāha' tumi, rahiha vṛndāvane\\nekabāra ihāṅ pāṭhāiha sanātane
verses.translation: "Now go to Vṛndāvana and stay there," the Lord said. "You may send here your elder brother, Sanātana.

verses.devanagari: ব্রজে যাই রসশাস্ত্র করিহ নিরূপণ ।\\nলুপ্ত-তীর্থ সব তাহাঁ করিহ প্রচারণ ॥২১৮॥
verses.transliteration: vraje yāi rasa-śāstra kariha nirūpaṇa\\nlupta-tīrtha saba tāhāṅ kariha pracāraṇa
verses.translation: "When you go to Vṛndāvana, stay there, preach transcendental literature and excavate the lost holy places.

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণসেবা, রসভক্তি করিহ প্রচার ।\\nআমিহ দেখিতে তাহাঁ যাইমু একবার ।।” ॥ ২১৯ ॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇa-sevā, rasa-bhakti kariha pracāra\\nāmiha dekhite tāhāṅ yāimu ekabāra"
verses.translation: "Establish the service of Lord Kṛṣṇa and preach the mellows of Lord Kṛṣṇa's devotional service. I shall also go to Vṛndāvana once more."

verses.devanagari: এত বলি’ প্রভু তাঁরে কৈলা আলিঙ্গন ।\\nরূপ গোসাঞি শিরে ধরে প্রভুর চরণ ॥২২০॥
verses.transliteration: eta bali' prabhu tāṅre kailā āliṅgana\\nrūpa gosāñi śire dhare prabhura caraṇa
verses.translation: Having thus spoken, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu embraced Rūpa Gosvāmī, who then placed the lotus feet of the Lord upon his head.

verses.devanagari: প্রভুর ভক্তগণ-পাশে বিদায় লইলা ।।\\nপুনরপি গৌড়-পথে বৃন্দাবনে আইলা ॥২২১॥
verses.transliteration: prabhura bhakta-gaṇa-pāśe vidāya la-ilā\\npunarapi gauḍa-pathe vṛndāvane āilā
verses.translation: Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī took leave of all the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and returned to Vṛndāvana by the path to Bengal.

verses.devanagari: এই ত’ কহিলাঙ পুনঃ রূপের মিলন ।\\nইহা যেই শুনে, পায় চৈতন্যচরণ ॥২২২॥
verses.transliteration: ei ta' kahilāṅa punaḥ rūpera milana\\nihā yei śune, pāya caitanya-caraṇa
verses.translation: Thus I have described the second meeting of Rūpa Gosvāmī and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Anyone who hears of this incident will certainly attain the shelter of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: শ্রীরূপ-রঘুনাথ-পদে যার আশ ।\\nচৈতন্যচরিতামৃত কহে কৃষ্ণদাস ॥২২৩॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa\\ncaitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa
verses.translation: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThus end the Bhaktivedanta purports to Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā,  First Chapter, describing the second meeting of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

sections.title: Chapter 2: The Chastisement of Junior Haridāsa

verses.devanagari: বন্দেঽহং শ্রীগুরোঃ শ্রীযুতপদকমলং শ্রীগুরূন্ বৈষ্ণবাংশ্চ\\nশ্রীরূপং সাগ্রজাতং সহগণরঘুনাথান্বিতং তং সজীবম্ ।\\nসাদ্বৈতং সাবধূতং পরিজনসহিতং কৃষ্ণচৈতন্যদেবং\\nশ্রীরাধাকৃষ্ণপাদান্ সহগণললিতা-শ্রীবিশাখান্বিতাংশ্চ ॥১॥
verses.transliteration: vande 'haṁ śrī-guroḥ śrī-yuta-pada-kamalaṁ śrī-gurūn vaiṣṇavāṁś ca\\nśrī-rūpaṁ sāgrajātaṁ saha-gaṇa-raghunāthānvitaṁ taṁ sa-jīvam\\nsādvaitaṁ sāvadhūtaṁ parijana-sahitaṁ kṛṣṇa-caitanya-devaṁ\\nśrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇa-pādān saha-gaṇa-lalitā-śrī-viśākhānvitāṁś ca
verses.translation: I offer my respectful obeisances unto the lotus feet of my spiritual master and of all the other preceptors on the path of devotional service. I offer my respectful obeisances unto all the Vaiṣṇavas and unto the six Gosvāmīs, including Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī, Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī, Jīva Gosvāmī and their associates. I offer my respectful obeisances unto Śrī Advaita Ācārya Prabhu, Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and all His devotees, headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura. I then offer my respectful obeisances unto the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and all the gopīs, headed by Lalitā and Viśākhā.

verses.devanagari: জয় জয় শ্রীচৈতন্য জয় নিত্যানন্দ ।\\nজয়াদ্বৈতচন্দ্র জয় গৌরভক্তবৃন্দ ॥২॥
verses.transliteration: jaya jaya śrī-caitanya jaya nityānanda\\njayādvaita-candra jaya gaura-bhakta-vṛnda
verses.translation: All glories to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Nityānanda Prabhu! All glories to Advaita Ācārya! And all glories to all the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu!

verses.devanagari: সর্ব-লোক উদ্ধারিতে গৌর-অবতার ।\\nনিস্তারের হেতু তার ত্রিবিধ প্রকার ॥৩॥
verses.transliteration: sarva-loka uddhārite gaura-avatāra\\nnistārera hetu tāra trividha prakāra
verses.translation: In His incarnation as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa descended to deliver all the living beings in the three worlds, from Brahmaloka down to Pātālaloka. He caused their deliverance in three ways.

verses.devanagari: সাক্ষাৎ-দর্শন, আর যোগ্যভক্ত-জীবে ।\\n‘আবেশ’ করয়ে কাহাঁ, কাহাঁ ‘আবির্ভাবে’ ॥৪॥
verses.transliteration: sākṣāt-darśana, āra yogya-bhakta-jīve\\n'āveśa' karaye kāhāṅ, kāhāṅ 'āvirbhāve'
verses.translation: The Lord delivered the fallen souls in some places by meeting them directly, in other places by empowering a pure devotee, and in still other places by appearing before someone Himself.

verses.devanagari: ‘সাক্ষাৎ-দর্শনে’ প্রায় সব নিস্তারিলা ।\\nনকুল-ব্রহ্মচারীর দেহে ‘আবিষ্ট’ হইলা ॥৫॥\\nপ্রদ্যুম্ন-নৃসিংহানন্দ আগে কৈলা ‘আবির্ভাব’ ।\\n‘লোক নিস্তারিব,’ — এই ঈশ্বর-স্বভাব ॥৬॥
verses.transliteration: pradyumna-nṛsiṁhānanda āge kailā 'āvirbhāva'\\n'loka nistāriba',—ei īśvara-svabhāva
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu delivered almost all the fallen souls by directly meeting them. He delivered others by entering the body of Nakula Brahmacārī and by appearing before Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī. "I shall deliver the fallen souls." This statement characterizes the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The Lord always manifested His
āvirbhāva
appearance in the following four places: (1) the house of Śrīmatī Śacīmātā, (2) wherever Nityānanda Prabhu danced in ecstasy, (3) the house of Śrīvāsa (when
kīrtana
was performed), and (4) the house of Rāghava Paṇḍita. Lord Caitanya Himself appeared in these four places. On this connection, one may consult text 34.)

verses.devanagari: সাক্ষাৎ-দর্শনে সব জগৎ তারিলা ।\\nএকবার যে দেখিলা, সে কৃতার্থ হইলা ॥৭॥
verses.transliteration: sākṣāt-darśane saba jagat tārilā\\neka-bāra ye dekhilā, se kṛtārtha ha-ilā
verses.translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was personally present, anyone in the world who met Him even once was fully satisfied and became spiritually advanced.

verses.devanagari: গৌড়-দেশের ভক্তগণ প্রত্যব্দ আসিয়া ।\\nপুনঃ গৌড়দেশে যায় প্রভুরে মিলিয়া ॥৮॥
verses.transliteration: gauḍa-deśera bhakta-gaṇa pratyabda āsiyā\\npunaḥ gauḍa-deśe yāya prabhure miliyā
verses.translation: Every year, devotees from Bengal would go to Jagannātha Purī to meet Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and after the meeting they would return to Bengal.

verses.devanagari: আর নানা-দেশের লোক আসি’ জগন্নাথ ।\\nচৈতন্য-চরণ দেখি’ হইল কৃতার্থ ॥৯॥
verses.transliteration: āra nānā-deśera loka āsi' jagannātha\\ncaitanya-caraṇa dekhi' ha-ila kṛtārtha
verses.translation: Similarly, people who went to Jagannātha Purī from various provinces of India were fully satisfied after seeing the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: সপ্তদ্বীপের লোক আর নবখণ্ডবাসী ।\\nদেব, গন্ধর্ব, কিন্নর মনুষ্য-বেশে আসি’ ॥১০॥
verses.transliteration: sapta-dvīpera loka āra nava-khaṇḍa-vāsī\\ndeva, gandharva, kinnara manuṣya-veśe āsi'
verses.translation: People from all over the universe, including the seven islands, the nine khaṇḍas, the planets of the demigods, Gandharvaloka and Kinnaraloka, would go there in the forms of human beings.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
For an explanation of
sapta-dvīpa,
see
Madhya-līlā,
Chapter Twenty, verse 218, and
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,
Fifth Canto, Chapters Sixteen and Twenty. in the
Siddhānta-śiromaṇi,
Chapter One (
Golādhyāya
), in the
Bhuvana-kośa
section, the nine
khaṇḍas
are mentioned as follows:
aindraṁ kaśeru sakalaṁ kila tāmraparṇam
anyad gabhastimad ataś ca kumārikākhyam
nāgaṁ ca saumyam iha vāruṇam antya-khaṇḍaṁ
gāndharva-saṁjñam iti bhārata-varṣa-madhye
"Within Bhārata-varṣa, there are nine
khaṇḍas.
They are known as (1) Aindra, (2) Kaśeru, (3) Tāmraparṇa, (4) Gabhastimat, (5) Kumārikā, (6) Nāga (7) Saumya, (8) Vāruṇa and (9) Gāndharva."

verses.devanagari: প্রভুরে দেখিয়া যায় ‘বৈষ্ণব’ হঞা ।\\nকৃষ্ণ বলি’ নাচে সব প্রেমাবিষ্ট হঞা ॥১১॥
verses.transliteration: prabhure dekhiyā yāya 'vaiṣṇava' hañā\\nkṛṣṇa bali' nāce saba premāviṣṭa hañā
verses.translation: Having seen the Lord, they all became Vaiṣṇavas. Thus they danced and chanted the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra in ecstatic love of Godhead.

verses.devanagari: এইমত দর্শনে ত্রিজগৎ নিস্তারি  ।\\nযে কেহ আসিতে নারে অনেক সংসারী ॥১২॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata darśane trijagat nistāri\\nye keha āsite nāre aneka saṁsārī
verses.translation: Thus by direct meetings, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu delivered the three worlds. Some people, however, could not go and were entangled in material activities.

verses.devanagari: তা-সবা তারিতে প্রভু সেই সব দেশে  ।\\nযোগ্যভক্ত জীবদেহে করেন ‘আবেশে’ ॥১৩॥
verses.transliteration: tā-sabā tārite prabhu sei saba deśe\\nyogya-bhakta jīva-dehe karena 'āveśe'
verses.translation: To deliver people in regions throughout the universe who could not meet Him, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu personally entered the bodies of pure devotees.

verses.devanagari: সেই জীবে নিজ-ভক্তি করেন প্রকাশে ।\\nতাহার দর্শনে ‘বৈষ্ণব’ হয় সর্বদেশে ॥১৪॥
verses.transliteration: sei jīve nija-bhakti karena prakāśe\\ntāhāra darśane 'vaiṣṇava' haya sarva-deśe
verses.translation: Thus He empowered living beings [His pure devotees] by manifesting in them so much of His own devotion that people in all other countries became devotees by seeing them.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
As stated in
Caitanya-caritāmṛta
(Antya 7.11):
kali-kālera dharma-kṛṣṇa-nāma-saṅkīrtana
kṛṣṇa-śakti vinā nahe tāra pravartana
Unless one is empowered by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, one cannot spread the holy names of the Hare Kṛṣṇa
mahā-mantra
throughout the world. Persons who do so are empowered. Therefore they are sometimes called
āveśa-avatāras
or incarnations, for they are endowed with the power of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: এইমত আবেশে তারিল ত্রিভুবন ।\\nগৌড়ে যৈছে আবেশ, করি দিগ্ দরশন ॥১৫॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata āveśe tārila tribhuvana\\ngauḍe yaiche āveśa, kari dig daraśana
verses.translation: In this way Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu delivered the entire three worlds, not only by His personal presence but also by empowering others. I shall briefly describe how He empowered a living being in Bengal.

verses.devanagari: আম্বুয়া-মুলুকে হয় নকুল-ব্রহ্মচারী ।\\nপরম-বৈষ্ণব তেঁহো বড় অধিকারী ॥১৬॥
verses.transliteration: āmbuyā-muluke haya nakula-brahmacārī\\nparama-vaiṣṇava teṅho baḍa adhikārī
verses.translation: In Āmbuyā-muluka there was a person named Nakula Brahmacārī, who was a perfectly pure devotee, greatly advanced in devotional service.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nŚrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura says that Āmbuyā-muluka is the present Ambikā, a city in the Vardhamāna district of West Bengal. Formerly, during the Mohammedan regime, it was known as Āmbuyā-muluka. In this city there is a neighborhood called Pyārīgañja, and that is where Nakula Brahmacārī used to live.

verses.devanagari: গৌড়দেশের লোক নিস্তারিতে মন হৈল ।\\nনকুল-হৃদয়ে প্রভু ‘আবেশ’ করিল ॥১৭॥
verses.transliteration: gauḍa-deśera loka nistārite mana haila\\nnakula-hṛdaye prabhu 'āveśa' karila
verses.translation: Desiring to deliver all the people of Bengal, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu entered the heart of Nakula Brahmacārī.

verses.devanagari: গ্রহগ্রস্তপ্রায় নকুল প্রেমাবিষ্ট হঞা ।\\nহাসে, কান্দে, নাচে, গায় উন্মত্ত হঞা ॥১৮॥
verses.transliteration: graha-grasta-prāya nakula premāviṣṭa hañā\\nhāse, kānde, nāce, gāya unmatta hañā
verses.translation: Nakula Brahmacārī became exactly like a man haunted by a ghost. Thus he sometimes laughed, sometimes cried, sometimes danced and sometimes chanted like a madman.

verses.devanagari: অশ্রু, কম্প, স্তম্ভ, স্বেদ, সাত্ত্বিক বিকার ।\\nনিরন্তর প্রেমে নৃত্য, সঘন হুঙ্কার ॥১৯॥
verses.transliteration: aśru, kampa, stambha, sveda, sāttvika vikāra\\nnirantara preme nṛtya, saghana huṅkāra
verses.translation: He continuously exhibited bodily transformations of transcendental love. Thus he cried, trembled, became stunned, perspired, danced in love of Godhead and made sounds like those of a cloud.

verses.devanagari: তৈছে গৌরকান্তি, তৈছে সদা প্রেমাবেশ ।\\nতাহা দেখিবারে আইসে সর্ব গৌড়দেশ ॥২০॥
verses.transliteration: taiche gaura-kānti, taiche sadā premāveśa\\ntāhā dekhibāre āise sarva gauḍa-deśa
verses.translation: His body shone with the same luster as that of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and he showed the same absorption in ecstatic love of Godhead. People came from all provinces of Bengal to see these symptoms.

verses.devanagari: যারে দেখে তারে কহে, — ‘কহ কৃষ্ণনাম’ ।\\nতাঁহার দর্শনে লোক হয় প্রেমোদ্দাম ॥২১॥
verses.transliteration: yāre dekhe tāre kahe,—'kaha kṛṣṇa-nāma'\\ntāṅhāra darśane loka haya premoddāma
verses.translation: He advised whomever he met to chant the holy names Hare Kṛṣṇa. Thus upon seeing him, people were overwhelmed with love of Godhead.

verses.devanagari: চৈতন্যের আবেশ হয় নকুলের দেহে ।\\nশুনি’ শিবানন্দ আইলা করিয়া সন্দেহে ॥২২॥
verses.transliteration: caitanyera āveśa haya nakulera dehe\\nśuni' śivānanda āilā kariyā sandehe
verses.translation: When Śivānanda Sena heard that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had entered the body of Nakula Brahmacārī, he went there with doubts in his mind.

verses.devanagari: পরীক্ষা করিতে তাঁর যবে ইচ্ছা হৈল  ।\\nবাহিরে রহিয়া তবে বিচার করিল ॥২৩॥
verses.transliteration: parīkṣā karite tāṅra yabe icchā haila\\nbāhire rahiyā tabe vicāra karila
verses.translation: Desiring to test the authenticity of Nakula Brahmacārī, he stayed outside, thinking as follows.

verses.devanagari: “আপনে বোলান মোরে, ইহা যদি জানি ।\\nআমার ইষ্ট-মন্ত্র জানি’ কহেন আপনি ॥২৪॥\\nতবে জানি, ইঁহাতে হয় চৈতন্য-আবেশে ।” এত চিন্তি’ শিবানন্দ রহিলা দূরদেশে ॥২৫॥
verses.transliteration: tabe jāni, iṅhāte haya caitanya-āveśe"\\neta cinti' śivānanda rahilā dūra-deśe
verses.translation: "If Nakula Brahmacārī personally calls me and knows my worshipable mantra, then I shall understand that he is inspired by the presence of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu." Thinking in this way, he stayed some distance apart.

verses.devanagari: অসংখ্য লোকের ঘটা, — কেহ আইসে যায় ।\\nলোকের সংঘট্টে কেহ দর্শন না পায় ॥২৬॥
verses.transliteration: asaṅkhya lokera ghaṭā,—keha āise yāya\\nlokera saṅghaṭṭe keha darśana nā pāya
verses.translation: There was a large crowd of people, some coming and some going. Indeed, some people in that great crowd could not even see Nakula Brahmacārī.

verses.devanagari: আবেশে ব্রহ্মচারী কহে, — ‘শিবানন্দ আছে দূরে ।\\nজন দুই চারি যাহ, বোলাহ তাহারে ।।’ ॥ ২৭ ॥
verses.transliteration: āveśe brahmacārī kahe,—'śivānanda āche dūre\\njana dui cāri yāha, bolāha tāhāre'
verses.translation: In his inspired state, Nakula Brahmacārī said, "Śivānanda Sena is staying some distance away. Two or four of you go call him."

verses.devanagari: চারিদিকে ধায় লোকে ‘শিবানন্দ’ বলি ।\\nশিবানন্দ কোন্, তোমায় বোলায় ব্রহ্মচারী ॥২৮॥
verses.transliteration: cāri-dike dhāya loke 'śivānanda' bali\\nśivānanda kon, tomāya bolāya brahmacārī
verses.translation: Thus people began running here and there, calling in all directions, "Śivānanda! Whoever is Śivānanda, please come. Nakula Brahmacārī is calling you."

verses.devanagari: শুনি’ শিবানন্দ সেন তাঁহা শীঘ্র আইল ।\\nনমস্কার করি’ তাঁর নিকটে বসিল ॥২৯॥
verses.transliteration: śuni, śivānanda sena tāṅhā śīghra āila\\nnamaskāra kari' tāṅra nikaṭe vasila
verses.translation: Hearing these calls, Śivānanda Sena quickly went there, offered obeisances to Nakula Brahmacārī, and sat down near him.

verses.devanagari: ব্রহ্মচারী বলে, — “তুমি করিলা সংশয়  ।\\nএক-মনা হঞা শুন তাহার নিশ্চয় ॥৩০॥
verses.transliteration: brahmacārī bale,—"tumi karilā saṁśaya\\neka-manā hañā śuna tāhāra niścaya
verses.translation: Nakula Brahmacārī said, "I know that you are doubtful. Now please hear this evidence with great attention.

verses.devanagari: ‘গৌরগোপাল মন্ত্র’ তোমার চারি অক্ষর  ।\\nঅবিশ্বাস ছাড়, যেই করিয়াছ অন্তর ।।” ৩১ ॥৩১॥
verses.transliteration: 'gaura-gopāla mantra' tomāra cāri akṣara\\naviśvāsa chāḍa, yei kariyācha antara"
verses.translation: "You are chanting the Gaura-gopāla mantra composed of four syllables. Now please give up the doubts that have resided within you."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura explains the Gaura-gopāla
mantra
in his
Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya.
Worshipers of Śrī Gaurasundara accept the four syllables
gau-ra-aṇ-ga
as the Gaura
mantra,
but pure worshipers of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa accept the four syllables
rā-dhā kṛṣ-ṇa
as the Gaura-gopāla
mantra.
However, Vaiṣṇavas consider Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu nondifferent from Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa (
śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya rādhā-kṛṣṇa nahe anya
). Therefore one who chants the
mantra
Gaurāṅga and one who chants the names of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa are on the same level.

verses.devanagari: তবে শিবানন্দের মন প্রতীতি হইল ।\\nঅনেক সম্মান করি’ বহু ভক্তি কৈল ॥৩২॥
verses.transliteration: tabe śivānandera mane pratīti ha-ila\\naneka sammāna kari' bahu bhakti kaila
verses.translation: Śivānanda Sena thereupon developed full confidence in his mind that Nakula Brahmacārī was filled with the presence of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Śivānanda Sena then offered him respect and devotional service.

verses.devanagari: এইমত মহাপ্রভুর অচিন্ত্য প্রভাব ।\\nএবে শুন প্রভুর যৈছে হয় ‘আবির্ভাব ।।’ ॥ ৩৩ ॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata mahāprabhura acintya prabhāva\\nebe śuna prabhura yaiche haya 'āvirbhāva'
verses.translation: In this way, one should understand the inconceivable potencies of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Now please hear how His appearance [āvirbhāva] takes place.

verses.devanagari: শচীর মন্দিরে, আর নিত্যানন্দ-নর্তনে ।\\nশ্রীবাস-কীর্তনে, আর রাঘব-ভবনে ॥৩৪॥\\nএই চারি ঠাঞি প্রভুর সদা ‘আবির্ভাব’ ।\\nপ্রেমাকৃষ্ট হয়, — প্রভুর সহজ স্বভাব ॥৩৫॥
verses.transliteration: ei cāri ṭhāñi prabhura sadā 'āvirbhāva'\\npremākṛṣṭa haya,—prabhura sahaja svabhāva
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu always appeared in four places-in the household temple of mother Śacī, in the places where Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu danced, in the house of Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita during congregational chanting and in the house of Rāghava Paṇḍita. He appeared because of His attraction to the love of His devotees. That is His natural characteristic.

verses.devanagari: নৃসিংহানন্দের আগে আবির্ভূত হঞা ।\\nভোজন করিলা, তাহা শুন মন দিয়া ॥৩৬॥
verses.transliteration: nṛsiṁhānandera āge āvirbhūta hañā\\nbhojana karilā, tāhā śuna mana diyā
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu appeared before Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī and ate his offerings. Please hear about this with attention.

verses.devanagari: শিবানন্দের ভাগিনা শ্রীকান্ত-সেন নাম ।\\nপ্রভুর কৃপাতে তেঁহো বড় ভাগ্যবান্ ॥৩৭॥
verses.transliteration: śivānandera bhāginā śrī-kānta-sena nāma\\nprabhura kṛpāte teṅho baḍa bhāgyavān
verses.translation: Śivānanda Sena had a nephew named Śrīkānta Sena, who by the grace of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was extremely fortunate.

verses.devanagari: এক বৎসর তেঁহো প্রথম একেশ্বর ।\\nপ্রভু দেখিবারে আইলা উৎকণ্ঠা-অন্তর ॥৩৮॥
verses.transliteration: eka vatsara teṅho prathama ekeśvara\\nprabhu dekhibāre āilā utkaṇṭhā-antara
verses.translation: One year, Śrīkānta Sena came alone to Jagannātha Purī in great eagerness to see the Lord.

verses.devanagari: মহাপ্রভু তারে দেখি’ বড় কৃপা কৈলা ।\\nমাস-দুই তেঁহো প্রভুর নিকটে রহিলা ॥৩৯॥
verses.transliteration: mahāprabhu tāre dekhi' baḍa kṛpā kailā\\nmāsa-dui teṅho prabhura nikaṭe rahilā
verses.translation: Seeing Śrīkānta Sena, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bestowed causeless mercy upon him. Śrīkānta Sena stayed near Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu for about two months at Jagannātha Purī.

verses.devanagari: তবে প্রভু তাঁরে আজ্ঞা কৈলা গৌড়ে যাইতে  ।\\n“ভক্তগণে নিষেধিহ এথাকে আসিতে ॥৪০॥
verses.transliteration: tabe prabhu tāṅre ājñā kailā gauḍe yāite\\n"bhakta-gaṇe niṣedhiha ethāke āsite
verses.translation: When he was about to return to Bengal, the Lord told him, "Forbid the devotees of Bengal to come to Jagannātha Purī this year.

verses.devanagari: এ-বৎসর তাঁহা আমি যাইমু আপনে  ।\\nতাহাই মিলিমু সব অদ্বৈতাদি সনে ॥৪১॥
verses.transliteration: e-vatsara tāṅhā āmi yāimu āpane\\ntāhāi milimu saba advaitādi sane
verses.translation: "This year I shall personally go to Bengal and meet all the devotees there, headed by Advaita Ācārya.

verses.devanagari: শিবানন্দে কহিহ, — আমি এই পৌষ-মাসে ।\\nআচম্বিতে অবশ্য আমি যাইব তাঁর পাশে ॥৪২॥
verses.transliteration: śivānande kahiha,—āmi ei pauṣa-māse\\nācambite avaśya āmi yāiba tāṅra pāśe
verses.translation: "Please inform Śivānanda Sena that this December I shall certainly go to his home.

verses.devanagari: জগদানন্দ হয় তাহাঁ, তেঁহো ভিক্ষা দিবে ।\\nসবারে কহিহ, — এ বৎসর কেহ না আসিবে ।।” ॥ ৪৩ ॥
verses.transliteration: jagadānanda haya tāhāṅ, teṅho bhikṣā dibe\\nsabāre kahiha,—e vatsara keha nā āsibe"
verses.translation: "Jagadānanda is there, and he will give Me offerings of food. Inform them all that no one should come to Jagannātha Purī this year."

verses.devanagari: শ্রীকান্ত আসিয়া গৌড়ে সন্দেশ কহিল ।\\nশুনি’ ভক্তগণ-মনে আনন্দ হইল ॥৪৪॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-kānta āsiyā gauḍe sandeśa kahila\\nśuni' bhakta-gaṇa-mane ānanda ha-ila
verses.translation: When Śrīkānta Sena returned to Bengal and delivered this message, the minds of all the devotees were very pleased.

verses.devanagari: চলিতেছিলা আচার্য, রহিলা স্থির হঞা ।\\nশিবানন্দ, জগদানন্দ রহে প্রত্যাশা করিয়া ॥৪৫॥
verses.transliteration: calitechilā ācārya, rahilā sthira hañā\\nśivānanda, jagadānanda rahe pratyāśā kariyā
verses.translation: Advaita Ācārya was just about to go to Jagannātha Purī with the other devotees, but upon hearing this message, He waited. Śivānanda Sena and Jagadānanda also stayed back, awaiting the arrival of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: পৌষ-মাস আইল দুহেঁ সামগ্রী করিয়া ।\\nসন্ধ্যা-পর্যন্ত রহে অপেক্ষা করিয়া ॥৪৬॥
verses.transliteration: pauṣa-māse āila duṅhe sāmagrī kariyā\\nsandhyā-paryanta rahe apekṣā kariyā
verses.translation: When the month of Pauṣa arrived, both Jagadānanda and Śivānanda collected all kinds of paraphernalia for the Lord's reception. Every day, they would wait until evening for the Lord to come.

verses.devanagari: এইমত মাস গেল, গোসাঞি না আইলা ।\\nজগদানন্দ, শিবানন্দ দুঃখিত হইলা ॥৪৭॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata māsa gela, gosāñi nā āilā\\njagadānanda, śivānanda duḥkhita ha-ilā
verses.translation: As the month passed but Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not come, Jagadānanda and Śivānanda became most unhappy.

verses.devanagari: আচম্বিতে নৃসিংহানন্দ তাহাঁই আইলা ।\\nদুঁহে তাঁরে মিলি’ তবে স্থানে বসাইলা ॥৪৮॥\\nদুঁহে দুঃখী দেখি’ তবে কহে নৃসিংহানন্দ ।\\n‘তোমা দুহাঁকারে কেনে দেখি নিরানন্দ ?’ ৪৯ ॥৪৯॥
verses.transliteration: duṅhe duḥkhī dekhi' tabe kahe nṛsiṁhānanda\\n'tomā duṅhākāre kene dekhi nirānanda?'
verses.translation: Suddenly Nṛsiṁhānanda arrived, and Jagadānanda and Śivānanda arranged for him to sit near them. Seeing them both so unhappy, Nṛsiṁhānanda inquired, "Why do I see that you are both despondent?"

verses.devanagari: তবে শিবানন্দ তাঁরে সকল কহিলা ।\\n‘আসিব আজ্ঞা দিলা প্রভু কেনে না আইলা ?’ ॥ ৫০ ॥
verses.transliteration: tabe śivānanda tāṅre sakala kahilā\\n'āsiba ājñā dilā prabhu kene nā āilā?'
verses.translation: Then Śivānanda Sena told him, "Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu promised that He would come. Why, then, has He not arrived?"

verses.devanagari: শুনি’ ব্রহ্মচারী কহে, — ‘করহ সন্তোষে ।\\nআমি ত’ আনিব তাঁরে তৃতীয় দিবসে ।।” ॥ ৫১ ॥
verses.transliteration: śuni' brahmacārī kahe,—'karaha santoṣe\\nāmi ta' āniba tāṅre tṛtīya divase'
verses.translation: Hearing this, Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī replied, "Please be satisfied. I assure you that I shall bring Him here three days from now."

verses.devanagari: তাঁহার প্রভাব-প্রেম জানে দুইজনে ।\\nআনিবে প্রভুরে এবে নিশ্চয় কৈলা মনে ॥৫২॥
verses.transliteration: tāṅhāra prabhāva-prema jāne dui-jane\\nānibe prabhure ebe niścaya kailā mane
verses.translation: Śivānanda and Jagadānanda knew of Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī's influence and love of Godhead. Therefore they now felt assured that he would certainly bring Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: ‘প্রদ্যুম্ন ব্রহ্মচারী’ — তাঁর নিজ-নাম ।\\n‘নৃসিংহানন্দ’ নাম তাঁর কৈলা গৌরধাম ॥৫৩॥
verses.transliteration: 'pradyumna brahmacārī'—tāṅra nija-nāma\\n'nṛsiṁhānanda' nāma tāṅra kailā gaura-dhāma
verses.translation: His real name was Pradyumna Brahmacārī. The name Nṛsiṁhānanda had been given to him by Lord Gaurasundara Himself.

verses.devanagari: দুই দিন ধ্যান করি’ শিবানন্দেরে কহিল  ।\\n“পাণিহাটি গ্রামে আমি প্রভুরে আনিল ॥৫৪॥
verses.transliteration: dui dina dhyāna kari' śivānandere kahila\\n"pāṇihāṭi grāme āmi prabhure ānila
verses.translation: After meditating for two days, Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī told Śivānanda Sena, "I have already brought Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to the village known as Pāṇihāṭi.

verses.devanagari: কালি মধ্যাহ্নে তেঁহো আসিবেন তোমার ঘরে  ।\\nপাক-সামগ্রী আনহ, আমি ভিক্ষা দিমু তাঁরে ॥৫৫॥
verses.transliteration: kāli madhyāhne teṅho āsibena tomāra ghare\\npāka-sāmagrī ānaha, āmi bhikṣā dimu tāṅre
verses.translation: "Tomorrow at noon He will come to your home. Therefore please bring all kinds of cooking ingredients. I shall personally cook and offer Him food.

verses.devanagari: তবে তাঁরে এথা আমি আনিব সত্বর ।\\nনিশ্চয় কহিলাঙ, কিছু সন্দেহ না কর ॥৫৬॥
verses.transliteration: tabe tāṅre ethā āmi āniba satvara\\nniścaya kahilāṅa, kichu sandeha nā kara
verses.translation: "In this way I shall bring Him here very soon. Be assured that I am telling you the truth. Do not be doubtful.

verses.devanagari: যে চাহিয়ে, তাহা কর হঞা তৎপর ।\\nঅতি ত্বরায় করিব পাক, শুন অতঃপর ॥৫৭॥
verses.transliteration: ye cāhiye, tāhā kara hañā tat-para\\nati tvarāya kariba pāka, śuna ataḥpara
verses.translation: "Bring all the ingredients very soon, for I want to begin cooking immediately. Please do what I say."

verses.devanagari: পাক-সামগ্রী আনহ, আমি যাহা চাই ।’\\nযে মাগিল, শিবানন্দ আনি’ দিলা তাই ॥৫৮॥
verses.transliteration: pāka-sāmagrī ānaha, āmi yāhā cāi'\\nye māgila, śivānanda āni' dilā tāi
verses.translation: Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī said to Śivānanda, "Please bring whatever cooking ingredients I want." Thus Śivānanda Sena immediately brought whatever he asked for.

verses.devanagari: প্রাতঃকাল হৈতে পাক করিলা অপার ।\\nনানা ব্যঞ্জন, পিঠা, ক্ষীর নানা উপহার ॥৫৯॥
verses.transliteration: prātaḥ-kāla haite pāka karilā apāra\\nnānā vyañjana, piṭhā, kṣīra nānā upahāra
verses.translation: Beginning early in the morning, Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī cooked many varieties of food, including vegetables, cakes, sweet rice and other preparations.

verses.devanagari: জগন্নাথের ভিন্ন ভোগ পৃথক্ বাড়িল  ।\\nচৈতন্য প্রভুর লাগি’ আর ভোগ কৈল ॥৬০॥
verses.transliteration: jagannāthera bhinna bhoga pṛthak bāḍila\\ncaitanya prabhura lāgi' āra bhoga kaila
verses.translation: After he finished cooking, he brought separate dishes for Jagannātha and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: ইষ্টদেব নৃসিংহ লাগি’ পৃথক্ বাড়িল  ।\\nতিন-জনে সমর্পিয়া বাহিরে ধ্যান কৈল ॥৬১॥
verses.transliteration: iṣṭa-deva nṛsiṁha lāgi' pṛthak bāḍila\\ntina-jane samarpiyā bāhire dhyāna kaila
verses.translation: He also separately offered dishes to Nṛsiṁhadeva, his worshipable Deity. Thus he divided all the food into three offerings. Then, outside the temple, he began to meditate upon the Lord.

verses.devanagari: দেখে, শীঘ্র আসি’ বসিলা চৈতন্য-গোসাঞি ।\\nতিন ভোগ খাইলা, কিছু অবশিষ্ট নাই ॥৬২॥
verses.transliteration: dekhe, śīghra āsi' vasilā caitanya-gosāñi\\ntina bhoga khāilā, kichu avaśiṣṭa nāi
verses.translation: In his meditation he saw Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu quickly come, sit down and eat all three offerings, leaving behind no remnants.

verses.devanagari: আনন্দে বিহ্বল প্রদ্যুম্ন, পড়ে অশ্রুধার ।\\n“হাহা কিবা কর” বলি’ করয়ে ফুৎকার ॥৬৩॥
verses.transliteration: ānande vihvala pradyumna, paḍe aśru-dhāra\\n"hāhā kibā kara" bali' karaye phutkāra
verses.translation: Pradyumna Brahmacārī was overwhelmed by transcendental ecstasy upon seeing Caitanya Mahāprabhu eating everything. Thus tears flowed from his eyes. Nevertheless, he expressed dismay, saying, "Alas, alas! My dear Lord, what are You doing? You are eating everyone's food!

verses.devanagari: ‘জগন্নাথে-তোমায় ঐক্য, খাও তাঁর ভোগ ।\\nনৃসিংহের ভোগ কেনে কর উপযোগ ? ॥ ৬৪ ॥
verses.transliteration: jagannāthe-tomāya aikya, khāo tāṅra bhoga\\nnṛsiṁhera bhoga kene kara upayoga?
verses.translation: "My dear Lord, You are one with Jagannātha; therefore I have no objection to Your eating His offering. But why are You touching the offering to Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva?

verses.devanagari: নৃসিংহের হৈল জানি আজি উপবাস ।\\nঠাকুর উপবাসী রহে, জিয়ে কৈছে দাস ?’ ॥ ৬৫ ॥
verses.transliteration: nṛsiṁhera haila jāni āji upavāsa\\nṭhākura upavāsī rahe, jiye kaiche dāsa?'
verses.translation: "I think that Nṛsiṁhadeva could not eat anything today, and therefore lie is fasting. If the master fasts, how can the servant live?"

verses.devanagari: ভোজন দেখি’ যদ্যপি তাঁর হৃদয়ে উল্লাস ।\\nনৃসিংহ লক্ষ্য করি’ বাহ্যে কিছু করে দুঃখাভাস ॥৬৬॥
verses.transliteration: bhojana dekhi' yadyapi tāṅra hṛdaye ullāsa\\nnṛsiṁha lakṣya kari' bāhye kichu kare duḥkhābhāsa
verses.translation: Although Nṛsiṁha Brahmacārī felt jubilation within his heart to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu eating everything, for the sake of Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva he externally expressed disappointment.

verses.devanagari: স্বয়ং ভগবান্ কৃষ্ণচৈতন্য-গোসাঞি ।\\nজগন্নাথ-নৃসিংহ-সহ কিছু ভেদ নাই ॥৬৭॥
verses.transliteration: svayaṁ bhagavān kṛṣṇa-caitanya-gosāñi\\njagannātha-nṛsiṁha-saha kichu bheda nāi
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself. Therefore there is no difference between Him, Lord Jagannātha and Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva.

verses.devanagari: ইহা জানিবারে প্রদ্যুম্নের গূঢ় হৈল মন ।\\nতাহা দেখাইলা প্রভু করিয়া ভোজন ॥৬৮॥
verses.transliteration: ihā jānibāre pradyumnera gūḍha haita mana\\ntāhā dekhāilā prabhu kariyā bhojana
verses.translation: Pradyumna Brahmacārī was deeply eager to understand this fact. Therefore Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu revealed it to him by a practical demonstration.

verses.devanagari: ভোজন করিয়া প্রভু গেলা পাণিহাটি ।\\nসন্তোষ পাইলা দেখি’ ব্যঞ্জন-পরিপাটী ॥৬৯॥
verses.transliteration: bhojana kariyā prabhu gelā pāṇihāṭi\\nsantoṣa pāilā dekhi' vyañjana-paripāṭī
verses.translation: After eating all the offerings, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu started for Pāṇihāṭi. There, He was greatly satisfied to see the different varieties of vegetables prepared in the house of Rāghava.

verses.devanagari: শিবানন্দ কহে, — ‘কেনে করহ ফুৎকার ?’ তেঁহ কহে, — “দেখ তোমার প্রভুর ব্যবহার ॥৭০॥
verses.transliteration: śivānanda kahe,—'kene karaha phutkāra?'\\nteṅha kahe,—"dekha tomāra prabhura vyavahāra
verses.translation: Śivānanda said to Nṛsiṁhānanda, "Why are you expressing dismay?" Nṛsiṁhānanda replied, "Just see the behavior of your Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: তিন জনার ভোগ তেঁহো একেলা খাইলা  ।\\nজগন্নাথ-নৃসিংহ উপবাসী হইলা ।।” ৭১ ॥৭১॥
verses.transliteration: tina janāra bhoga teṅho ekelā khāilā\\njagannātha-nṛsiṁha upavāsī ha-ilā"
verses.translation: "He alone has eaten the offerings for all three Deities. Because of this, both Jagannātha and Nṛsiṁhadeva remain fasting."

verses.devanagari: শুনি শিবানন্দের চিত্তে হইল সংশয় ।\\nকিবা প্রেমাবেশে কহে, — কিবা সত্য হয় ॥৭২॥
verses.transliteration: śuni śivānandera citte ha-ila saṁśaya\\nkibā premāveśe kahe, kibā satya haya
verses.translation: When Śivānanda Sena heard this statement, he was unsure whether Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī was speaking that way because of ecstatic love or because it was actually a fact.
