verses.devanagari: তবে শিবানন্দে কিছু কহে ব্রহ্মচারী ।\\n‘সামগ্রী আন নৃসিংহ লাগি পুনঃ পাক করি’ ॥৭৩॥
verses.transliteration: tabe śivānande kichu kahe brahmacārī\\nsāmagrī āna nṛsiṁha lāgi punaḥ pāka kari'
verses.translation: When Śivānanda Sena was thus perplexed, Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī said to him, "Bring more food. Let me cook again for Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva."

verses.devanagari: তবে শিবানন্দ ভোগ-সামগ্রী আনিলা ।\\nপাক করি’ নৃসিংহের ভোগ লাগাইলা ॥৭৪॥
verses.transliteration: tabe śivānanda bhoga-sāmagrī ānilā\\npāka kari' nṛsiṁhera bhoga lāgāilā
verses.translation: Then Śivānanda Sena again brought the ingredients with which to cook, and Pradyumna Brahmacārī again cooked and offered the food to Nṛsiṁhadeva.

verses.devanagari: বর্ষান্তরে শিবানন্দ লঞা ভক্তগণ ।\\nনীলাচলে দেখে যাঞা প্রভুর চরণ ॥৭৫॥
verses.transliteration: varṣāntare śivānanda lañā bhakta-gaṇa\\nnīlācale dekhe yāñā prabhura caraṇa
verses.translation: The next year, Śivānanda went to Jagannātha Purī with all the other devotees to see the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: একদিন সভাতে প্রভু বাত চালাইলা ।\\nনৃসিংহানন্দের গুণ কহিতে লাগিলা ॥৭৬॥
verses.transliteration: eka-dina sabhāte prabhu vāta cālāilā\\nnṛsiṁhānandera guṇa kahite lāgilā
verses.translation: One day, in the presence of all the devotees, the Lord raised these topics concerning Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī and praised his transcendental qualities.

verses.devanagari: ‘গতবর্ষ পৌষে মোরে করাইল ভোজন ।\\nকভু নাহি খাই ঐছে মিষ্টান্ন-ব্যঞ্জন ॥৭৭॥
verses.transliteration: 'gata-varṣa pauṣe more karāila bhojana\\nkabhu nāhi khāi aiche miṣṭānna-vyañjana'
verses.translation: The Lord said, "Last year in the month of Pauṣa, when Nṛsiṁhānanda gave me varieties of sweetmeats and vegetables to eat, they were so good that I had never before eaten such preparations."

verses.devanagari: শুনি’ ভক্তগণ মনে আশ্চর্য মানিল ।\\nশিবানন্দের মনে তবে প্রত্যয় জন্মিল ॥৭৮॥
verses.transliteration: śuni' bhakta-gaṇa mane āścarya mānila\\nśivānandera mane tabe pratyaya janmila
verses.translation: Hearing this, all the devotees were struck with wonder, and Śivānanda became confident that the incident was true.

verses.devanagari: এইমত শচীগৃহে সতত ভোজন ।\\nশ্রীবাসের গৃহে করেন কীর্তন-দর্শন ॥৭৯॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata śacī-gṛhe satata bhojana\\nśrīvāsera gṛhe karena kīrtana-darśana
verses.translation: In this way Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu used to eat at the temple of Śacīmātā every day and also visit the house of Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura when kīrtana was performed.

verses.devanagari: নিত্যানন্দের নৃত্য দেখেন আসি’ বারে বারে ।\\n‘নিরন্তর আবির্ভাব’ রাঘবের ঘরে ॥৮০॥
verses.transliteration: nityānandera nṛtya dekhena āsi' bāre bāre\\n'nirantara āvirbhāva' rāghavera ghare
verses.translation: Similarly, He was always present when Nityānanda Prabhu danced, and He regularly appeared at the house of Rāghava.

verses.devanagari: প্রেমবশ গৌরপ্রভু, যাহাঁ প্রেমোত্তম ।\\nপ্রেমবশ হঞা তাহা দেন দরশন ॥৮১॥
verses.transliteration: prema-vaśa gaura-prabhu, yāhāṅ premottama\\nprema-vasa hañā tāhā dena daraśana
verses.translation: Lord Gaurasundara is greatly influenced by the love of His devotees. Therefore wherever there is pure devotion to the Lord, the Lord Himself, subdued by such love, appears, and His devotees see Him.

verses.devanagari: শিবানন্দের প্রেমসীমা কে কহিতে পারে ?\\nযাঁর প্রেমে বশ প্রভু আইসে বারে বারে ॥৮২॥
verses.transliteration: śivānandera prema-sīmā ke kahite pāre?\\nyāṅra preme vaśa prabhu āise bāre bāre
verses.translation: Influenced by the loving affairs of Śivānanda Sena, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu came again and again. Therefore who can estimate the limits of his love?

verses.devanagari: এই ত’ কহিলু গৌরের ‘আবির্ভাব’ ।\\nইহা যেই শুনে, জানে চৈতন্য-প্রভাব ॥৮৩॥
verses.transliteration: ei ta' kahilu gaurera 'āvirbhāva'\\nihā yei śune, jāne caitanya-prabhāva
verses.translation: Thus I have described the appearance of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Anyone who hears about these incidents can understand the transcendental opulence of the Lord.

verses.devanagari: পুরুষোত্তমে প্রভু-পাশে ভগবান্ আচার্য ।\\nপরম বৈষ্ণব তেঁহো সুপণ্ডিত আর্য ॥৮৪॥
verses.transliteration: puruṣottame prabhu-pāśe bhagavān ācārya\\nparama vaiṣṇava teṅho supaṇḍita ārya
verses.translation: At Jagannātha Purī, in the association of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, lived Bhagavān Ācārya, who was certainly a gentleman, a learned scholar and a great devotee.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
For a description of Bhagavān Ācārya, one may refer to the
Ādi-līlā,
Tenth Chapter, verse 136.

verses.devanagari: সখ্যভাবাক্রান্ত-চিত্ত, গোপ-অবতার ।\\nস্বরূপ-গোসাঞি-সহ সখ্য-ব্যবহার ॥৮৫॥
verses.transliteration: sakhya-bhāvākrānta-citta, gopa-avatāra\\nsvarūpa-gosāñi-saha sakhya-vyavahāra
verses.translation: He was fully absorbed in thoughts of fraternal relationships with God. He was an incarnation of a cowherd boy, and thus his dealings with Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī were very friendly.

verses.devanagari: একান্তভাবে আশ্রিয়াছেন চৈতন্যচরণ ।\\nমধ্যে মধ্যে প্রভুর তেঁহো করেন নিমন্ত্রণ ॥৮৬॥
verses.transliteration: ekānta-bhāve āśriyāchena caitanya-caraṇa\\nmadhye madhye prabhura teṅho karena nimantraṇa
verses.translation: He sought the shelter of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu with full surrender. Sometimes he would invite the Lord to dine at his home.

verses.devanagari: ঘরে ভাত করি’ করেন বিবিধ ব্যঞ্জন ।\\nএকলে গোসাঞি লঞা করান ভোজন ॥৮৭॥
verses.transliteration: ghare bhāta kari' karena vividha vyañjana\\nekale gosāñi lañā karāna bhojana
verses.translation: Bhagavān Ācārya prepared varieties of rice and vegetables at home and brought the Lord there alone to eat.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Generally those who invited Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu for dinner used to offer Him the remnants of food that had first been offered to Lord Jagannātha. Bhagavān Ācārya, however, instead of giving Him the remnants of Jagannātha's food, prepared dinner at his home. In Orissa, food offered to Lord Jagannātha is called
prasādī,
and that which is not offered to Lord Jagannātha is known as
āmānī
or
ghara-bhāta,
rice prepared at home.

verses.devanagari: তাঁর পিতা ‘বিষয়ী’ বড় শতানন্দ-খাঁন ।\\n‘বিষয়বিমুখ’ আচার্য — ‘বৈরাগ্যপ্রধান’ ॥৮৮॥
verses.transliteration: tāṅra pitā 'viṣayī' baḍa śatānanda-khāṅna\\n'viṣaya-vimukha' ācārya—'vairāgya-pradhāna'
verses.translation: Bhagavān Ācārya's father, whose name was Śatānanda Khān, was an expert statesman, whereas Bhagavān Ācārya was not at all interested in the management of the state. Indeed, he was almost in the renounced order of life.

verses.devanagari: ‘গোপাল-ভট্টাচার্য’ নাম তাঁর ছোট-ভাই ।\\nকাশীতে বেদান্ত পড়ি’ গেলা তাঁর ঠাঞি ॥৮৯॥
verses.transliteration: 'gopāla-bhaṭṭācārya' nāma tāṅra choṭa-bhāi\\nkāśīte vedānta paḍi' gelā tāṅra ṭhāñi
verses.translation: Bhagavān Ācārya's brother, whose name was Gopāla Bhaṭṭācārya, had studied Vedānta philosophy at Benares and had then returned to Bhagavān Ācārya's home.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
During those days and also at the present, Vedānta philosophy is understood through the commentary of Śaṅkarācārya, which is known as
Śārīraka-bhāṣya.
Thus it appears that Gopāla Bhaṭṭācārya the younger brother of Bhagavān Ācārya, had studied Vedānta according to the way of the
Śārīraka-bhāṣya,
which expounds the Māyāvāda philosophy of the impersonalists.

verses.devanagari: আচার্য তাহারে প্রভুপদে মিলাইলা ।\\nঅন্তর্যামী প্রভু চিত্তে সুখ না পাইলা ॥৯০॥
verses.transliteration: ācārya tāhāre prabhu-pade milāilā\\nantaryāmī prabhu citte sukha nā pāilā
verses.translation: Bhagavān Ācārya took his brother to meet Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, but the Lord, knowing that Gopāla Bhaṭṭācārya was a Māyāvādī philosopher, could not get much happiness from meeting him.

verses.devanagari: আচার্য-সম্বন্ধে বাহ্যে করে প্রীত্যাভাস ।\\nকৃষ্ণভক্তি বিনা প্রভুর না হয় উল্লাস ॥৯১॥
verses.transliteration: ācārya-sambandhe bāhye kare prītyābhāsa\\nkṛṣṇa-bhakti vinā prabhura nā haya ullāsa
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu derives no happiness from meeting one who is not a pure devotee of Kṛṣṇa. Thus because Gopāla Bhaṭṭācārya was a Māyāvādī scholar, the Lord felt no jubilation in meeting him. Nevertheless, because Gopāla Bhaṭṭācārya was related to Bhagavān Ācārya, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu feigned pleasure in seeing him.

verses.devanagari: স্বরূপ গোসাঞিরে আচার্য কহে আর দিনে  ।\\n‘বেদান্ত পড়িয়া গোপাল আইসাছে এখানে ॥৯২॥
verses.transliteration: svarūpa gosāñire ācārya kahe āra dine\\n'vedānta paḍiyā gopāla āisāche ekhāne
verses.translation: Bhagavān Ācārya said to Svarūpa Dāmodara, "Gopāla, my younger brother, has returned to my home, having concluded his study of Vedānta philosophy."

verses.devanagari: সবে মেলি’ আইস, শুনি ‘ভাষ্য’ ইহার স্থানে’  ।\\nপ্রেম-ক্রোধ করি’ স্বরূপ বলয় বচনে ॥৯৩॥
verses.transliteration: sabe meli' āisa, śuni 'bhāṣya' ihāra sthāne'\\nprema-krodha kari' svarūpa balaya vacane
verses.translation: Bhagavān Ācārya requested Svarūpa Dāmodara to hear from Gopāla the commentary upon Vedānta. Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, however, somewhat angry because of love, spoke as follows.

verses.devanagari: “বুদ্ধি ভ্রষ্ট হৈল তোমার গোপালের সঙ্গে  ।\\nমায়াবাদ শুনিবারে উপজিল রঙ্গে ॥৯৪॥
verses.transliteration: "buddhi bhraṣṭa haila tomāra gopālera saṅge\\nmāyāvāda śunibāre upajila raṅge
verses.translation: "You have lost your intelligence in the association of Gopāla, and therefore you are eager to hear the Māyāvāda philosophy.

verses.devanagari: বৈষ্ণব হঞা যেবা শারীরক-ভাষ্য শুনে ।\\nসেব্য-সেবক-ভাব ছাড়ি’ আপনারে ‘ঈশ্বর’ মানে ॥৯৫॥
verses.transliteration: vaiṣṇava hañā yebā śārīraka-bhāṣya śune\\nsevya-sevaka-bhāva chāḍi' āpanāre 'īśvara' māne
verses.translation: "When a Vaiṣṇava listens to the Śārīraka-bhāṣya, the Māyāvāda commentary upon Vedānta-sūtra, he gives up the Kṛṣṇa conscious attitude that the Lord is the master and the living entity is His servant. Instead, he considers himself the Supreme Lord.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The philosophers known as
kevalādvaita-vādīs
generally occupy themselves with hearing the
Śārīraka-bhāṣya,
a commentary by Śaṅkarācārya advocating that one impersonally consider oneself the Supreme Lord. Such Māyāvāda philosophical commentaries upon Vedānta are simply imaginary, but there are other commentaries on Vedānta philosophy. The commentary by Śrīla Rāmānujācārya, known as
Śrī-bhāṣya,
establishes the
viśiṣṭādvaita-vāda
philosophy. Similarly, in the Brahma-sampradāya, Madhvācārya's
Pūrṇaprajña-bhāṣya
establishes
śuddha-dvaita-vāda.
In the Kumāra-sampradāya, or Nimbārka-sampradāya, Śrī Nimbārka establishes the philosophy of
dvaitādvaita-vāda
in the
Pārijāta-saurabha-bhāṣya.
And in the Viṣṇusvāmi-sampradāya, or Rudra-sampradāya, which comes from Lord Śiva, Viṣṇusvāmī has written a commentary called
Sarvajña-bhāṣya,
which establishes
śuddhādvaita-vāda.
A Vaiṣṇava should study the commentaries on
Vedānta-sūtra
written by the four
sampradāya-ācāryas,
namely Śrī Rāmānujācārya, Madhvācārya, Viṣṇusvāmī and Nimbārka, for these commentaries are based upon the philosophy that the Lord is the master and that all living entities are His eternal servants. One interested in studying Vedānta philosophy properly must study these commentaries, especially if he is a Vaiṣṇava. These commentaries are always adored by Vaiṣṇavas. The commentary by Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī is elaborately given in the
Ādi-līlā,
Chapter Seven, text 101. The Māyāvāda commentary
Śārīraka-bhāṣya
is like poison for a Vaiṣṇava. It should not be touched at all. Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura remarks that even a
mahā-bhāgavata,
or highly elevated devotee who has surrendered himself unto the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, sometimes falls down from pure devotional service if he hears the Māyāvāda philosophy of
Śārīraka-bhāṣya.
This commentary should therefore be shunned by all Vaiṣṇavas.

verses.devanagari: মহাভাগবত যেই, কৃষ্ণ প্রাণধন যার ।\\nমায়াবাদ-শ্রবণে চিত্ত অবশ্য ফিরে তাঁর ।।” ॥ ৯৬ ॥
verses.transliteration: mahā-bhāgavata yei, kṛṣṇa prāṇa-dhana yāra\\nmāyāvāda-śravaṇe citta avaśya phire tāṅra"
verses.translation: "The Māyāvāda philosophy presents such a jugglery of words that even a highly elevated devotee who has accepted Kṛṣṇa as his life and soul changes his decision when he reads the Māyāvāda commentary on Vedānta-sūtra."

verses.devanagari: আচার্য কহে, — ‘আমা সবার কৃষ্ণনিষ্ঠ-চিত্তে ।\\nআমা সবার মন ভাষ্য নারে ফিরাইতে ।।’ ॥ ৯৭ ॥
verses.transliteration: ācārya kahe,—'āmā sabāra kṛṣṇa-niṣṭha-citte\\nāmā sabāra mana bhāṣya nāre phirāite'
verses.translation: In spite of Svarūpa Dāmodara's protest, Bhagavān Ācārya continued, "We are all fixed at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa with our hearts and souls. Therefore the Śārīraka-bhāṣya cannot change our minds."

verses.devanagari: স্বরূপ কহে, — “তথাপি মায়াবাদ-শ্রবণে ।\\n“চিৎ, ব্রহ্ম, মায়া, মিথ্যা’ — এইমাত্র শুনে ॥৯৮॥
verses.transliteration: svarūpa kahe, "tathāpi māyāvāda-śravaṇe\\n'cit, brahma, māyā, mithyā'—ei-mātra śune
verses.translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara replied, "Nevertheless, when we hear the Māyāvāda philosophy, we hear that Brahman is knowledge and that the universe of māyā is false, but we gain no spiritual understanding.

verses.devanagari: জীবাজ্ঞান-কল্পিত ঈশ্বরে, সকলই অজ্ঞান ।\\nযাহার শ্রবণে ভক্তের ফাটে মন প্রাণ ।।” ॥ ৯৯ ॥
verses.transliteration: jīvājñāna-kalpita īśvare, sakala-i ajñāna\\nyāhāra śravaṇe bhaktera phāṭe mana prāṇa"
verses.translation: "The Māyāvādī philosopher tries to establish that the living entity is only imaginary and that the Supreme Personality of Godhead is under the influence of māyā. Hearing this kind of commentary breaks the heart and life of a devotee."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrīla Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī wanted to impress upon Bhagavān Ācārya that even though someone firmly fixed in devotion to Kṛṣṇa's service might not be deviated by hearing the Māyāvāda
bhāṣya,
that
bhāṣya
is nevertheless full of impersonal words and ideas such as Brahman which represent knowledge but which are impersonal. The Māyāvādīs say that the world created by
māyā
is false, and that actually there is no living entity but only one spiritual effulgence. They further say that God is imaginary, that people think of God only because of ignorance, and that when the Supreme Absolute Truth is befooled by the external energy,
māyā,
He becomes a
jīva,
or living entity. Upon hearing all these nonsensical ideas from the nondevotee, a devotee is greatly afflicted, as if his heart and soul were broken.

verses.devanagari: লজ্জা-ভয় পাঞা আচার্য মৌন হইলা ।\\nআর দিন গোপালেরে দেশে পাঠাইলা ॥১০০॥
verses.transliteration: lajjā-bhaya pāñā ācārya mauna ha-ilā\\nāra dina gopālere deśe pāṭhāilā
verses.translation: Thus Bhagavān Ācārya, greatly ashamed and fearful, remained silent. The next day, he asked Gopāla Bhaṭṭācārya to return to his own district.

verses.devanagari: একদিন আচার্য প্রভুরে কৈলা নিমন্ত্রণ ।\\nঘরে ভাত করি’ করে বিবিধ ব্যঞ্জন ॥১০১॥
verses.transliteration: eka-dina ācārya prabhure kailā nimantraṇa\\nghare bhāta kari' kare vividha vyañjana
verses.translation: One day Bhagavān Ācārya invited Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to dine at his home. Thus he was preparing rice and various types of vegetables.

verses.devanagari: ‘ছোট-হরিদাস’ নাম প্রভুর কীর্তনীয়া  ।\\nতাহারে কহেন আচার্য ডাকিয়া আনিয়া ॥১০২॥
verses.transliteration: 'choṭa-haridāsa' nāma prabhura kīrtanīyā\\ntāhāre kahena ācārya ḍākiyā āniyā
verses.translation: A devotee named Choṭa Haridāsa used to sing for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Bhagavān Ācārya called him to his home and spoke as follows.

verses.devanagari: ‘মোর নামে শিখি-মাহিতির ভগিনী-স্থানে গিয়া  ।\\nশুক্লচাউল এক মান আনহ মাগিয়া ।।” ১০৩ ॥১০৩॥
verses.transliteration: 'mora nāme śikhi-māhitira bhaginī-sthāne giyā\\nśukla-cāula eka māna ānaha māgiyā'
verses.translation: "Please go to the sister of Śikhi Māhiti. In my name, ask her for a māna of white rice and bring it here."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
In India
śukla-cāula
(white rice) is also called
ātapa-cāula,
or rice that has not been boiled before being threshed. Another kind of rice, called
siddha-cāula
(brown rice), is boiled before being threshed. Generally, first-class fine white rice is required for offerings to the Deity. Thus Bhagavān Ācārya asked Choṭa Haridāsa, or Junior Haridāsa, a singer in the assembly of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, to get some of this rice from the sister of Śikhi Māhiti. A
māna
is a standard of measurement in Orissa for rice and other food grains.

verses.devanagari: মাহিতির ভগিনী সেই, নাম — মাধবী-দেবী ।\\nবৃদ্ধা তপস্বিনী আর পরমা বৈষ্ণবী ॥১০৪॥
verses.transliteration: māhitira bhaginī sei, nāma—mādhavī-devī\\nvṛddhā tapasvinī āra paramā vaiṣṇavī
verses.translation: Śikhi Māhiti's sister was named Mādhavīdevī. She was an elderly lady who always performed austerities. She was very advanced in devotional service.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু লেখা করে যারে — রাধিকার ‘গণ’  ।\\nজগতের মধ্যে ‘পাত্র’ — সাড়ে তিন জন ॥১০৫॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu lekhā kare yāre—rādhikāra 'gaṇa'\\njagatera madhye 'pātra'—sāḍe tina jana
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted her as having formerly been an associate of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. In the entire world, three and a half people were His intimate devotees.

verses.devanagari: স্বরূপ গোসাঞি, আর রায় রামানন্দ  ।\\nশিখি-মাহিতি — তিন, তাঁর ভগিনী — অর্ধজন ॥১০৬॥
verses.transliteration: svarūpa gosāñi, āra rāya rāmānanda\\nśikhi-māhiti—tina, tāṅra bhaginī—ardha-jana
verses.translation: The three were Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, Rāmānanda Rāya and Śikhi Māhiti, and the half a person was Śikhi Māhiti's sister.

verses.devanagari: তাঁর ঠাঞি তণ্ডুল মাগি’ আনিল হরিদাস ।\\nতণ্ডুল দেখি’ আচার্যের অধিক উল্লাস ॥১০৭॥
verses.transliteration: tāṅra ṭhāñi taṇḍula māgi' ānila haridāsa\\ntaṇḍula dekhi' ācāryera adhika ullāsa
verses.translation: After begging the rice from her, Junior Haridāsa brought it to Bhagavān Ācārya, who was very pleased to see its quality.

verses.devanagari: স্নেহে রান্ধিল প্রভুর প্রিয় যে ব্যঞ্জন ।\\nদেউল প্রসাদ, আদা-চাকি, লেম্বু-সলবণ ॥১০৮॥
verses.transliteration: snehe rāndhila prabhura priya ye vyañjana\\ndeula prasāda, ādā-cāki, lembu-salavaṇa
verses.translation: In great affection, Bhagavān Ācārya cooked varieties of vegetables and other preparations dear to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He also obtained remnants of food from Lord Jagannātha and digestive aids such as ground ginger and also lime with salt.

verses.devanagari: মধ্যাহ্নে আসিয়া প্রভু ভোজনে বসিলা  ।\\nশাল্যন্ন দেখি’ প্রভু আচার্যে পুছিলা ॥১০৯॥
verses.transliteration: madhyāhne āsiyā prabhu bhojane vasilā\\nśālyanna dekhi' prabhu ācārye puchilā
verses.translation: At noon, when Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu came to eat the offerings of Bhagavān Ācārya, He first appreciated the fine rice and therefore questioned him.

verses.devanagari: উত্তম অন্ন এত তণ্ডুল কাঁহাতে পাইলা ? আচার্য কহে, — মাধবী-পাশ মাগিয়া আনিলা ॥১১০॥
verses.transliteration: uttama anna eta taṇḍula kāṅhāte pāilā?\\nācārya kahe,—mādhavī-pāśa māgiyā ānilā
verses.translation: "Where did you get such fine rice?" the Lord asked. Bhagavān Ācārya replied, "I got it by begging from Mādhavīdevī."

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহে, — ‘কোন্ যাই’ মাগিয়া আনিল ?’\\nছোট-হরিদাসের নাম আচার্য কহিল ॥১১১॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahe,—'kon yāi' māgiyā ānila?'\\nchoṭa-haridāsera nāma ācārya kahila
verses.translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu asked who had begged the rice and brought it back, Bhagavān Ācārya mentioned the name of Junior Haridāsa.

verses.devanagari: অন্ন প্রশংসিয়া প্রভু ভোজন করিলা  ।\\nনিজগৃহে আসি’ গোবিন্দেরে আজ্ঞা দিলা ॥১১২॥
verses.transliteration: anna praśaṁsiyā prabhu bhojana karilā\\nnija-gṛhe āsi' govindere ājñā dilā
verses.translation: Praising the quality of the rice, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu partook of the prasāda. Then, after returning to His residence, He gave the following order to Govinda, His personal assistant.

verses.devanagari: ‘আজি হৈতে এই মোর আজ্ঞা পালিবা  ।\\nছোট হরিদাসে ইহাঁ আসিতে না দিবা ।।’ ১১৩ ॥১১৩॥
verses.transliteration: 'āji haite ei mora ājñā pālibā\\nchoṭa haridāse ihāṅ āsite nā dibā'
verses.translation: " From this day forward, do not allow Choṭa Haridāsa to come here."

verses.devanagari: দ্বার মানা হৈল, হরিদাস দুঃখী হৈল মনে ।\\nকি লাগিয়া দ্বার-মানা কেহ নাহি জানে ॥১১৪॥
verses.transliteration: dvāra mānā haila, haridāsa duḥkhī haila mane\\nki lāgiyā dvāra-mānā keha nāhi jāne
verses.translation: When Junior Haridāsa heard that he had been ordered not to approach Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he was very unhappy. No one could understand why he had been ordered not to come.

verses.devanagari: তিনদিন হৈল হরিদাস করে উপবাস  ।\\nস্বরূপাদি আসি, পুছিলা মহাপ্রভুর পাশ ॥১১৫॥
verses.transliteration: tina-dina haila haridāsa kare upavāsa\\nsvarūpādi āsi, puchilā mahāprabhura pāśa
verses.translation: Haridāsa fasted continuously for three days. Then Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and other confidential devotees approached Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to inquire from Him.

verses.devanagari: “কোন্ অপরাধ, প্রভু, কৈল হরিদাস ? কি লাগিয়া দ্বার-মানা, করে উপবাস ?” ১১৬ ॥১১৬॥
verses.transliteration: "kon aparādha, prabhu, kaila haridāsa?\\nki lāgiyā dvāra-mānā, kare upavāsa?"
verses.translation: "What great offense has Junior Haridāsa committed? Why has he been forbidden to come to Your door? He has now been fasting for three days."

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহে, — “বৈরাগী করে প্রকৃতি সম্ভাষণ ।\\nদেখিতে না পারোঁ আমি তাহার বদন ॥১১৭॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahe,—"vairāgī kare prakṛti sambhāṣaṇa\\ndekhite nā pāroṅ āmi tāhāra vadana
verses.translation: The Lord replied, "I cannot tolerate seeing the face of a person who has accepted the renounced order of life but who still talks intimately with a woman.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura comments that
saralatā,
or simplicity, is the first qualification of a Vaiṣṇava, whereas duplicity or cunning behavior is a great offense against the principles of devotional service. As one advances in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, one must gradually become disgusted with material attachment and thus become more and more attached to the service of the Lord. If one is not factually detached from material activities but still proclaims himself advanced in devotional service, he is cheating. No one will be happy to see such behavior.

verses.devanagari: দুর্বার ইন্দ্রিয় করে বিষয়-গ্রহণ ।\\nদারবী প্রকৃতি হরে মুনেরপি মন ॥১১৮॥
verses.transliteration: durvāra indriya kare viṣaya-grahaṇa\\ndāravī prakṛti hare munerapi mana
verses.translation: "So strongly do the senses adhere to the objects of their enjoyment that indeed a wooden statue of a woman attracts the mind of even a great saintly person.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThe senses and the sense objects are so intimately connected that the mind of even a great saintly person is attracted to a wooden doll if it is attractively shaped like a young woman. The sense objects, namely form, sound, smell, taste and touch, are always attractive for the eyes, ears, nose, tongue and skin. Since the senses and sense objects are naturally intimately related, sometimes even a person claiming control over his senses remains always subject to the control of sense objects. The senses are impossible to control unless purified and engaged in the service of the Lord. Thus even though a saintly person vows to control his senses, the senses are still sometimes perturbed by sense objects.

verses.devanagari: মাত্রা স্বস্রা দুহিত্রা বা নাবিবিক্তাসনো ভবেৎ ।\\nবলবানিন্দ্রিয়গ্রামো বিদ্বাংসমপি কর্ষতি ॥১১৯॥
verses.transliteration: mātrā svasrā duhitrā vā\\nnā viviktāsano bhavet\\nbalavān indriya-grāmo\\nvidvāṁsam api karṣati
verses.translation: “ 'One should not sit closely with one's mother, sister or daughter, for the senses are so strong that they may attract even a person advanced in knowledge.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse appears in the
Manu-saṁhitā
(2.215) and
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(9.19.17).

verses.devanagari: ক্ষুদ্রজীব সব মর্কট-বৈরাগ্য করিয়া ।\\nইন্দ্রিয় চরাঞা বুলে ‘প্রকৃতি’ সম্ভাষিয়া ।।” ॥ ১২০ ॥
verses.transliteration: kṣudra-jīva saba markaṭa-vairāgya kariyā\\nindriya carāñā bule 'prakṛti' sambhāṣiyā"
verses.translation: "There are many persons with little in their possession who accept the renounced order of life like monkeys. They go here and there engaging in sense gratification and speaking intimately with women."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
One should strictly follow the regulative principles, namely no illicit sex, no meat-eating, no intoxication and no gambling, and in this way one should make progress in spiritual life. If an unfit person sentimentally accepts
vairāgya
or takes
sannyāsa
but at the same time remains attached to women, he is in a very dangerous position. His renunciation is called
markaṭa-vairāgya,
or renunciation like that of a monkey. The monkey lives in the forest, eats fruit and does not even cover itself with a cloth. In this way it resembles a saint, but the monkey always thinks of female monkeys and sometimes keeps dozens of them for sexual intercourse. This is called
markaṭa-vairāgya.
Therefore one who is unfit should not accept the renounced order of life. One who accepts the order of
sannyāsa
but again becomes agitated by sensual disturbances and talks privately with women is called
dharma-dhvajī
or
dharma-kalaṅka,
which means that he brings condemnation upon the religious order. Therefore one should be extremely careful in this connection. Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura explains the word
markaṭa
to mean "restless." A restless person cannot be steady; therefore he simply wanders about, gratifying his senses. Just to get praise from others, to get cheap adoration from his followers or people in general, such a person sometimes accepts the dress of a
sannyāsī
or
bābājī
in the renounced order, but he cannot give up desires for sense gratification, especially for the association of women. Such a person cannot make advancement in spiritual life. There are eight different kinds of sensual enjoyment with women, including talking about them and thinking about them. Thus for a
sannyāsī,
a person in the renounced order, talking intimately with women is a great offense. Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya and Śrīla Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura actually achieved the most elevated stage of the renounced order, but those who imitate them, accepting them as ordinary human beings, fall under the influence of the material energy, for that is a great misunderstanding.

verses.devanagari: এত কহি’ মহাপ্রভু অভ্যন্তরে গেলা ।\\nগোসাঞির আবেশ দেখি’ সবে মৌন হৈলা ॥১২১॥
verses.transliteration: eta kahi' mahāprabhu abhyantare gelā\\ngosāñira āveśa dekhi' sabe mauna hailā
verses.translation: After saying this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu entered His room. Seeing Him in such an angry mood, all the devotees fell silent.

verses.devanagari: আর দিনে সবে মেলি’ প্রভুর চরণে  ।\\nহরিদাস লাগি, কিছু কৈলা নিবেদনে ॥১২২॥
verses.transliteration: āra dine sabe meli' prabhura caraṇe\\nharidāsa lāgi, kichu kailā nivedane
verses.translation: The next day, all the devotees together approached the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to submit an appeal on behalf of Junior Haridāsa.

verses.devanagari: “অল্প অপরাধ, প্রভু করহ প্রসাদ  ।\\nএবে শিক্ষা হইল না করিবে অপরাধ” ॥১২৩॥
verses.transliteration: "alpa aparādha, prabhu karaha prasāda\\nebe śikṣā ha-ila nā karibe aparādha"
verses.translation: "Haridāsa has committed a small offense," they said. "Therefore, O Lord, please be merciful to him. Now he has received a sufficient lesson. In the future he will not commit such a offense."

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহে, — “মোর বশ নহে মোর মন ।\\nপ্রকৃতিসম্ভাষী বৈরাগী না করে দর্শন ॥১২৪॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahe,—"mora vaśa nahe mora mana\\nprakṛti-sambhāṣī vairāgī nā kare darśana
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "My mind is not under My control. It does not like to see anyone in the renounced order who talks intimately with women.

verses.devanagari: নিজ কার্যে যাহ সবে, ছাড় বৃথা কথা ।\\nপুনঃ যদি কহ আমা না দেখিবে হেথা ।।” ॥ ১২৫ ॥
verses.transliteration: nija kārye yāha sabe, chāḍa vṛthā kathā\\npunaḥ yadi kaha āmā nā dekhibe hethā"
verses.translation: "You should all tend to your respective engagements. Give up this useless talk. If you speak this way again, I shall go away, and you will no longer see Me here."

verses.devanagari: এত শুনি’ সবে নিজ-কর্ণে হস্ত দিয়া ।\\nনিজ নিজ কার্যে সবে গেল ত’ উঠিয়া ॥১২৬॥
verses.transliteration: eta śuni' sabe nija-karṇe hasta diyā\\nnija nija kārye sabe gela ta' uṭhiyā
verses.translation: Hearing this, all the devotees covered their ears with their hands, got up and went about their respective duties.

verses.devanagari: মহাপ্রভু মধ্যাহ্ন করিতে চলি’ গেলা ।\\nবুঝন না যায় এই মহাপ্রভুর লীলা ॥১২৭॥
verses.transliteration: mahāprabhu madhyāhna karite cali, gelā\\nbujhana nā yāya ei mahāprabhura līlā
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu also left that place to perform His noon duties. No one could understand His pastimes.

verses.devanagari: আর দিন সবে পরমানন্দপুরী-স্থানে ।\\n‘প্রভুকে প্রসন্ন কর’ — কৈলা নিবেদনে ॥১২৮॥
verses.transliteration: āra dina sabe paramānanda-purī-sthāne\\n'prabhuke prasanna kara'—kailā nivedane
verses.translation: The next day, all the devotees went to Śrī Paramānanda Purī and requested him to pacify the Lord.

verses.devanagari: তবে পুরী-গোসাঞি একা প্রভুস্থানে আইলা ।\\nনমস্করি’ প্রভু তাঁরে সম্ভ্রমে বসাইলা ॥১২৯॥
verses.transliteration: tabe purī-gosāñi ekā prabhu-sthāne āilā\\nnamaskari' prabhu tāṅre sambhrame vasāilā
verses.translation: Paramānanda Purī thereupon went alone to the residence of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. The Lord, after offering him obeisances, seated him by His side with great respect.

verses.devanagari: পুছিলা, — কি আজ্ঞা, কেনে হৈল আগমন ?\\n‘হরিদাসে প্রসাদ লাগি’ কৈলা নিবেদন ॥১৩০॥
verses.transliteration: puchilā,—ki ājñā, kene haila āgamana?\\n'haridāse prasāda lāgi' kailā nivedana
verses.translation: The Lord inquired, "What is your order? For what purpose have you come here?" Paramānanda Purī then submitted his prayer that the Lord show favor to Junior Haridāsa.

verses.devanagari: শুনিয়া কহেন প্রভু, — “শুনহ, গোসাঞি  ।\\nসব বৈষ্ণব লঞা তুমি রহ এই ঠাঞি ॥১৩১॥
verses.transliteration: śuniyā kahena prabhu,—"śunaha, gosāñi\\nsaba vaiṣṇava lañā tumi raha ei ṭhāñi
verses.translation: Hearing this request, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "My dear lord, please hear me. It is better for you to stay here with all the Vaiṣṇavas.

verses.devanagari: মোরে আজ্ঞা হয়, মুঞি যাঙ আলালনাথ  ।\\nএকলে রহিব তাহাঁ, গোবিন্দ-মাত্র সাথ ।।” ১৩২ ॥১৩২॥
verses.transliteration: more ājñā haya, muñi yāṅa ālālanātha\\nekale rahiba tāhāṅ, govinda-mātra sātha"
verses.translation: "Please give Me permission to go to Ālālanātha. I shall remain there alone; only Govinda will go with Me."

verses.devanagari: এত বলি’ প্রভু যদি গোবিন্দে বোলাইলা ।\\nপুরীরে নমস্কার করি’ উঠিয়া চলিলা ॥১৩৩॥
verses.transliteration: eta bali' prabhu yadi govinde bolāilā\\npurīre namaskāra kari' uṭhiyā calilā
verses.translation: After saying this, the Lord called for Govinda. Offering obeisances to Paramānanda Purī, He got up and began to leave.

verses.devanagari: আস্তে-ব্যস্তে পুরী-গোসাঞি প্রভু আগে গেলা ।\\nঅনুনয় করি’ প্রভুরে ঘরে বসাইলা ॥১৩৪॥
verses.transliteration: āste-vyaste purī-gosāñi prabhu āge gelā\\nanunaya kari' prabhure ghare vasāilā
verses.translation: In great haste Paramānanda Purī Gosāñi went before Him and with great humility persuaded Him to sit down in His own room.

verses.devanagari: “তোমার যে ইচ্ছা, কর, স্বতন্ত্র ঈশ্বর । কেবা কি বলিতে পারে তোমার উপর ? ১৩৫ ।। লোক-হিত লাগি’ তোমার সব ব্যবহার  ।\\nআমি সব না জানি গম্ভীর হৃদয় তোমার ।।” ১৩৬ ॥১৩৫॥
verses.transliteration: "tomāra ye icchā, kara, svatantra īśvara\\nkebā ki balite pāre tomāra upara?
verses.translation: Paramānanda Purī said, "My dear Lord Caitanya, You are the independent Personality of Godhead. You can do whatever You like. Who can say anything above You?

verses.devanagari: লোকহিত লাগি' তোমার সব ব্যবহার ।\\nআমি সব না জানি গম্ভীর হৃদয় তোমার" ॥১৩৬॥
verses.transliteration: loka-hita lāgi' tomāra saba vyavahāra\\nāmi saba nā jāni gambhīra hṛdaya tomāra"
verses.translation: "All Your activities are for the benefit of people in general. We cannot understand them, for Your intentions are deep and grave."

verses.devanagari: এত বলি’ পুরী-গোসাঞি গেলা নিজ-স্থানে ।\\nহরিদাস-স্থানে গেলা সব ভক্তগণে ॥১৩৭॥
verses.transliteration: eta bali' purī-gosāñi gelā nija-sthāne\\nharidāsa-sthāne gelā saba bhakta-gaṇe
verses.translation: After saying this, Paramānanda Purī Gosāñi left for his own home. Then all the devotees went to see Junior Haridāsa.

verses.devanagari: স্বরূপ-গোসাঞি কহে, “শুন, হরিদাস  ।\\nসবে তোমার হিত বাঞ্ছি, করহ বিশ্বাস ॥১৩৮॥
verses.transliteration: svarūpa-gosāñi kahe,—"śuna, haridāsa\\nsabe tomāra hita vāñchi, karaha viśvāsa
verses.translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosāñi said, "Please hear us, Haridāsa, for we all wish you well. Please believe this.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু হঠে পড়িয়াছে স্বতন্ত্র ঈশ্বর  ।\\nকভু কৃপা করিবেন যাতে দয়ালু অন্তর ॥১৩৯॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu haṭhe paḍiyāche svatantra īśvara\\nkabhu kṛpā karibena yāte dayālu antara
verses.translation: "At present Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is persisting in His mood of anger because He is the independent Supreme Personality of Godhead. At some time, however, He will surely be merciful, for at heart He is very kind.

verses.devanagari: তুমি হঠ কৈলে তাঁর হঠ সে বাড়িবে  ।\\nস্নান ভোজন কর, আপনে ক্রোধ যাবে ।।” ১৪০ ॥১৪০॥
verses.transliteration: tumi haṭha kaile tāṅra haṭha se bāḍibe\\nsnāna bhojana kara, āpane krodha yābe"
verses.translation: "The Lord is persisting, and if you also persist, His persistence will increase. It is better for you to bathe and take prasāda. In due course, His anger will automatically subside."

verses.devanagari: এত বলি তারে স্নান ভোজন করাঞা ।\\nআপন ভবন আইলা তারে আশ্বাসিয়া ॥১৪১॥
verses.transliteration: eta bali tāre snāna bhojana karāñā\\nāpana bhavana āilā tāre āśvāsiyā
verses.translation: Having said this, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī induced Haridāsa to bathe and take prasāda. After thus reassuring him, he returned home.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু যদি যান জগন্নাথ-দরশনে ।\\nদূরে রহি’ হরিদাস করেন দর্শনে ॥১৪২॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu yadi yāna jagannātha-daraśane\\ndūre rahi' haridāsa karena darśane
verses.translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to see Lord Jagannātha in the temple, Haridāsa would stay a long distance away and see Him.

verses.devanagari: মহাপ্রভু — কৃপাসিন্ধু, কে পারে বুঝিতে ?\\nপ্রিয় ভক্তে দণ্ড করেন ধর্ম বুঝাইতে ॥১৪৩॥
verses.transliteration: mahāprabhu—kṛpā-sindhu, ke pāre bujhite?\\npriya bhakte daṇḍa karena dharma bujhāite
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is the ocean of mercy. Who can understand Him? When He chastises His dear devotees, He certainly does so to reestablish the principles of religion or duty.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura says in this connection that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the ocean of mercy, chastised Junior Haridāsa, although Junior Haridāsa was His dear devotee, to establish that one in the devotional line, engaged in pure devotional service, should not be a hypocrite. For a person engaged in devotional service in the renounced order, having intimate relationships with women is certainly hypocrisy. This chastisement was given to Junior Haridāsa as an example to future
sahajiyās
who might adopt the dress of the renounced order to imitate Rūpa Gosvāmī and other bona fide
sannyāsīs
but secretly have illicit connections with women. To teach such men, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu chastised His dear devotee Haridāsa for a slight deviation from the regulative principles. Śrīmatī Mādhavīdevī was a highly elevated devotee; therefore approaching her to ask for some rice to serve Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was certainly not very offensive. Nevertheless, just to preserve the regulative principles for the future, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu enforced the hard-and-fast rule that no one in the renounced order should intimately mix with women. Had Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu not chastised Junior Haridāsa for this slight deviation, so-called devotees of the Lord would have exploited the example of Junior Haridāsa to continue their habit of illicit connections with women unrestrictedly. Indeed, they still preach that such behavior is allowed for a Vaiṣṇava. But it is strictly not allowed. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is the teacher of the entire world, and therefore He enforced this exemplary punishment to establish that illicit sexual connections are never allowed by Vaiṣṇava philosophy. This was His purpose in chastising Junior Haridāsa. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is in fact the most magnanimous incarnation of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, but He strictly prohibited illicit sex.

verses.devanagari: দেখি’ ত্রাস উপজিল সব ভক্তগণে ।\\nস্বপ্নেহ ছাড়িল সবে স্ত্রী-সম্ভাষণে ॥১৪৪॥
verses.transliteration: dekhi' trāsa upajila saba bhakta-gaṇe\\nsvapne-ha chāḍila sabe strī-sambhāṣaṇe
verses.translation: After all the devotees saw this example, a mentality of fear grew among them. Therefore they all stopped talking with women, even in dreams.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
In connection with
strī-sambhāṣaṇa,
talking with women, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura says that talking with women for the purpose of mingling with them for sense gratification, subtle or gross, is strictly prohibited. Cāṇakya Paṇḍita, the great moral instructor, says,
mātṛvat para-dāreṣu.
Thus not only a person in the renounced order or one engaged in devotional service but everyone should avoid mingling with women. One should consider another's wife his mother.

verses.devanagari: এইমতে হরিদাসের এক বৎসর গেল ।\\nতবু মহাপ্রভুর মনে প্রসাদ নহিল ॥১৪৫॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mate haridāsera eka vatsara gela\\ntabu mahāprabhura mane prasāda nahila
verses.translation: In this way a complete year passed for Junior Haridāsa, but still there was not a sign of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's mercy toward him.

verses.devanagari: রাত্রি অবশেষে প্রভুরে দণ্ডবৎ হঞা ।\\nপ্রয়াগেতে গেল কারেহ কিছু না বলিয়া ॥১৪৬॥
verses.transliteration: rātri avaśeṣe prabhure daṇḍavat hañā\\nprayāgete gela kāreha kichu nā baliyā
verses.translation: Thus at the end of one night, Junior Haridāsa, after offering Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu his respectful obeisances, departed for Prayāga without saying anything to anyone.

verses.devanagari: প্রভুপদপ্রাপ্তি লাগি’ সঙ্কল্প করিল ।\\nত্রিবেণী প্রবেশ করি’ প্রাণ ছাড়িল ॥১৪৭॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu-pada-prāpti lāgi' saṅkalpa karila\\ntriveṇī praveśa kari' prāṇa chāḍila
verses.translation: Junior Haridāsa had conclusively decided to attain shelter at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Thus he entered deep into the water at Triveṇī, the confluence of the Ganges and Yamunā at Prayāga, and in this way gave up his life.

verses.devanagari: সেইক্ষণে দিব্যদেহে প্রভুস্থানে আইলা ।\\nপ্রভুকৃপা পাঞা অন্তর্ধানেই রহিলা ॥১৪৮॥
verses.transliteration: sei-kṣaṇe divya-dehe prabhu-sthāne āilā\\nprabhu-kṛpā pāñā antardhānei rahilā
verses.translation: Immediately after committing suicide in this way, he went in his spiritual body to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and received the mercy of the Lord. However, he still remained invisible.

verses.devanagari: গন্ধর্ব-দেহে গান করেন অন্তর্ধানে ।\\nরাত্র্যে প্রভুরে শুনায় গীত, অন্যে নাহি জানে ॥১৪৯॥
verses.transliteration: gandharva-dehe gāna karena antardhāne\\nrātrye prabhure śunāya gīta, anye nāhi jāne
verses.translation: In a spiritual body resembling that of a Gandharva, Junior Haridāsa, although invisible, would sing at night for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to hear. No one but the Lord, however, knew of this.

verses.devanagari: একদিন মহাপ্রভু পুছিলা ভক্তগণে ।\\n‘হরিদাস কাঁহা? তারে আনহ এখানে’ ॥১৫০॥
verses.transliteration: eka-dina mahāprabhu puchilā bhakta-gaṇe\\n'haridāsa kāṅhā? tāre ānaha ekhāne'
verses.translation: One day Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu inquired from the devotees, "Where is Haridāsa? Now you may bring him here."

verses.devanagari: সব কহে, — “হরিদাস বর্ষপূর্ণ দিনে ।\\nরাত্রে উঠি কাঁহা গেলা, কেহ নাহি জানে ।।” ॥ ১৫১ ॥
verses.transliteration: sabe kahe,—'haridāsa varṣa-pūrṇa dine\\nrātre uṭhi kāṅhā gelā, keha nāhi jāne"
verses.translation: The devotees all replied, "One night at the end of a full year, Junior Haridāsa got up and went away. No one knows where he has gone."

verses.devanagari: শুনি’ মহাপ্রভু ঈষৎ হাসিয়া রহিলা ।\\nসব ভক্তগণ মনে বিস্ময় হইলা ॥১৫২॥
verses.transliteration: śuni' mahāprabhu īṣat hāsiyā rahilā\\nsaba bhakta-gaṇa mane vismaya ha-ilā
verses.translation: While hearing the devotees lament, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was mildly smiling. Thus all the devotees were very astonished.

verses.devanagari: একদিন জগদানন্দ, স্বরূপ, গোবিন্দ ।\\nকাশীশ্বর, শঙ্কর, দামোদর, মুকুন্দ ॥১৫৩॥\\nসমুদ্রস্নানে গেলা সবে, শুনে কথো দূরে ।\\nহরিদাস গায়েন, যেন ডাকি’ কণ্ঠস্বরে ॥১৫৪॥
verses.transliteration: samudra-snāne gelā sabe, śune katho dūre\\nharidāsa gāyena, yena ḍāki' kaṇṭha-svare
verses.translation: One day Jagadānanda, Svarūpa, Govinda, Kāśīśvara, Śaṅkara, Dāmodara and Mukunda all went to bathe in the sea. They could hear Haridāsa singing from a distant place as if calling them in his original voice.

verses.devanagari: মনুষ্য না দেখে — মধুর গীতমাত্র শুনে  ।\\nগোবিন্দাদি সবে মেলি’ কৈল অনুমানে ॥১৫৫॥
verses.transliteration: manuṣya nā dekhe—madhura gīta-mātra śune\\ngovindādi sabe meli' kaila anumāne
verses.translation: No one could see him, but they could hear him singing in a sweet voice. Therefore all the devotees, headed by Govinda, made this guess.

verses.devanagari: ‘বিষাদি খাঞা হরিদাস আত্মঘাত কৈল  ।\\nসেই পাপে জানি ‘ব্রহ্মরাক্ষস’ হৈল ॥১৫৬॥
verses.transliteration: 'viṣādi khāñā haridāsa ātma-ghāta kaila\\nsei pāpe jāni 'brahma-rākṣasa' haila
verses.translation: "Haridāsa must have committed suicide by drinking poison, and because of this sinful act, he has now become a brāhmaṇa ghost.

verses.devanagari: আকার না দেখি, মাত্র শুনি তার গান ।’\\nস্বরূপ কহেন, — “এই মিথ্যা অনুমান ॥১৫৭॥
verses.transliteration: ākāra nā dekhi, mātra śuni tāra gāna'\\nsvarūpa kahena,—"ei mithyā anumāna
verses.translation: "We cannot see his material form," they said, "but still we hear his sweet singing. Therefore he must have become a ghost." Svarūpa Dāmodara, however, protested, "This is a false guess.

verses.devanagari: আজন্ম কৃষ্ণকীর্তন, প্রভুর সেবন  ।\\nপ্রভু-কৃপাপাত্র, আর ক্ষেত্রের মরণ ॥১৫৮॥
verses.transliteration: ājanma kṛṣṇa-kīrtana, prabhura sevana\\nprabhu-kṛpā-pātra, āra kṣetrera maraṇa
verses.translation: "Junior Haridāsa chanted the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra throughout his entire life and served the Supreme Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Moreover, he is dear to the Lord and has died in a holy place.

verses.devanagari: দুর্গতি না হয় তার, সদ্গতি সে হয়  ।\\nপ্রভু-ভঙ্গী এই, পাছে জানিবা নিশ্চয় ।।” ১৫৯ ॥১৫৯॥
verses.transliteration: durgati nā haya tāra, sad-gati se haya\\nprabhu-bhaṅgī ei, pāche jānibā niścaya"
verses.translation: "Haridāsa cannot have been degraded; he must have attained liberation. This is a pastime of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. You will all understand it later."

verses.devanagari: প্রয়াগ হইতে এক বৈষ্ণব নবদ্বীপে আইল ।\\nহরিদাসের বার্তা তেঁহো সবারে কহিল ॥১৬০॥
verses.transliteration: prayāga ha-ite eka vaiṣṇava navadvīpa āila\\nharidāsera vārtā teṅho sabāre kahila
verses.translation: A devotee returned to Navadvīpa from Prayāga and told everyone the details of Junior Haridāsa's suicide.

verses.devanagari: যৈছে সংকল্প, যৈছে ত্রিবেণী প্রবেশিল ।\\nশুনি’ শ্রীবাসাদির মনে বিস্ময় হইল ॥১৬১॥
verses.transliteration: yaiche saṅkalpa, yaiche triveṇī praveśila\\nśuni, śrīvāsādira mane vismaya ha-ila
verses.translation: He explained how Junior Haridāsa had made his resolution and had thus entered the waters at the confluence of the Yamunā and Ganges. Hearing these details, Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura and the other devotees were very surprised.

verses.devanagari: বর্ষান্তরে শিবানন্দ সব ভক্ত লঞা ।\\nপ্রভুরে মিলিলা আসি’ আনন্দিত হঞা ॥১৬২॥
verses.transliteration: varṣāntare śivānanda saba bhakta lañā\\nprabhure mililā āsi' ānandita hañā
verses.translation: At the end of the year, Śivānanda Sena came to Jagannātha Purī as usual, accompanied by the other devotees, and thus in great happiness met Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: ‘হরিদাস কাঁহা?’ যদি শ্রীবাস পুছিলা ।\\n‘স্বকর্মফলভুক্ পুমান্” — প্রভু উত্তর দিলা ॥১৬৩॥
verses.transliteration: 'haridāsa kāṅhā?' yadi śrīvāsa puchilā\\n"sva-karma-phala-bhuk pumān"—prabhu uttara dilā
verses.translation: When Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura inquired from Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, "Where is Junior Haridāsa?" The Lord replied, "A person is sure to achieve the results of his fruitive activities."

verses.devanagari: তবে শ্রীবাস তার বৃত্তান্ত কহিল ।\\nযৈছে সংকল্প, যৈছে ত্রিবেণী প্রবেশিল ॥১৬৪॥
verses.transliteration: tabe śrīvāsa tāra vṛttānta kahila\\nyaiche saṅkalpa, yaiche triveṇī praveśila
verses.translation: Then Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura related the details of Haridāsa's decision and his entering the waters at the confluence of the Ganges and Yamunā.

verses.devanagari: শুনি’ প্রভু হাসি’ কহে সুপ্রসন্ন চিত্ত ।\\n‘প্রকৃতি দর্শন কৈলে এই প্রায়শ্চিত্ত’ ॥১৬৫॥
verses.transliteration: śuni' prabhu hāsi' kahe suprasanna citta\\n'prakṛti darśana kaile ei prāyaścitta'
verses.translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard these details, He smiled in a pleased mood and said, "If with sensual intentions one looks at women, this is the only process of atonement."

verses.devanagari: স্বরূপাদি মিলি’ তবে বিচার করিলা ।\\nত্রিবেণী-প্রভাবে হরিদাস প্রভুপদ পাইলা ॥১৬৬॥
verses.transliteration: svarūpādi mili' tabe vicāra karilā\\ntriveṇī-prabhāve haridāsa prabhu-pada pāilā
verses.translation: Then all the devotees, headed by Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, concluded that because Haridāsa had committed suicide at the confluence of the rivers Ganges and Yamunā, he must have ultimately attained shelter at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura remarks that after one adopts the renounced order and accepts the dress of either a
sannyāsī
or a
bābājī,
if he entertains the idea of sense gratification, especially in relationship with a woman, the only atonement is to commit suicide in the confluence of the Ganges and Yamunā. Only by such atonement can his sinful life be purified. If such a person is thus punished, it is possible for him to attain the shelter of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Without such punishment, however, the shelter of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is very difficult to regain.

verses.devanagari: এইমত লীলা করে শচীর নন্দন ।\\nযাহা শুনি’ ভক্তগণের যুড়ায় কর্ণ-মন ॥১৬৭॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata līlā kare śacīra nandana\\nyāhā śuni' bhakta-gaṇera yuḍāya karṇa-mana
verses.translation: In this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the son of mother Śacī, performs His pastimes, which greatly satisfy the ears and minds of pure devotees who hear about them.

verses.devanagari: আপন কারুণ্য, লোকে বৈরাগ্য-শিক্ষণ ।\\nস্বভক্তের গাঢ়-অনুরাগ-প্রকটীকরণ ॥১৬৮॥
verses.transliteration: āpana kāruṇya, loke vairāgya-śikṣaṇa\\nsva-bhaktera gāḍha-anurāga-prakaṭī-karaṇa
verses.translation: This incident manifests the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, His teaching that a sannyāsī should remain in the renounced order, and the deep attachment to Him felt by His faithful devotees.

verses.devanagari: তীর্থের মহিমা, নিজ ভক্তে আত্মসাৎ ।\\nএক লীলায় করেন প্রভু কার্য পাঁচ-সাত ॥১৬৯॥
verses.transliteration: tīrthera mahimā, nija bhakte ātmasāt\\neka līlāya karena prabhu kārya pāṅca-sāta
verses.translation: It also demonstrates the glories of holy places and shows how the Lord accepts His faithful devotee. Thus the Lord fulfilled five or seven purposes by performing one pastime.

verses.devanagari: মধুর চৈতন্যলীলা — সমুদ্র-গম্ভীর ।\\nলোকে নাহি বুঝে, বুঝে যেই ‘ভক্ত’ ‘ধীর’ ॥১৭০॥
verses.transliteration: madhura caitanya-līlā—samudra-gambhīra\\nloke nāhi bujhe, bujhe yei 'bhakta' 'dhīra'
verses.translation: The pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are like nectar, and they are deep like the ocean. People in general cannot understand them, but a sober devotee can.

verses.devanagari: বিশ্বাস করিয়া শুন চৈতন্যচরিত ।\\nতর্ক না করিহ, তর্কে হবে বিপরীত ॥১৭১॥
verses.transliteration: viśvāsa kariyā śuna caitanya-carita\\ntarka nā kariha, tarke habe viparīta
verses.translation: Please hear the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu with faith and confidence. Do not argue, for arguments will produce a contrary result.

verses.devanagari: শ্রীরূপ-রঘুনাথ-পদে যার আশ ।\\nচৈতন্যচরিতামৃত কহে কৃষ্ণদাস ॥১৭২॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa\\ncaitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa
verses.translation: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Instructions from this Chapter
Summarizing this chapter, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura says that one should derive from it the following lessons. (1) Although Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is an incarnation of mercy, He nevertheless gave up the company of one of His personal associates, namely Junior Haridāsa, for if He had not done so, pseudo-devotees would have taken advantage of Junior Haridāsa's fault by using it as an excuse to live as devotees and at the same time have illicit sexual connections. Such activities would have demoralized the cult of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and as a result, devotees would surely have gone to a hellish life in the name of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. (2) By chastising Junior Haridāsa, the Lord set the standard for
ācāryas,
or the heads of institutions propagating the Caitanya cult, and for all actual devotees. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu wanted to maintain the highest standard. (3) Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu instructed that a pure devotee should be simple and free from sinful activities, for thus one can be His bona fide servant. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu taught His followers how to observe the renounced order strictly. (4) Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu wanted to prove that His devotees are exalted and that their character is ideal. He kindly accepts His faithful devotees and teaches them how much tribulation and disturbance can be produced by even a slight deviation from the strict principles of devotional life. (5) By chastising Junior Haridāsa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu exhibited His mercy toward him, thus showing how elevated was junior Haridāsa's devotion for Him. Because of this transcendental relationship, the Lord corrected even a slight offense committed by His pure devotee. Therefore one who wants to be a pure devotee of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu should give up all material sense gratification; otherwise, the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are very difficult to attain. (6) If one dies in such a celebrated holy place as Prayāga, Mathurā or Vṛndāvana, one can be relieved of the reactions to sinful life and then attain the shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. (7) Although a pure or faithful devotee may fall down, he nevertheless ultimately gets the chance to go back home, back to Godhead, by the mercy of the Lord.
Thus end the Bhaktivedanta purports to Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā,  Second Chapter, describing the chastisement of Junior Haridāsa.

sections.title: Chapter 3: The Glories of Śrīla Haridāsa Ṭhākura

verses.devanagari: বন্দেঽহং শ্রীগুরোঃ শ্রীযুতপদকমলং শ্রীগুরূন্ বৈষ্ণবাংশ্চ\\nশ্রীরূপং সাগ্রজাতং সহগণরঘুনাথান্বিতং তং সজীবম্ ।\\nসাদ্বৈতং সাবধূতং পরিজনসহিতং কৃষ্ণচৈতন্যদেবং\\nশ্রীরাধাকৃষ্ণপাদান্ সহগণললিতা-শ্রীবিশাখান্বিতাংশ্চ ॥১॥
verses.transliteration: vande 'haṁ śrī-guroḥ śrī-yuta-pada-kamalaṁ śrī-gurūn vaiṣṇavāṁś ca\\nśrī-rūpaṁ sāgrajātaṁ saha-gaṇa-raghunāthānvitaṁ taṁ sa-jīvam\\nsādvaitaṁ sāvadhūtaṁ parijana-sahitaṁ kṛṣṇa-caitanya-devaṁ\\nśrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇa-pādān saha-gaṇa-lalitā-śrī-viśākhānvitāṁś ca
verses.translation: I offer my respectful obeisances unto the lotus feet of my spiritual master and of all the other preceptors on the path of devotional service, unto all the Vaiṣṇavas and unto the six Gosvāmīs, including Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī, Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī, Jīva Gosvāmī and their associates. I offer my respectful obeisances unto Śrī Advaita Ācārya Prabhu, Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, as well as all His devotees, headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura. I then offer my respectful obeisances unto the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa and Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and all the gopīs, headed by Lalitā and Viśākhā.

verses.devanagari: জয় জয় গৌরচন্দ্র জয় নিত্যানন্দ ।\\nজয়াদ্বৈতচন্দ্র জয় গৌরভক্তবৃন্দ ॥২॥
verses.transliteration: jaya jaya gauracandra jaya nityānanda\\njayādvaita-candra jaya gaura-bhakta-vṛnda
verses.translation: All glories to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Nityānanda Prabhu! All glories to Advaita Ācārya! And all glories to all the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu!

verses.devanagari: পুরুষোত্তমে এক উড়িয়া-ব্রাহ্মণকুমার ।\\nপিতৃশূন্য, মহাসুন্দর, মৃদুব্যবহার ॥৩॥
verses.transliteration: puruṣottame eka uḍiyā-brāhmaṇa-kumāra\\npitṛ-śūnya, mahā-sundara, mṛdu-vyavahāra
verses.translation: In Jagannātha Purī there was a young boy who had been born of an Orissa brāhmaṇa but had later lost his father. The boy's features were very beautiful, and his behavior was extremely gentle.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু-স্থানে নিত্য আইসে, করে নমস্কার ।\\nপ্রভু-সনে বাত্ কহে প্রভু-‘প্রাণ’ তার ॥৪॥\\nপ্রভুতে তাহার প্রীতি, প্রভু দয়া করে ।\\nদামোদর তার প্রীতি সহিতে না পারে ॥৫॥
verses.transliteration: prabhute tāhāra prīti, prabhu dayā kare\\ndāmodara tāra prīti sahite nā pāre
verses.translation: The boy came dally to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and offered Him respectful obeisances. He was free to talk with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu because the Lord was his life and soul, but the boy's intimacy with the Lord and the Lord's mercy toward him were intolerable to Dāmodara Paṇḍita.

verses.devanagari: বার বার নিষেধ করে ব্রাহ্মণকুমারে ।\\nপ্রভুরে না দেখিলে সেই রহিতে না পারে ॥৬॥
verses.transliteration: bāra bāra niṣedha kare brāhmaṇa-kumāre\\nprabhure nā dekhile sei rahite nā pāre
verses.translation: Dāmodara Paṇḍita again and again forbade the son of the brāhmaṇa to visit the Lord, but the boy could not bear staying home and not seeing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: নিত্য আইসে, প্রভু তারে করে মহাপ্রীত ।\\nযাঁহা প্রীতি তাঁহা আইসে, — বালকের রীত ॥৭॥
verses.transliteration: nitya āise, prabhu tāre kare mahā-prīta\\nyāṅhā prīti tāṅhā āise,—bālakera rīta
verses.translation: The boy came every day to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who treated him with great affection. It is the nature of ay boy to go see a ma who loves him.

verses.devanagari: তাহা দেখি’ দামোদর দুঃখ পায় মনে ।\\nবলিতে না পারে, বালক নিষেধ না মানে ॥৮॥
verses.transliteration: tāhā dekhi' dāmodara duḥkha pāya mane\\nbalite nā pāre, bālaka niṣedha nā māne
verses.translation: This was intolerable for Dāmodara Paṇḍita. He became greatly unhappy, but there was nothing he could say, for the boy would ignore his restrictions.

verses.devanagari: আর দিন সেই বালক প্রভুস্থানে আইলা ।\\nগোসাঞি তারে প্রীতি করি’ বার্তা পুছিলা ॥৯॥
verses.transliteration: āra dina sei bālaka prabhu-sthāne āilā\\ngosāñi tāre prīti kari' vārtā puchilā
verses.translation: One day when the boy came to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Lord very affectionately inquired from him about all kinds of news.

verses.devanagari: কতক্ষণে সে বালক উঠি’ যবে গেলা ।\\nসহিতে না পারে, দামোদর কহিতে লাগিলা ॥১০॥
verses.transliteration: kata-kṣaṇe se bālaka uṭhi' yabe gelā\\nsahite nā pāre, dāmodara kahite lāgilā
verses.translation: After some time, when the boy stood up and left, the intolerant Dāmodara Paṇḍita began to speak.

verses.devanagari: অন্যোপদেশে পণ্ডিত — কহে গোসাঞির ঠাঞি ।\\n‘গোসাঞি’ ‘গোসাঞি’ এবে জানিমু ‘গোসাঞি’ ॥১১॥
verses.transliteration: anyopadeśe paṇḍita—kahe gosāñira ṭhāñi\\n'gosāñi"gosāñi' ebe jānimu 'gosāñi'
verses.translation: Dāmodara Paṇḍita impudently said to the Lord, "Everyone says that You are a great teacher because of Your instructions to others, but now we shall find out what kind of teacher You are.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Dāmodara Paṇḍita was a great devotee of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Sometimes, however, a person in such a position becomes impudent, being influenced by the external energy and material considerations. Thus a devotee mistakenly dares to criticize the activities of the spiritual master or the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Despite the logic that "Caesar's wife must be above suspicion," a devotee should not be disturbed by the activities of his spiritual master and should not try to criticize him. A devotee should be fixed in the conclusion that the spiritual master cannot be subject to criticism and should never be considered equal to a common man. Even if there appears to be some discrepancy according to an imperfect devotee's estimation, the devotee should be fixed in the conviction that even if his spiritual master goes to a liquor shop, he is not a drunkard; rather, he must have some purpose in going there. it is said in a Bengali poem:
yadyapi nityānanda surā-bāḍi yāya
tathāpio haya nityānanda-rāya
"Even if I see that Lord Nityānanda has entered a liquor shop, I shall not be diverted from my conclusion that Nityānanda Rāya is the Supreme Personality of Godhead."

verses.devanagari: এবে গোসাঞির গুণ-যশ সব লোকে গাইবে ।\\nতবে গোসাঞির প্রতিষ্ঠা পুরুষোত্তমে হইবে ॥১২॥
verses.transliteration: ebe gosāñira guṇa-yaśa saba loke gāibe\\ntabe gosāñira pratiṣṭhā puruṣottame ha-ibe
verses.translation: "You are known as Gosāñi [teacher or ācārya], but now talk about Your attributes and reputation will spread throughout the city of Puruṣottama. How Your position will be impaired!"

verses.devanagari: শুনি’ প্রভু কহে, — ‘ক্যা কহ, দামোদর ?’ দামোদর কহে, — “তুমি স্বতন্ত্র ‘ঈশ্বর’ ॥১৩॥
verses.transliteration: śuni' prabhu kahe,—'kyā kaha, dāmodara?'\\ndāmodara kahe,—tumi svatantra 'īśvara'
verses.translation: Although Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu knew that Dāmodara Paṇḍita was a pure and simple devotee, upon hearing this impudent talk the Lord said, "My dear Dāmodara, what nonsense are you speaking?" Dāmodara Paṇḍita replied, "You are the independent Personality of Godhead, beyond all criticism.

verses.devanagari: স্বচ্ছন্দে আচার কর, কে পারে বলিতে ? মুখর জগতের মুখ পার আচ্ছাদিতে ? ১৪ ॥১৪॥
verses.transliteration: svacchande ācāra kara, ke pāre balite?\\nmukhara jagatera mukha pāra ācchādite?
verses.translation: "My dear Lord, You can act as You please. No one can say anything to restrict You. Nevertheless, the entire world is impudent. People can say anything. How can You stop them?

verses.devanagari: পণ্ডিত হঞা মনে কেনে বিচার না কর ?\\nরাণ্ডী ব্রাহ্মণীর বালকে প্রীতি কেনে কর ? ॥ ১৫ ॥
verses.transliteration: paṇḍita hañā mane kene vicāra nā kara?\\nrāṇḍī brāhmaṇīra bālake prīti kene kara?
verses.translation: "Dear Lord, You are a learned teacher. Why then don't You consider that this boy is the son of a widowed brāhmaṇī? Why are You so affectionate to him?

verses.devanagari: যদ্যপি ব্রাহ্মণী সেই তপস্বিনী সতী ।\\nতথাপি তাহার দোষ — সুন্দরী যুবতী ॥১৬॥
verses.transliteration: yadyapi brāhmaṇī sei tapasvinī satī\\ntathāpi tāhāra doṣa—sundarī yuvatī
verses.translation: "Although the boy's mother is completely austere and chaste, she has one natural fault-she is a very beautiful young girl.

verses.devanagari: তুমিহ — পরম যুবা, পরম সুন্দর ।\\nলোকের কাণাকাণি-বাতে দেহ অবসর ।।” ॥ ১৭ ॥
verses.transliteration: tumi-ha—parama yuvā, parama sundara\\nlokera kāṇākāṇi-vāte deha avasara"
verses.translation: "And You, my dear Lord, are a handsome, attractive young man. Therefore certainly people will whisper about You. Why should You give them such a opportunity?"
verses.purport: PURPORT\nAs a simple and staunch devotee of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Dāmodara Paṇḍita could not tolerate criticism of the Lord, but unfortunately he himself was criticizing Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in his own way. The Lord could understand that it was because of Dāmodara Paṇḍita's simplicity that he impudently dared criticize Him. Nevertheless, such behavior by a devotee is not very good.

verses.devanagari: এত বলি’ দামোদর মৌন হইলা  ।\\nঅন্তরে সন্তোষ প্রভু হাসি’ বিচারিলা ॥১৮॥
verses.transliteration: eta bali' dāmodara mauna ha-ilā\\nantare santoṣa prabhu hāsi' vicārilā
verses.translation: Having said this, Dāmodara Paṇḍita became silent. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu smiled, pleased within Himself, and considered the impudence of Dāmodara Paṇḍita.

verses.devanagari: “ইহারে কহিয়ে শুদ্ধপ্রেমের তরঙ্গ  ।\\nদামোদর-সম মোর নাহি ‘অন্তরঙ্গ’ ।।” ১৯ ॥১৯॥
verses.transliteration: "ihāre kahiye śuddha-premera taraṅga\\ndāmodara-sama mora nāhi 'antaraṅga' "
verses.translation: "This impudence is also a sign of pure love for Me. I have no other intimate friend like Dāmodara Paṇḍita."

verses.devanagari: এতেক বিচারি’ প্রভু মধ্যাহ্নে চলিলা  ।\\nআর দিনে দামোদরে নিভৃতে বোলাইলা ॥২০॥
verses.transliteration: eteka vicāri' prabhu madhyāhne calilā\\nāra dine dāmodare nibhṛte bolāilā
verses.translation: Thinking in this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to perform His noon duties. The next day, He called Dāmodara Paṇḍita to a solitary place.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহে, — “দামোদর, চলহ নদীয়া  ।\\nমাতার সমীপে তুমি রহ তাঁহা যাঞা ॥২১॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahe,—"dāmodara, calaha nadīyā\\nmātāra samīpe tumi raha tāṅhā yāñā
verses.translation: The Lord said, "My dear friend Dāmodara, you had better go to Nadia and stay with My mother.

verses.devanagari: তোমা বিনা তাঁহার রক্ষক নাহি দেখি আন ।\\nআমাকেহ যাতে তুমি কৈলা সাবধান ॥২২॥
verses.transliteration: tomā vinā tāṅhāra rakṣaka nāhi dekhi āna\\nāmāke-ha yāte tumi kailā sāvadhāna
verses.translation: "I see no one but you to protect her, for you are so careful that you can caution even Me.

verses.devanagari: তোমা সম ‘নিরপেক্ষ’ নাহি মোর গণে ।\\n‘নিরপেক্ষ’ নহিলে ‘ধর্ম’ না যায় রক্ষণে ॥২৩॥
verses.transliteration: tomā sama 'nirapekṣa' nāhi mora gaṇe\\n'nirapekṣa' nahile 'dharma' nā yāya rakṣaṇe
verses.translation: "You are the most neutral among My associates. This is very good, for without being neutral one cannot protect religious principles.

verses.devanagari: আমা হৈতে যে না হয়, সে তোমা হৈতে হয় ।\\nআমারে করিলা দণ্ড, আন কেবা হয় ॥২৪॥
verses.transliteration: āmā haite ye nā haya, se tomā haite haya\\nāmāre karilā daṇḍa, āna kebā haya
verses.translation: "You can do whatever I cannot. Indeed, you can chastise even Me, not to speak of others.

verses.devanagari: মাতার গৃহে রহ যাই মাতার চরণে ।\\nতোমার আগে নহিবে কারো স্বচ্ছন্দাচরণে ॥২৫॥
verses.transliteration: mātāra gṛhe raha yāi mātāra caraṇe\\ntomāra āge nahibe kāro svacchandācaraṇe
verses.translation: "It is best for you to go to the shelter of My mother's lotus feet, for no one will be able to behave independently in front of you.

verses.devanagari: মধ্যে মধ্যে আসিবা কভু আমার দরশনে ।\\nশীঘ্র করি’ পুনঃ তাহাঁ করহ গমনে ॥২৬॥
verses.transliteration: madhye madhye āsibā kabhu āmāra daraśane\\nśīghra kari' punaḥ tāhāṅ karaha gamane
verses.translation: "At intervals you may come see Me here and then soon again go there.

verses.devanagari: মাতারে কহিহ মোর কোটী নমস্কারে ।\\nমোর সুখ-কথা কহি’ সুখ দিহ’ তাঁরে ॥২৭॥
verses.transliteration: mātāre kahiha mora koṭī namaskāre\\nmora sukha-kathā kahi' sukha diha' tāṅre
verses.translation: "Offer My mother millions of My obeisances. Please speak to her about My happiness here and thus give her happiness.

verses.devanagari: ‘নিরন্তর নিজ-কথা তোমারে শুনাইতে ।\\nএই লাগি’ প্রভু মোরে পাঠাইলা ইহাঁতে’ ॥২৮॥
verses.transliteration: 'nirantara nija-kathā tomāre śunāite\\nei lāgi' prabhu more pāṭhāilā ihāṅte'
verses.translation: "Tell her that I sent you to inform her of My personal activities so that she may share in My happiness.

verses.devanagari: এত কহি’ মাতার মনে সন্তোষ জন্মাইহ  ।\\nআর গুহ্যকথা তাঁরে স্মরণ করাইহ ॥২৯॥
verses.transliteration: eta kahi' mātāra mane santoṣa janmāiha\\nāra guhya-kathā tāṅre smaraṇa karāiha
verses.translation: "Speaking in this way, satisfy the mind of mother Śacī. Also, remind her of one most confidential incident with this message from Me.

verses.devanagari: ‘বারে বারে আসি’ আমি তোমার ভবনে  ।\\nমিষ্টান্ন ব্যঞ্জন সব করিয়ে ভোজনে ॥৩০॥
verses.transliteration: 'bāre bāre āsi' āmi tomāra bhavane\\nmiṣṭānna vyañjana saba kariye bhojane
verses.translation: "I come to your home again and again to eat all the sweetmeats and vegetables you offer.

verses.devanagari: ভোজন করিয়ে আমি, তুমি তাহা জান ।\\nবাহ্য বিরহে তাহা স্বপ্ন করি মান ॥৩১॥
verses.transliteration: bhojana kariye āmi, tumi tāhā jāna\\nbāhya virahe tāhā svapna kari māna
verses.translation: “ 'You know that I come and eat the offerings, but because of external separation, you consider this a dream.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Because mother Śacī was feeling separation from Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, she thought she was dreaming that her son had come to her. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, however, wanted to inform her that actually it was not a dream. He actually came there and ate whatever His mother offered Him. Such are the dealings of advanced devotees with the Supreme personality of Godhead. As stated in the
Brahma-saṁhitā:
premāñjana-cchurita-bhakti-vilocanena
santaḥ sadaiva hṛdayeṣu vilokayanti
yaṁ śyāmasundaram acintya-guṇa-svarūpaṁ
govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi
"I worship the primeval Lord, Govinda, who is always seen by the devotee whose eyes are anointed with the pulp of love. He is seen in His eternal form of Śyāmasundara, situated within the heart of the devotee." (
Brahma-saṁhitā
5.38) pure devotees realize dealings with the Lord on the transcendental plane, but because the devotees are still in the material world, they think that these are dreams. The Lord, however, talks with the advanced devotee, and the advanced devotee also sees Him. It is all factual; it is not a dream.

verses.devanagari: এই-মাঘ-সংক্রান্ত্যে তুমি রন্ধন করিলা  ।\\nনানা ব্যঞ্জন, ক্ষীর, পিঠা, পায়স রান্ধিলা ॥৩২॥
verses.transliteration: ei māgha-saṅkrāntye tumi randhana karilā\\nnānā vyañjana, kṣīra, piṭhā, pāyasa rāndhilā
verses.translation: "During the last Māgha-saṅkrānti festival, you cooked varieties of vegetables, condensed milk, cakes and sweet rice for Me.

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণে ভোগ লাগাঞা যবে কৈলা ধ্যান  ।\\nআমার স্ফূর্তি হৈল, অশ্রু ভরিল নয়ন ॥৩৩॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇe bhoga lāgāñā yabe kailā dhyāna\\nāmāra sphūrti haila, aśru bharila nayana
verses.translation: "You offered the food to Lord Kṛṣṇa, and while you were in meditation I suddenly appeared, and your eyes filled with tears.

verses.devanagari: আস্তে-ব্যস্তে আমি গিয়া সকলি খাইল ।\\nআমি খাই, — দেখি’ তোমার সুখ উপজিল ॥৩৪॥
verses.transliteration: āste-vyaste āmi giyā sakali khāila\\nāmi khāi,—dekhi' tomāra sukha upajila
verses.translation: "I went there in great haste and ate everything. When you saw Me eating, you felt great happiness.

verses.devanagari: ক্ষণেকে অশ্রু মুছিয়া শূন্য দেখি’ পাত ।\\nস্বপন দেখিলুঁ, ‘যেন নিমাঞি খাইল ভাত’ ॥৩৫॥
verses.transliteration: kṣaṇeke aśru muchiyā śūnya dekhi' pāta\\nsvapana dekhiluṅ,'yena nimāñi khāila bhāta'
verses.translation: "In a moment, after you had wiped your eyes, you saw that the plate you had offered Me was empty. Then you thought, "I dreamt as if Nimāi were eating everything."

verses.devanagari: বাহ্য-বিরহ-দশায় পুনঃ ভ্রান্তি হৈল ।\\n‘ভোগ না লাগাইলুঁ’, — এই জ্ঞান হৈল ॥৩৬॥
verses.transliteration: bāhya-viraha-daśāya punaḥ bhrānti haila\\n'bhoga nā lāgāiluṅ',—ei jñāna haila
verses.translation: "In the condition of external separation, you were again under illusion, thinking that you had not offered the food to Lord Viṣṇu.

verses.devanagari: পাকপাত্রে দেখিলা সব অন্ন আছে ভরি’ ।\\nপুনঃ ভোগ লাগাইলা স্থান-সংস্কার করি’ ॥৩৭॥
verses.transliteration: pāka-pātre dekhilā saba anna āche bhari'\\npunaḥ bhoga lāgāilā sthāna-saṁskāra kari'
verses.translation: "Then you went to see the cooking pots and found that every pot was filled with food. Therefore you again offered the food, after cleansing the place for the offering.

verses.devanagari: এইমত বার বার করিয়ে ভোজন  ।\\nতোমার শুদ্ধপ্রেমে মোরে করে আকর্ষণ ॥৩৮॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata bāra bāra kariye bhojana\\ntomāra śuddha-preme more kare ākarṣaṇa
verses.translation: "Thus I again and again eat everything you offer Me, for I am attracted by your pure love.

verses.devanagari: তোমার আজ্ঞাতে আমি আছি নীলাচলে  ।\\nনিকটে লঞা যাও আমা তোমার প্রেমবলে’ ॥৩৯॥
verses.transliteration: tomāra ājñāte āmi āchi nīlācale\\nnikaṭe lañā yāo āmā tomāra prema-bale'
verses.translation: "Only by your order am I living in Nīlācala [Jagannātha Purī]. Nevertheless, you still pull Me near you because of your great love for Me.' "

verses.devanagari: এইমত বার বার করাইহ স্মরণ ।\\nমোর নাম লঞা তাঁর বন্দিহ চরণ ।।” ॥ ৪০ ॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata bāra bāra karāiha smaraṇa\\nmora nāma lañā tāṅra vandiha caraṇa"
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu told Dāmodara Paṇḍita, "Remind mother Śacī in this way again and again and worship her lotus feet in My name."

verses.devanagari: এত কহি’ জগন্নাথের প্রসাদ আনাইল ।\\nমাতাকে বৈষ্ণবে দিতে পৃথক্ পৃথক্ দিল ॥৪১॥
verses.transliteration: eta kahi' jagannāthera prasāda ānāila\\nmātāke vaiṣṇave dite pṛthak pṛthak dila
verses.translation: After saying this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ordered that varieties of prasāda offered to Lord Jagannātha be brought. The Lord then gave him the prasāda, separately packed, to offer to various Vaiṣṇavas and His mother.

verses.devanagari: তবে দামোদর চলি’ নদীয়া আইলা ।\\nমাতারে মিলিয়া তাঁর চরণে রহিলা ॥৪২॥
verses.transliteration: tabe dāmodara cali' nadīyā āilā\\nmātāre miliyā tāṅra caraṇe rahilā
verses.translation: In this way Dāmodara Paṇḍita went to Nadia [Navadvīpa]. After meeting mother Śacī, he stayed under the care of her lotus feet.

verses.devanagari: আচার্যাদি বৈষ্ণবেরে মহাপ্রসাদ দিলা ।\\nপ্রভুর যৈছে আজ্ঞা, পণ্ডিত তাহা আচরিলা ॥৪৩॥
verses.transliteration: ācāryādi vaiṣṇavere mahā-prasāda dilā\\nprabhura yaiche ājñā, paṇḍita tāhā ācarilā
verses.translation: He delivered all the prasāda to such great Vaiṣṇavas as Advaita Ācārya. Thus he stayed there and behaved according to the order of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: দামোদর আগে স্বাতন্ত্র্য না হয় কাহার ।\\nতার ভয়ে সবে করে সঙ্কোচ ব্যবহার ॥৪৪॥
verses.transliteration: dāmodara āge svātantrya nā haya kāhāra\\ntāra bhaye sabe kare saṅkoca vyavahāra
verses.translation: Everyone knew that Dāmodara Paṇḍita was strict in practical dealings. Therefore everyone was afraid of him and dared not do anything independent.

verses.devanagari: প্রভুগণে যাঁর দেখে অল্পমর্যাদা-লঙ্ঘন ।\\nবাক্যদণ্ড করি’ করে মর্যাদা স্থাপন ॥৪৫॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu-gaṇe yāṅra dekhe alpa-maryādā-laṅghana\\nvākya-daṇḍa kari' kare maryādā sthāpana
verses.translation: Dāmodara Paṇḍita would verbally chastise every devotee of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu whom he found deviating even slightly from proper behavior. Thus he established the standard etiquette.

verses.devanagari: এইত কহিল দামোদরের বাক্যদণ্ড ।\\nযাহার শ্রবণে ভাগে ‘অজ্ঞান পাষণ্ড’ ॥৪৬॥
verses.transliteration: ei-ta kahila dāmodarera vākya-daṇḍa\\nyāhāra śravaṇe bhāge 'ajñāna pāṣaṇḍa'
verses.translation: In this way I have described Dāmodara Paṇḍita's verbal chastisements. As one hears about this, atheistic principles and ignorance depart.

verses.devanagari: চৈতন্যের লীলা — গম্ভীর, কোটিসমুদ্র হৈতে ।\\nকি লাগি’ কি করে, কেহ না পারে বুঝিতে ॥৪৭॥
verses.transliteration: caitanyera līlā—gambhīra, koṭi-samudra haite\\nki lāgi' ki kare, keha nā pāre bujhite
verses.translation: The pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are deeper than millions of seas and oceans. Therefore no one can understand what He does nor why He does it.

verses.devanagari: অতএব গূঢ় অর্থ কিছুই না জানি ।\\nবাহ্য অর্থ করিবারে করি টানাটানি ॥৪৮॥
verses.transliteration: ataeva gūḍha artha kichui nā jāni\\nbāhya artha karibāre kari ṭānāṭāni
verses.translation: I do not know the deep meaning of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's activities. As far as possible I shall try to explain them externally.

verses.devanagari: একদিন প্রভু হরিদাসেরে মিলিলা  ।\\nতাঁহা লঞা গোষ্ঠী করি’ তাঁহারে পুছিলা ॥৪৯॥
verses.transliteration: eka-dina prabhu haridāsere mililā\\ntāṅhā lañā goṣṭhī kari' tāṅhāre puchilā
verses.translation: One day Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu met Haridāsa Ṭhākura as usual, and in the course of discussion He inquired as follows.

verses.devanagari: “হরিদাস, কলিকালে যবন অপার  ।\\nগো-ব্রাহ্মণে হিংসা করে মহা দুরাচার ॥৫০॥
verses.transliteration: "haridāsa, kali-kāle yavana apāra\\ngo-brāhmaṇe hiṁsā kare mahā durācāra
verses.translation: "My dear Ṭhākura Haridāsa, in this age of Kali most people are bereft of Vedic culture, and therefore they are called yavanas. They are concerned only with killing cows and brahminical culture. In this way they all engage in sinful acts.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
From this statement by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu we can clearly understand that the word
yavana
does not refer only to a particular class of men. Anyone who is against the behavior of the Vedic principles is called a
yavana.
Such a
yavana
may be in India or outside of India. As described here, the symptom of
yavanas
is that they are violent killers of cows and brahminical culture. We offer our prayers to the Lord by saying,
namo brahmaṇya-devāya go-brāhmaṇa-hitāya ca.
The Lord is the maintainer of brahminical culture. His first concern is to see to the benefit of cows and
brāhmaṇas.
As soon as human civilization turns against brahminical culture and allows unrestricted killing of cows, we should understand that men are no longer under the control of the Vedic culture but are all
yavanas
and
mlecchas.
It is said that the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement will be prominent within the next ten thousand years, but after that people will all become
mlecchas
and
yavanas.
Thus at the end of the
yuga,
Kṛṣṇa will appear as the Kalki
avatāra
and kill them without consideration.

verses.devanagari: ইহা-সবার কোন্ মতে হইবে নিস্তার ?\\nতাহার হেতু না দেখিয়ে, — এ দুঃখ অপার ।।” ॥ ৫১ ॥
verses.transliteration: ihā-sabāra kon mate ha-ibe nistāra?\\ntāhāra hetu nā dekhiye,—e duḥkha apāra"
verses.translation: "How will these yavanas be delivered? To My great unhappiness, I do not see any way."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse reveals the significance of Lord Śrī Caitanya's appearance as
patita-pāvana,
the deliverer of all the fallen souls. Śrīla Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura sings,
patita-pāvana-hetu tava avatāra:
"O my Lord, You have appeared just to deliver all the fallen souls."
mo-sama patita prabhu nā pāibe āra:
"And among all the fallen souls, I am the lowest." How Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu was always thinking about the deliverance of the fallen souls is shown by the statement
e duḥkha apāra
("It is My great unhappiness"). This statement indicates that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who is the Supreme personality of Godhead Kṛṣṇa Himself, is always very unhappy to see the fallen souls in the material world. Therefore He Himself comes as He is, or He comes as a devotee in the form of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, to deliver love of Kṛṣṇa directly to the fallen souls.
Namo mahā-vadānyāya kṛṣṇa-prema-pradāya te.
Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is so merciful that He not only gives knowledge of Kṛṣṇa but by His practical activities teaches everyone how to love Kṛṣṇa (
kṛṣṇa-prema-pradāya te).
Those who are following in the footsteps of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu should take the Lord's mission most seriously. In this age of Kali, people are gradually becoming less than animals. Nevertheless, although they are eating the flesh of cows and are envious of brahminical culture, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is considering how to deliver them from this horrible condition of life. Thus He asks all Indians to take up His mission.
bhārata-bhūmite haila manuṣya-janma yāra
janma sārthaka kari' kara para-upakāra
"One who has taken his birth as a human being in the land of India [Bhārata-varṣa] should make his life successful and work for the benefit of all other people." (Cc. Ādi-līlā 9.41) it is therefore the duty of every advanced and cultured Indian to take this cause very seriously. All Indians should help the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement in its progress, to the best of their ability. Then they will be considered real followers of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Unfortunately, even some so-called Vaiṣṇavas enviously refuse to cooperate with this movement but instead condemn it in so many ways. We are very sorry to say that these people try to find fault with us, being unnecessarily envious of our activities, although we are trying to the best of our ability to introduce the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement directly into the countries of the
yavanas
and
mlecchas.
Such
yavanas
and
mlecchas
are coming to us and becoming purified Vaiṣṇavas who follow in the footsteps of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. One who identifies himself as a follower of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu should feel like Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who said,
ihā-sabāra kon mate ha-ibe nistāra:
"How will all these
yavanas
be delivered?" Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was always anxious to deliver the fallen souls because their fallen condition gave Him great unhappiness. That is the platform on which one can propagate the mission of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: হরিদাস কহে, — “প্রভু, চিন্তা না করিহ ।\\nযবনের সংসার দেখি’ দুঃখ না ভাবিহ ॥৫২॥
verses.transliteration: haridāsa kahe,—"prabhu, cintā nā kariha\\nyavanera saṁsāra dekhi' duḥkha nā bhāviha
verses.translation: Haridāsa Ṭhākura replied, "My dear Lord, do not be in anxiety. Do not be unhappy to see the condition of the yavanas in material existence.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThese words of Haridāsa Ṭhākura are just befitting a devotee who has dedicated his life and soul to the service of the Lord. When the Lord is unhappy because of the condition of the fallen souls, the devotee consoles Him, saying, "My dear Lord, do not be in anxiety." This is service. Everyone should adopt the cause of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to try to relieve Him from the anxiety He feels. This is actually service to the Lord. One who tries to relieve Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's anxiety for the fallen souls is certainly a most dear and confidential devotee of the Lord. To blaspheme such a devotee who is trying his best to spread the cult of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is the greatest offense. One who does so is simply awaiting punishment for his envy.

verses.devanagari: যবনসকলের ‘মুক্তি’ হবে অনায়াসে ।\\n‘হা রাম, হা রাম’ বলি’ কহে নামাভাসে ॥৫৩॥
verses.transliteration: yavana-sakalera 'mukti' habe anāyāse\\n'hā rāma, hā rāma' bali' kahe nāmābhāse
verses.translation: "Because the yavanas are accustomed to saying, 'hā rāma, hā rāma' [O Lord Rāmacandra], they will very easily be delivered by this nāmābhāsa.

verses.devanagari: মহাপ্রেমে ভক্ত কহে, — ‘হা রাম, হা রাম’ ।\\nযবনের ভাগ্য দেখ, লয় সেই নাম ॥৫৪॥
verses.transliteration: mahā-preme bhakta kahe,—'hā rāma, hā rāma'\\nyavanera bhāgya dekha, laya sei nāma
verses.translation: "A devotee in advanced ecstatic love exclaims, 'O my Lord Rāmacandra! O my Lord Rāmacandra!' But the yavanas also chant, 'hā rāma, hā rāma!' Just see their good fortune!"
verses.purport:
PURPORT
If a child touches fire, the fire will burn him, and if an elderly man touches fire, it will burn him also. Haridāsa Ṭhākura says that a great devotee of the Lord exclaims,
"hā rāma, hā rāma,
" but although
yavanas
do not know the transcendental meaning of
"hā rāma, hā rāma,
" they say those words in the course of their ordinary life. For the
yavanas
the words
"hā rāma
" mean "abominable," whereas the devotee exclaims the words
"hā rāma
" in ecstatic love. Nevertheless, because the words
"hā rāma
" are the spiritual
summum bonum,
the fact is the same, whether they are uttered by
yavanas
or by great devotees, just as fire is the same both for a child and for an elderly man. In other words, the holy name of the Lord,
"hā rāma,
" always acts, even when the holy names are chanted without reference to the Supreme Lord.
Yavanas
utter the holy name in a different attitude than devotees, but the holy name
"hā rāma
" is so powerful spiritually that it acts anywhere, whether one knows it or not. This is explained as follows.
