verses.translation: Another day, Gadādhara Paṇḍita invited Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to dinner. The Lord took prasāda at his home with His personal associates.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nŚrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura comments that Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu acted as a very merciful well-wisher toward Vallabha Bhaṭṭa by externally neglecting him in many ways to purify him of his false pride in being a learned scholar. The Lord neglected Gadādhara Paṇḍita for a few days because of his associating with Vallabha Bhaṭṭa. Actually He was not at all displeased with Gadādhara Paṇḍita. Indeed, because Gadādhara Paṇḍita is the personal potency of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, there is no chance of the Lord's being dissatisfied with him. However, a person who is too attracted to externals cannot understand the deep meaning of these dealings of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. If one therefore becomes disrespectful to Gadādhara Paṇḍita, he will surely be vanquished.

verses.devanagari: তাহাঁই বল্লভ-ভট্ট প্রভুর আজ্ঞা লৈল ।\\nপণ্ডিত-ঠাঞি পূর্বপ্রার্থিত সব সিদ্ধি হৈল ॥১৭১॥
verses.transliteration: tāhāṅi vallabha-bhaṭṭa prabhura ājñā laila\\npaṇḍita-ṭhāñi pūrva-prārthita saba siddhi haila
verses.translation: There Vallabha Bhaṭṭa took permission from Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and his desire to be initiated by Gadādhara Paṇḍita was thus fulfilled.

verses.devanagari: এই ত’ কহিলুঁ বল্লভ-ভট্টের মিলন ।\\nযাহার শ্রবণে পায় গৌরপ্রেমধন ॥১৭২॥
verses.transliteration: ei ta' kahiluṅ vallabha-bhaṭṭera milana\\nyāhāra śravaṇe pāya gaura-prema-dhana
verses.translation: I have thus explained the Lord's meeting with Vallabha Bhaṭṭa. By hearing of this incident, one can achieve the treasure of love for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: শ্রীরূপ-রঘুনাথ-পদে যার আশ ।\\nচৈতন্যচরিতামৃত কহে কৃষ্ণদাস ॥১৭৩॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa\\ncaitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa
verses.translation: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThus end the Bhaktivedanta purports to Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā,  Ninth Chapter, describing the meeting of Vallabha Bhaṭṭa with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

sections.title: Chapter 8: Rāmacandra Purī Criticizes the Lord

verses.devanagari: তং বন্দে কৃষ্ণচৈতন্যং রামচন্দ্রপুরীভয়াৎ ।\\nলৌকিকাহারতঃ স্বং যো ভিক্ষান্নং সমকোচয়ৎ ॥১॥
verses.transliteration: taṁ vande kṛṣṇa-caitanyaṁ\\nrāmacandra-purī-bhayāt\\nlaukikāhārataḥ svaṁ yo\\nbhikṣānnaṁ samakocayat
verses.translation: Let me offer my respectful obeisances to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who reduced His eating due to fear of the criticism of Rāmacandra Purī.

verses.devanagari: জয় জয় শ্রীচৈতন্য করুণাসিন্ধু-অবতার ।\\nব্রহ্মা-শিবাদিক ভজে চরণ যাঁহার ॥২॥
verses.transliteration: jaya jaya śrī-caitanya karuṇā-sindhu-avatāra\\nbrahmā-śivādika bhaje caraṇa yāṅhāra
verses.translation: All glories to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the incarnation of the ocean of mercy. His lotus feet are worshiped by demigods like Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva.

verses.devanagari: জয় জয় অবধূতচন্দ্র নিত্যানন্দ ।\\nজগৎ বাঁধিল যেঁহ দিয়া প্রেমফাঁদ ॥৩॥
verses.transliteration: jaya jaya avadhūta-candra nityānanda\\njagat bāṅdhila yeṅha diyā prema-phāṅda
verses.translation: All glories to Nityānanda Prabhu, the greatest of mendicants, who bound the entire world with a knot of ecstatic love for God.

verses.devanagari: জয় জয় অদ্বৈত ঈশ্বর অবতার ।\\nকৃষ্ণ অবতারি’ কৈল জগৎ-নিস্তার ॥৪॥
verses.transliteration: jaya jaya advaita īśvara avatāra\\nkṛṣṇa avatāri' kaila jagat-nistāra
verses.translation: All glories to Advaita Prabhu, the incarnation of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. He induced Kṛṣṇa to descend and thus delivered the entire world.

verses.devanagari: জয় জয় শ্রীবাসাদি যত ভক্তগণ ।\\nশ্রীকৃষ্ণচৈতন্য প্রভু — যাঁর প্রাণধন ॥৫॥
verses.transliteration: jaya jaya śrīvāsādi yata bhakta-gaṇa\\nśrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya prabhu—yāṅra prāṇa-dhana
verses.translation: All glories to all the devotees, headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura. Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu is their life and soul.

verses.devanagari: এইমত গৌরচন্দ্র নিজভক্ত-সঙ্গে ।\\nনীলাচলে ক্রীড়া করে কৃষ্ণপ্রেমতরঙ্গে ॥৬॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata gauracandra nija-bhakta-saṅge\\nnīlācale krīḍā kare kṛṣṇa-prema-taraṅge
verses.translation: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, at Jagannātha Purī, performed His various pastimes with His own devotees in the waves of love for Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: হেনকালে রামচন্দ্রপুরী-গোসাঞি আইলা ।\\nপরমানন্দ-পুরীরে আর প্রভুরে মিলিলা ॥৭॥
verses.transliteration: hena-kāle rāmacandra-purī-gosāñi āilā\\nparamānanda-purīre āra prabhure mililā
verses.translation: Then a sannyāsī named Rāmacandra Purī Gosāñi came to see Paramānanda Purī and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: পরমানন্দ-পুরী কৈল চরণ বন্দন ।\\nপুরী-গোসাঞি কৈল তাঁরে দৃঢ় আলিঙ্গন ॥৮॥
verses.transliteration: paramānanda-purī kaila caraṇa vandana\\npurī-gosāñi kaila tāṅre dṛḍha āliṅgana
verses.translation: Paramānanda Purī offered respects at the feet of Rāmacandra Purī, and Rāmacandra Purī strongly embraced him.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Because Rāmacandra Purī was a disciple of Mādhavendra Purī, both Paramānanda Purī and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu offered him respectful obeisances. Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura comments that although Rāmacandra Purī was naturally very envious and although he was against the principles of Vaiṣṇavism-or, in other words, against the principles of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and His devotees-common people nevertheless addressed him as
Gosvāmī
or
Gosāñi
because he was superficially in the renounced order and dressed like a
sannyāsī.
In the modern age the title
gosvāmī
is used by a caste of
gṛhasthas,
but formerly it was not. Rūpa Gosvāmī and Sanātana Gosvāmī, for example, were called
gosvāmī
because they were in the renounced order. Similarly, because Paramānanda Purī was a
sannyāsī,
he was called Purī Gosvāmī. By careful scrutiny, therefore, one will find that gosvāmī is not the title for a certain caste; rather, it is properly the title for a person in the renounced order.

verses.devanagari: মহাপ্রভু কৈলা তাঁরে দণ্ডবৎ নতি ।\\nআলিঙ্গন করি’ তেঁহো কৈল কৃষ্ণস্মৃতি ॥৯॥
verses.transliteration: mahāprabhu kailā tāṅre daṇḍavat nati\\nāliṅgana kari' teṅho kaila kṛṣṇa-smṛti
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu also offered obeisances unto Rāmacandra Purī, who then embraced Him and thus remembered Kṛṣṇa.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu offered obeisances to Rāmacandra Purī in consideration of his being a disciple of Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī, the spiritual master of His own spiritual master, Īśvara Purī. When a Vaiṣṇava
sannyāsī
meets another Vaiṣṇava
sannyāsī,
they both remember Kṛṣṇa. Even Māyāvādī
sannyāsīs
generally remember Nārāyaṇa, who is also Kṛṣṇa, by saying
oṁ namo bhagavate nārāyaṇa
or
namo nārāyaṇa.
Thus it is the duty of a
sannyāsī
to remember Kṛṣṇa. According to
smṛti-śāstra,
a
sannyāsī
does not offer obeisances or blessings to anyone. it is said,
sannyāsī nirāśīr nirnamaṣkriyaḥ:
a
sannyāsī
should not offer anyone blessings or obeisances.

verses.devanagari: তিনজনে ইষ্টগোষ্ঠী কৈলা কতক্ষণ ।\\nজগদানন্দ-পণ্ডিত তাঁরে কৈলা নিমন্ত্রণ ॥১০॥
verses.transliteration: tina-jane iṣṭha-goṣṭhī kailā kata-kṣaṇa\\njagadānanda-paṇḍita tāṅre kailā nimantraṇa
verses.translation: The three of them talked about Kṛṣṇa for some time, and then Jagadānanda came and extended an invitation to Rāmacandra Purī.

verses.devanagari: জগন্নাথের প্রসাদ আনিলা ভিক্ষার লাগিয়া ।\\nযথেষ্ট ভিক্ষা করিলা তেঁহো নিন্দার লাগিয়া ॥১১॥
verses.transliteration: jagannāthera prasāda ānilā bhikṣāra lāgiyā\\nyatheṣṭa bhikṣā karilā teṅho nindāra lāgiyā
verses.translation: A large quantity of the remnants of food from Lord Jagannātha was brought in for distribution. Rāmacandra Purī ate sumptuously, and then he wanted to find faults in Jagadānanda Paṇḍita.

verses.devanagari: ভিক্ষা করি’ কহে পুরী, — “শুন, জগদানন্দ ।\\nঅবশেষ প্রসাদ তুমি করহ ভক্ষণ ।।” ॥ ১২ ॥
verses.transliteration: bhikṣā kari' kahe purī,—"śuna, jagadānanda\\navaśeṣa prasāda tumi karaha bhakṣaṇa"
verses.translation: After finishing the meal, Rāmacandra Purī requested, "My dear Jagadānanda, please listen. You eat the food that is left."

verses.devanagari: আগ্রহ করিয়া তাঁরে বসি’ খাওয়াইল ।\\nআপনে আগ্রহ করি’ পরিবেশন কৈল ॥১৩॥
verses.transliteration: āgraha kariyā tāṅre vasi' khāoyāila\\nāpane āgraha kari' pariveśana kaila
verses.translation: With great eagerness Rāmacandra Purī seated Jagadānanda Paṇḍita and personally served him prasāda.

verses.devanagari: আগ্রহ করিয়া পুনঃ পুনঃ খাওয়াইল ।\\nআচমন কৈলে নিন্দা করিতে লাগিল ॥১৪॥
verses.transliteration: āgraha kariyā punaḥ punaḥ khāoyāila\\nācamana kaile nindā karite lāgila
verses.translation: Encouraging him again and again, Rāmacandra Purī fed him sumptuously, but when Jagadānanda had washed his hands and mouth, Rāmacandra Purī began criticizing him.

verses.devanagari: “শুনি, চৈতন্যগণ করে বহুত ভক্ষণ ।\\n‘সত্য’ সেই বাক্য, — সাক্ষাৎ দেখিলুঁ এখন ॥১৫॥
verses.transliteration: "śuni, caitanya-gaṇa kare bahuta bhakṣaṇa\\n'satya' sei vākya,—sākṣāt dekhiluṅ ekhana
verses.translation: "I have heard," he said, "that the followers of Caitanya Mahāprabhu eat more than necessary. Now I have directly seen that this is true.

verses.devanagari: সন্ন্যাসীরে এত খাওয়াঞা করে ধর্ম নাশ ।\\nবৈরাগী হঞা এত খায়, বৈরাগ্যের নাহি ‘ভাস’ ।।” ॥ ১৬ ॥
verses.transliteration: sannyāsīre eta khāoyāñā kare dharma nāśa\\nvairāgī hañā eta khāya, vairāgyera nāhi 'bhāsa' "
verses.translation: "Feeding a sannyāsī too much breaks his regulative principles, for when a sannyāsī eats too much, his renunciation is destroyed."

verses.devanagari: এই ত’ স্বভাব তাঁর আগ্রহ করিয়া ।\\nপিছে নিন্দা করে, আগে বহুত খাওয়াঞা ॥১৭॥
verses.transliteration: ei ta' svabhāva tāṅra āgraha kariyā\\npiche nindā kare, āge bahuta khāoyāñā
verses.translation: The characteristic of Rāmacandra Purī was that first he would induce someone to eat more than necessary and then he would criticize him.

verses.devanagari: পূর্বে যবে মাধবেন্দ্র করেন অন্তর্ধান ।\\nরামচন্দ্রপুরী তবে আইলা তাঁর স্থান ॥১৮॥
verses.transliteration: pūrve yabe mādhavendra karena antardhāna\\nrāmacandra-purī tabe āilā tāṅra sthāna
verses.translation: Formerly, when Mādhavendra Purī was at the last stage of his life, Rāmacandra Purī came to where he was staying.

verses.devanagari: পুরী-গোসাঞি করে কৃষ্ণনাম-সঙ্কীর্তন ।\\n‘মথুরা না পাইনু’ বলি’ করেন ক্রন্দন ॥১৯॥
verses.transliteration: purī-gosāñi kare kṛṣṇa-nāma-saṅkīrtana\\n'mathurā nā pāinu' bali' karena krandana
verses.translation: Mādhavendra Purī was chanting the holy name of Kṛṣṇa, and sometimes he would cry, "O my Lord, I did not get shelter at Mathurā."

verses.devanagari: রামচন্দ্রপুরী তবে উপদেশে তাঁরে ।\\nশিষ্য হঞা গুরুকে কহে, ভয় নাহি করে ॥২০॥
verses.transliteration: rāmacandra-purī tabe upadeśe tāṅre\\nśiṣya hañā guruke kahe, bhaya nāhi kare
verses.translation: Then Rāmacandra Purī was so foolish that he fearlessly dared to instruct his spiritual master.

verses.devanagari: “তুমি — পূর্ণ-ব্রহ্মানন্দ, করহ স্মরণ ।\\nব্রহ্মবিৎ হঞা কেনে করহ রোদন?” ॥২১॥
verses.transliteration: "tumi—pūrṇa-brahmānanda, karaha smaraṇa\\nbrahmavit hañā kene karaha rodana?"
verses.translation: "If you are in full transcendental bliss," he said, "you should now remember only Brahman. Why are you crying?"
verses.purport:
PURPORT
As stated in
Bhagavad-gītā, brahma-bhūtaḥ prasannātmā:
a Brahman realized person is always happy.
Na śocati na kāṅkṣati:
he neither laments nor aspires for anything. Not knowing why Mādhavendra Purī was crying, Rāmacandra Purī tried to become his advisor. Thus he committed a great offense, for a disciple should never try to instruct his spiritual master.

verses.devanagari: শুনি’ মাধবেন্দ্র-মনে ক্রোধ উপজিল ।\\n‘দূর, দূর, পাপিষ্ঠ’ বলি’ ভর্ৎসনা করিল ॥২২॥
verses.transliteration: śuni' mādhavendra-mane krodha upajila\\n'dūra, dūra, pāpiṣṭha' bali' bhartsanā karila
verses.translation: Hearing this instruction, Mādhavendra Purī, greatly angry, rebuked him by saying, "Get out, you sinful rascal!
verses.purport: PURPORT\nRāmacandra Purī could not understand that his spiritual master, Mādhavendra Purī, was feeling transcendental separation. His lamentation was not material. Rather, it proceeded from the highest stage of ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa. When he was crying in separation, "I could not achieve Kṛṣṇa! I could not reach Mathurā!" this was not ordinary material lamentation. Rāmacandra Purī was not sufficiently expert to understand the feelings of Mādhavendra Purī, but nevertheless he thought himself very advanced. Therefore, regarding Mādhavendra Purī's expressions as ordinary material lamentation, he advised him to remember Brahman because he was latently an impersonalist. Mādhavendra Purī understood Rāmacandra Purī's position as a great fool and therefore immediately rebuked him. Such a reprimand from the spiritual master is certainly for the betterment of the disciple.

verses.devanagari: ‘কৃষ্ণ না পাইনু, না পাইনু ‘মথুরা’ ।\\nআপন-দুঃখে মরোঁ — এই দিতে আইল জ্বালা ॥২৩॥
verses.transliteration: 'kṛṣṇa nā pāinu, nā pāinu 'mathurā'\\nāpana-duḥkhe maroṅ—ei dite āila jvālā
verses.translation: "O my Lord Kṛṣṇa, I could not reach You, nor could I reach Your abode, Mathurā. I am dying in my unhappiness, and now this rascal has come to give me more pain.

verses.devanagari: মোরে মুখ না দেখাবি তুই, যাও যথি-তথি ।\\nতোরে দেখি’ মৈলে মোর হবে অসদ্গতি ॥২৪॥
verses.transliteration: more mukha nā dekhābi tui, yāo yathi-tathi\\ntore dekhi' maile mora habe asad-gati
verses.translation: "Don't show your face to me! Go anywhere else you like. If I die seeing your face, I shall not achieve the destination of my life.

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণ না পাইনু মুঞি মরোঁ আপনার দুঃখে ।\\nমোরে ‘ব্রহ্ম’ উপদেশে এই ছার মূর্খে ।।” ॥ ২৫ ॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇa nā pāinu muñi maroṅ āpanāra duḥkhe\\nmore 'brahma' upadeśe ei chāra mūrkhe"
verses.translation: "I am dying without achieving the shelter of Kṛṣṇa, and therefore I am greatly unhappy. Now this condemned foolish rascal has come to instruct me about Brahman."

verses.devanagari: এই যে শ্রীমাধবেন্দ্র শ্রীপাদ উপেক্ষা করিল ।\\nসেই অপরাধে ইঁহার ‘বাসনা’ জন্মিল ॥২৬॥
verses.transliteration: ei ye śrī-mādhavendra śrī-pāda upekṣā karila\\nsei aparādhe iṅhāra 'vāsanā, janmila
verses.translation: Rāmacandra Purī was thus denounced by Mādhavendra Purī. Due to his offense, gradually material desire appeared within him.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The word
vāsanā
("material desires") refers to dry speculative knowledge. Such speculative knowledge is only material. As confirmed in
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(10.14.4), a person without devotional service who simply wants to know things
(kevala-bodha-labdhaye
) gains only dry speculative knowledge but no spiritual profit. This is also confirmed in the
Bhakti-sandarbha
(111), wherein it is said:
jīvan-muktā api punar
yānti saṁsāra-vāsanām
yady acintya-mahā-śaktau
bhagavaty aparādhinaḥ
"Even though one is liberated in this life, if one offends the Supreme Personality of Godhead he falls down in the midst of material desires, of which dry speculation about spiritual realization is one."
In his
Laghu-toṣaṇī
commentary on
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(10.2.32), Jīva Gosvāmī says;
jīvan-muktā api punar
bandhanaṁ yānti karmabhiḥ
yady acintya-mahā-śaktau
bhagavaty aparādhinaḥ
"Even if one is liberated in this life, he becomes addicted to material desires because of offenses to the Supreme Personality of Godhead."
A similar quotation from one of the
Purāṇas
also appears in the
Viṣṇu-bhakti-candrodaya:
jīvan-muktāḥ prapadyante
kvacit saṁsāra-vāsanām
yogino na vilipyante
karmabhir bhagavat-parāḥ
"Even liberated souls sometimes fall down to material desires, but those who fully engaged in devotional service to the Supreme Personality of Godhead are not affected by such desires."
These are references from authoritative revealed scriptures. If one becomes an offender to his spiritual master or the Supreme Personality of Godhead, he falls down to the material platform to merely speculate.

verses.devanagari: শুষ্ক-ব্রহ্মজ্ঞানী, নাহি কৃষ্ণের ‘সম্বন্ধ’ ।\\nসর্ব লোক নিন্দা করে, নিন্দাতে নির্বন্ধ ॥২৭॥
verses.transliteration: śuṣka-brahma-jñānī, nāhi kṛṣṇera 'sambandha'\\nsarva loka nindā kare, nindāte nirbandha
verses.translation: One who is attached to dry speculative knowledge has no relationship with Kṛṣṇa. His occupation is criticizing Vaiṣṇavas. Thus he is situated in criticism.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura has explained in his
Anubhāṣya
that the word
nirbandha
indicates that Rāmacandra Purī had a steady desire to criticize others. Impersonalist Māyāvādīs who have no relationship with Kṛṣṇa, who cannot take to devotional service and who simply engage in material arguments to understand Brahman regard devotional service to Kṛṣṇa as
karma-kāṇḍa,
or fruitive activities. According to them, devotional service to Kṛṣṇa is but another means for attaining
dharma, artha, kāma
and
mokṣa.
Therefore they criticize the devotees for engaging in material activities. They think that devotional service is
māyā
and that Kṛṣṇa or Viṣṇu is also
māyā.
Therefore they are called Māyāvādīs. Such a mentality awakens in a person who is an offender to Kṛṣṇa and His devotees.

verses.devanagari: ঈশ্বরপুরী গোসাঞি করে শ্রীপাদ-সেবন ।\\nস্বহস্তে করেন মলমূত্রাদি মার্জন ॥২৮॥
verses.transliteration: īśvara-purī gosāñi kare śrī-pāda-sevana\\nsvahaste karena mala-mūtrādi mārjana
verses.translation: Īśvara Purī, the spiritual master of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, performed service to Mādhavendra Purī, cleaning up his stool and urine with his own hand.

verses.devanagari: নিরন্তর কৃষ্ণনাম করায় স্মরণ ।\\nকৃষ্ণনাম, কৃষ্ণলীলা শুনায় অনুক্ষণ ॥২৯॥
verses.transliteration: nirantara kṛṣṇa-nāma karāya smaraṇa\\nkṛṣṇa-nāma, kṛṣṇa-līlā śunāya anukṣaṇa
verses.translation: Īśvara Purī was always chanting the holy name and pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa for Mādhavendra Purī to hear. In this way he helped Mādhavendra Purī remember the holy name and pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa at the time of death.

verses.devanagari: তুষ্ট হঞা পুরী তাঁরে কৈলা আলিঙ্গন ।\\nবর দিলা — ‘কৃষ্ণে তোমার হউক প্রেমধন’ ॥৩০॥
verses.transliteration: tuṣṭa hañā purī tāṅre kailā āliṅgana\\nvara dilā—'kṛṣṇe tomāra ha-uka prema-dhana'
verses.translation: Pleased with Īśvara Purī, Mādhavendra Purī embraced him and gave him the benediction that he would be a great devotee and lover of Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: সেই হৈতে ঈশ্বরপুরী — ‘প্রেমের সাগর’ ।\\nরামচন্দ্রপুরী হৈল সর্বনিন্দাকর ॥৩১॥
verses.transliteration: sei haite īśvara-purī—'premera sāgara'\\nrāmacandra-purī haila sarva-nindākara
verses.translation: Thus Īśvara Purī became like an ocean of ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa, whereas Rāmacandra Purī became a dry speculator and a critic of everyone else.

verses.devanagari: মহদনুগ্রহ-নিগ্রহের ‘সাক্ষী’ দুইজনে ।\\nএই দুইদ্বারে শিখাইলা জগজনে ॥৩২॥
verses.transliteration: mahad-anugraha-nigrahera 'sākṣī' dui-jane\\nei dui-dvāre śikhāilā jaga-jane
verses.translation: Īśvara Purī received the blessing of Mādhavendra Purī, whereas Rāmacandra Purī received a rebuke from him. Therefore these two persons, Īśvara Purī and Rāmacandra Purī, are examples of the objects of a great personality's benediction and punishment. Mādhavendra Purī instructed the entire world by presenting these two examples.

verses.devanagari: জগদ্গুরু মাধবেন্দ্র করি’ প্রেম দান ।\\nএই শ্লোক পড়ি’ তেঁহো কৈল অন্তর্ধান ॥৩৩॥
verses.transliteration: jagad-guru mādhavendra kari' prema dāna\\nei śloka paḍi' teṅho kaila antardhāna
verses.translation: His Divine Grace Mādhavendra Purī, the spiritual master of the entire world, thus distributed ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa. While passing away from the material world, he chanted the following verse.

verses.devanagari: অয়ি দীনদয়ার্দ্রনাথ হে\\nমথুরানাথ কদাবলোক্যসে ।\\nহৃদয়ং ত্বদলোককাতরং\\nদয়িত ভ্রাম্যতি কিং করোম্যহম্ ॥৩৪॥
verses.transliteration: ayi dīna-dayārdra nātha he\\nmathurā-nātha kadāvalokyase\\nhṛdayaṁ tvad-aloka-kātaraṁ\\ndayita bhrāmyati kiṁ karomy aham
verses.translation: "O my Lord! O most merciful master! O master of Mathurā! When shall I see You again? Because of my not seeing You, my agitated heart has become unsteady. O most beloved one, what shall I do now?"

verses.devanagari: এই শ্লোকে কৃষ্ণপ্রেম করে উপদেশ ।\\nকৃষ্ণের বিরহে ভক্তের ভাববিশেষ ॥৩৫॥
verses.transliteration: ei śloke kṛṣṇa-prema kare upadeśa\\nkṛṣṇera virahe bhaktera bhāva-viśeṣa
verses.translation: In this verse Mādhavendra Purī instructs how to achieve ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa. By feeling separation from Kṛṣṇa, one becomes spiritually situated.

verses.devanagari: পৃথিবীতে রোপণ করি’ গেলা প্রেমাঙ্কুর ।\\nসেই প্রেমাঙ্কুরের বৃক্ষ — চৈতন্যঠাকুর ॥৩৬॥
verses.transliteration: pṛthivīte ropaṇa kari' gelā premāṅkura\\nsei premāṅkurera vṛkṣa—caitanya-ṭhākura
verses.translation: Mādhavendra Purī sowed the seed of ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa within this material world and then departed. That seed later became a great tree in the form of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: প্রস্তাবে কহিলুঁ পুরী-গোসাঞির নির্যাণ ।\\nযেই ইহা শুনে, সেই বড় ভাগ্যবান্ ॥৩৭॥
verses.transliteration: prastāve kahiluṅ purī-gosāñira niryāṇa\\nyei ihā śune, sei baḍa bhāgyavān
verses.translation: I have incidentally described the passing away of Mādhavendra Purī. Anyone who hears this must be considered very fortunate.

verses.devanagari: রামচন্দ্রপুরী ঐছে রহিলা নীলাচলে ।\\nবিরক্ত স্বভাব, কভু রহে কোন স্থলে ॥৩৮॥
verses.transliteration: rāmacandra-purī aiche rahilā nīlācale\\nvirakta svabhāva, kabhu rahe kona sthale
verses.translation: Thus Rāmacandra Purī stayed at Jagannātha Purī. As customary for those in the renounced order, he would sometimes stay someplace and then go away.

verses.devanagari: অনিমন্ত্রণ ভিক্ষা করে, নাহিক নির্ণয় ।\\nঅন্যের ভিক্ষার স্থিতির লয়েন নিশ্চয় ॥৩৯॥
verses.transliteration: animantraṇa bhikṣā kare, nāhika nirṇaya\\nanyera bhikṣāra sthitira layena niścaya
verses.translation: There was no certainty of where Rāmacandra Purī would take his meal, for he would do so even uninvited. Nevertheless, he was very particular to keep account of how others were taking their meals.

verses.devanagari: প্রভুর নিমন্ত্রণে লাগে কৌড়ি চারি পণ ।\\nকভু কাশীশ্বর, গোবিন্দ খান তিন জন ॥৪০॥
verses.transliteration: prabhura nimantraṇe lāge kauḍi cāri paṇa\\nkabhu kāśīśvara, govinda khāna tina jana
verses.translation: To invite Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would cost 320 kauḍis [small conchshells]. This would provide lunch for three people, including Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and sometimes Kāśīśvara and Govinda.

verses.devanagari: প্রত্যহ প্রভুর ভিক্ষা ইতি-উতি হয় ।\\nকেহ যদি মূল্য আনে, চারিপণ-নির্ণয় ॥৪১॥
verses.transliteration: pratyaha prabhura bhikṣā iti-uti haya\\nkeha yadi mūlya āne, cāri-paṇa-nirṇaya
verses.translation: Every day the Lord would take His meal at a different place, and if someone was prepared to pay for a meal, the price was fixed at only four paṇas.

verses.devanagari: প্রভুর স্থিতি, রীতি, ভিক্ষা, শয়ন, প্রয়াণ ।\\nরামচন্দ্রপুরী করে সর্বানুসন্ধান ॥৪২॥
verses.transliteration: prabhura sthiti, rīti, bhikṣā, śayana, prayāṇa\\nrāmacandra-purī kare sarvānusandhāna
verses.translation: Rāmacandra Purī concerned himself with gathering all sorts of information about how Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was situated, including His regulative principles, His lunch, His sleep and His movements.

verses.devanagari: প্রভুর যতেক গুণ স্পর্শিতে নারিল ।\\nছিদ্র চাহি’ বুলে, কাঁহা ছিদ্র না পাইল ॥৪৩॥
verses.transliteration: prabhura yateka guṇa sparśite nārila\\nchidra cāhi' bule, kāṅhā chidra nā pāila
verses.translation: Because Rāmacandra Purī was interested only in finding faults, he could not understand the transcendental qualities of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. His only concern was finding faults, but still he could not find any.

verses.devanagari: ‘সন্ন্যাসী হঞা করে মিষ্টান্ন ভক্ষণ ।\\nএই ভোগে হয় কৈছে ইন্দ্রিয়-বারণ’? ॥৪৪॥
verses.transliteration: 'sannyāsī hañā kare miṣṭānna bhakṣaṇa\\nei bhoge haya kaiche indriya-vāraṇa'?
verses.translation: At last he found a fault. "How can a person in the renounced order eat so many sweetmeats?" he said. "If one eats sweets, controlling the senses is very difficult."

verses.devanagari: এই নিন্দা করি’ কহে সর্বলোক-স্থানে ।\\nপ্রভুরে দেখিতেহ অবশ্য আইসে প্রতিদিনে ॥৪৫॥
verses.transliteration: ei nindā kari' kahe sarva-loka-sthāne\\nprabhure dekhiteha avaśya āise prati-dine
verses.translation: In this way Rāmacandra Purī blasphemed Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu before everyone, but nevertheless he would regularly come to see the Lord every day.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু গুরুবুদ্ধ্যে করেন সম্ভ্রম, সম্মান ।\\nতেঁহো ছিদ্র চাহি’ বুলে, — এই তার কাম ॥৪৬॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu guru-buddhye karena sambhrama, sammāna\\nteṅho chidra cāhi' bule,—ei tāra kāma
verses.translation: When they met, the Lord would offer him respectful obeisances, considering him a Godbrother of His spiritual master. Rāmacandra Purī's business, however, was to search for faults in the Lord.

verses.devanagari: যত নিন্দা করে তাহা প্রভু সব জানে ।\\nতথাপি আদর করে বড়ই সম্ভ্রমে ॥৪৭॥
verses.transliteration: yata nindā kare tāhā prabhu saba jāne\\ntathāpi ādara kaṛe baḍa-i sambhrame
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu knew that Rāmacandra Purī was criticizing Him before everyone, but whenever Rāmacandra Purī came to see Him, the Lord offered him respects with great attention.

verses.devanagari: একদিন প্রাতঃকালে আইলা প্রভুর ঘর ।\\nপিপীলিকা দেখি’ কিছু কহেন উত্তর ॥৪৮॥
verses.transliteration: eka-dina prātaḥ-kāle āilā prabhura ghara\\npipīlikā dekhi' kichu kahena uttara
verses.translation: One day Rāmacandra Purī came in the morning to the abode of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Seeing many ants, he said something to criticize the Lord.

verses.devanagari: “রাত্রাবত্র ঐক্ষবমাসীৎ, তেন পিপীলিকাঃ সঞ্চরন্তি ।\\nঅহো! বিরক্তানাং সন্ন্যাসিনামিয়মিন্দ্রিয়লালসেতি ব্রুবন্নুত্থায় গতঃ ।।” ॥ ৪৯ ॥
verses.transliteration: "rātrāv atra aikṣavam āsīt, tena\\npipīlikāḥ sañcaranti aho! viraktānāṁ\\nsannyāsinām iyam indriya-lālaseti\\nbruvann utthāya gataḥ."
verses.translation: "Last night there was sugar candy here," he said. "Therefore ants are wandering about. Alas, this renounced sannyāsī is attached to such sense gratification!" After speaking in this way, he got up and left.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু পরম্পরায় নিন্দা কৈরাছেন শ্রবণ ।\\nএবে সাক্ষাৎ শুনিলেন ‘কল্পিত’ নিন্দন ॥৫০॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu paramparāya nindā kairāchena śravaṇa\\nebe sākṣāt śunilena 'kalpita' nindana
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had heard rumors about Rāmacandra Purī's blasphemy. Now He directly heard his fanciful accusations.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nRāmacandra Purī could find no faults in the character of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, for He is situated in a transcendental position as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Ants are generally found everywhere, but when Rāmacandra Purī saw ants crawling in the abode of the Lord, he took for granted that they must have been there because Caitanya Mahāprabhu had been eating sweetmeats. He thus discovered imaginary faults in the Lord and then left.

verses.devanagari: সহজেই পিপীলিকা সর্বত্র বেড়ায় ।\\nতাহাতে তর্ক উঠাঞা দোষ লাগায় ॥৫১॥
verses.transliteration: sahajei pipīlikā sarvatra beḍāya\\ntāhāte tarka uṭhāñā doṣa lāgāya
verses.translation: Ants generally crawl about here, there and everywhere, but Rāmacandra Purī, looking for imaginary faults, criticized Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu by alleging that there had been sweetmeats in His room.

verses.devanagari: শুনি’ তাহা প্রভুর সঙ্কোচ-ভয় মনে  ।\\nগোবিন্দে বোলাঞা কিছু কহেন বচনে ॥৫২॥
verses.transliteration: śuni' tāhā prabhura saṅkoca-bhaya mane\\ngovinde bolāñā kichu kahena vacane
verses.translation: After hearing this criticism, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was doubtful and apprehensive. Therefore He called Govinda and instructed him as follows.

verses.devanagari: “আজি হৈতে ভিক্ষা আমার এই ত’ নিয়ম  ।\\nপিণ্ডাভোগের এক চৌঠি, পাঁচগণ্ডার ব্যঞ্জন ॥৫৩॥
verses.transliteration: "āji haite bhikṣā āmāra ei ta' niyama\\npiṇḍā-bhogera eka cauṭhi, pāṅca-gaṇḍāra vyañjana
verses.translation: "From today on it will be a rule that I shall accept only one-fourth of a pot of Lord Jagannātha's prasāda and five gaṇḍās worth of vegetables.

verses.devanagari: ইহা বই অধিক আর কিছু না আনিবা ।\\nঅধিক আনিলে আমা এথা না দেখিবা ।।” ॥ ৫৪ ॥
verses.transliteration: ihā ba-i adhika āra kichu nā ānibā\\nadhika ānile āmā ethā nā dekhibā"
verses.translation: "If you bring any more than this, you will not see Me here anymore."

verses.devanagari: সকল বৈষ্ণবে গোবিন্দ কহে এই বাত্ ।\\nশুনি’ সবার মাথে যৈছে হৈল বজ্রাঘাত ॥৫৫॥
verses.transliteration: sakala vaiṣṇave govinda kahe ei vāt\\nśuni' sabāra māthe yaiche haila vajrāghāta
verses.translation: Govinda relayed this message to all the devotees. When they heard it, they felt as if their heads had been struck by thunderbolts.

verses.devanagari: রামচন্দ্রপুরীকে সবায় দেয় তিরস্কার ।\\n‘এই পাপিষ্ঠ আসি’ প্রাণ লইল সবার’ ॥৫৬॥
verses.transliteration: rāmacandra-purīke sabāya deya tiraskāra\\n'ei pāpiṣṭha āsi' prāṇa la-ila sabāra'
verses.translation: All the devotees condemned Rāmacandra Purī, saying, "This sinful man has come here and taken our lives."

verses.devanagari: সেইদিন একবিপ্র কৈল নিমন্ত্রণ ।\\nএক-চৌঠি ভাত, পাঁচ-গণ্ডার ব্যঞ্জন ॥৫৭॥\\nএইমাত্র গোবিন্দ কৈল অঙ্গীকার ।\\nমাথায় ঘা মারে বিপ্র, করে হাহাকার ॥৫৮॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mātra govinda kaila aṅgīkāra\\nmāthāya ghā māre vipra, kare hāhākāra
verses.translation: That day, a brāhmaṇa extended an invitation to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. When Govinda accepted only five gaṇḍās worth of vegetables and a fourth of a pot of rice, the brāhmaṇa, in great despair, struck his head with his hand and cried, "Alas! Alas!"

verses.devanagari: সেই ভাত-ব্যঞ্জন প্রভু অর্ধেক খাইল ।\\nযে কিছু রহিল, তাহা গোবিন্দ পাইল ॥৫৯॥
verses.transliteration: sei bhāta-vyañjana prabhu ardheka khāila\\nye kichu rahila, tāhā govinda pāila
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ate only half of the rice and vegetables, and whatever remained was taken by Govinda.

verses.devanagari: অর্ধাশন করেন প্রভু, গোবিন্দ অর্ধাশন ।\\nসব ভক্তগণ তবে ছাড়িল ভোজন ॥৬০॥
verses.transliteration: ardhāśana karena prabhu, govinda ardhāśana\\nsaba bhakta-gaṇa tabe chāḍila bhojana
verses.translation: Thus both Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Govinda ate only half the food they needed. Because of this, all the other devotees gave up eating.

verses.devanagari: গোবিন্দ-কাশীশ্বরে প্রভু কৈলা আজ্ঞাপন ।\\n‘দুঁহে অন্যত্র মাগি’ কর উদর ভরণ’ ॥৬১॥
verses.transliteration: govinda-kāśīśvare prabhu kailā ājñāpana\\n'duṅhe anyatra māgi' kara udara bharaṇa'
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ordered Govinda and Kāśīśvara, "You may both take alms elsewhere to fill your bellies."

verses.devanagari: এইরূপ মহাদুঃখে দিন কত গেল ।\\nশুনি’ রামচন্দ্রপুরী প্রভু-পাশ আইল ॥৬২॥
verses.transliteration: ei-rūpa mahā-duḥkhe dina kata gela\\nśuni, rāmacandra-purī prabhu-pāśa āila
verses.translation: In this way, some days passed in great unhappiness. Hearing of all this, Rāmacandra Purī went to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: প্রণাম করি’ প্রভু কৈলা চরণ বন্দন ।\\nপ্রভুরে কহয়ে কিছু হাসিয়া বচন ॥৬৩॥
verses.transliteration: praṇāma kari' prabhu kailā caraṇa vandana\\nprabhure kahaye kichu hāsiyā vacana
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu offered His obeisances to Rāmacandra Purī, worshiping his feet. Then Rāmacandra Purī smiled and spoke to the Lord.

verses.devanagari: “সন্ন্যাসীর ধর্ম নহে ‘ইন্দ্রিয়-তর্পণ’ ।\\nযৈছে তৈছে করে মাত্র উদর ভরণ ॥৬৪॥
verses.transliteration: "sannyāsīra dharma nahe 'indriya-tarpaṇa'\\nyaiche taiche kare mātra udara bharaṇa
verses.translation: Rāmacandra Purī advised, "It is not the business of a sannyāsī to gratify his senses. He should fill his belly some way or other.

verses.devanagari: তোমারে ক্ষীণ দেখি, শুনি, — কর অর্ধাশন ।\\nএই ‘শুষ্ক-বৈরাগ্য’ নহে সন্ন্যাসীর ‘ধর্ম’ ॥৬৫॥
verses.transliteration: tomāre kṣīṇa dekhi, śuni,—kara ardhāśana\\nei 'śuṣka-vairāgya' nahe sannyāsīra 'dharma'
verses.translation: "I have heard that You have cut Your eating in half. Indeed, I see that You are skinny. Such dry renunciation is also not the religion of a sannyāsī.

verses.devanagari: যথাযোগ্য উদর ভরে, না করে ‘বিষয়’ ভোগ ।\\nসন্ন্যাসীর তবে সিদ্ধ হয় জ্ঞানযোগ ॥৬৬॥
verses.transliteration: yathā-yogya udara bhare, nā kare 'viṣaya' bhoga\\nsannyāsīra tabe siddha haya jñāna-yoga
verses.translation: "A sannyāsī eats as much as necessary to maintain his body, but he does not enjoy satisfying his senses materially. Thus a sannyāsī becomes perfect in his spiritual advancement in knowledge.

verses.devanagari: নাত্যশ্নতোঽপি যোগোঽস্তি ন চৈকান্তমনশ্নতঃ ।\\nন চাতিস্বপ্নশীলস্য জাগ্রতো নৈব চার্জুন ॥৬৭॥\\nযুক্তাহারবিহারস্য যুক্তচেষ্টস্য কর্মসু ।\\nযুক্তস্বপ্নাববোধস্য যোগো ভবতি দুঃখহা ।।” ৬৮ ॥৬৮॥
verses.transliteration: yuktāhāra-vihārasya\\nyukta-ceṣṭasya karmasu\\nyukta-svapnāvabodhasya\\nyogo bhavati duḥkha-hā"
verses.translation: "My dear Arjuna, one cannot perform mystic yoga if he eats more than necessary or needlessly fasts, sleeps and dreams too much or does not sleep enough. One should eat and enjoy his senses as much as necessary, one should properly endeavor to execute his duties, and one should regulate his sleep and wakefulness. Thus one can become freed from material pains by executing mystic yoga.' "
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Bhagavad-gītā
(6.16-17).

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহে, — “অজ্ঞ বালক মুই ‘শিষ্য’ তোমার ।\\nমোরে শিক্ষা দেহ’, — এই ভাগ্য আমার ।।” ॥ ৬৯ ॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahe,—"ajña bālaka mui 'śiṣya' tomāra\\nmore śikṣā deha',—ei bhāgya āmāra"
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then humbly submitted, "I am just like an ignorant boy and am like your disciple. It is My great fortune that you are instructing Me."

verses.devanagari: এত শুনি’ রামচন্দ্রপুরী উঠি’ গেলা ।\\nভক্তগণ অর্ধাশন করে, — পুরী গোসাঞি শুনিলা ॥৭০॥
verses.transliteration: eta śuni' rāmacandra-purī uṭhi' gelā\\nbhakta-gaṇa ardhāśana kare,—purī gosāñi śunilā
verses.translation: Hearing this, Rāmacandra Purī got up and left. He also heard from various sources that all the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu were eating half as much as usual.

verses.devanagari: আর দিন ভক্তগণ-সহ পরমানন্দপুরী  ।\\nপ্রভু-পাশে নিবেদিলা দৈন্য-বিনয় করি’ ॥৭১॥
verses.transliteration: āra dina bhakta-gaṇa-saha paramānanda-purī\\nprabhu-pāśe nivedilā dainya-vinaya kari'
verses.translation: The next day, Paramānanda Purī and other devotees approached Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu with great humility and submission.

verses.devanagari: “রামচন্দ্রপুরী হয় নিন্দুক-স্বভাব  ।\\nতার বোলে অন্ন ছাড়ি’ কিবা হবে লাভ? ॥৭২॥
verses.transliteration: "rāmacandra-purī haya ninduka-svabhāva\\ntāra bole anna chāḍi' kibā habe lābha?
verses.translation: Paramānanda Purī said, "My Godbrother Rāmacandra Purī is by nature a bad critic. If You give up eating because of his words, what will be the profit?

verses.devanagari: পুরীর স্বভাব, — যথেষ্ট আহার করাঞা ।\\nযে না খায়, তারে খাওয়ায় যতন করিয়া ॥৭৩॥
verses.transliteration: purīra svabhāva,—yatheṣṭa āhāra karāñā\\nye nā khāya, tāre khāoyāya yatana kariyā
verses.translation: "It is the nature of Rāmacandra Purī that first he lets one eat as much as desired, and if one does not eat more than necessary, with great attention he makes him eat more.

verses.devanagari: খাওয়াঞা পুনঃ তারে করয়ে নিন্দন ।\\n‘এত অন্ন খাও, — তোমার কত আছে ধন? ॥৭৪॥
verses.transliteration: khāoyāñā punaḥ tāre karaye nindana\\n'eta anna khāo,—tomāra kata āche dhana?
verses.translation: "In this way he induces one to eat more than necessary, and then he directly criticizes him, saying,'You eat so much. How much money do you have in your treasury?

verses.devanagari: সন্ন্যাসীকে এত খাওয়াঞা কর ধর্ম নাশ !\\nঅতএব জানিনু, — তোমার কিছু নাহি ভাস’ ॥৭৫॥
verses.transliteration: sannyāsīke eta khāoyāñā kara dharma nāśa!\\nataeva jāninu,—tomāra kichu nāhi bhāsa'
verses.translation: "Also, by inducing sannyāsīs to eat so much, you spoil their religious principles. Therefore I can understand that you have no advancement.'

verses.devanagari: কে কৈছে ব্যবহারে, কেবা কৈছে খায় ।\\nএই অনুসন্ধান তেঁহো করয় সদায় ॥৭৬॥
verses.transliteration: ke kaiche vyavahāre, kebā kaiche khāya\\nei anusandhāna teṅho karaya sadāya
verses.translation: "It is Rāmacandra Purī's business to inquire always about how others are eating and conducting their daily affairs.

verses.devanagari: শাস্ত্রে যেই দুই ধর্ম কৈরাছে বর্জন ।\\nসেই কর্ম নিরন্তর ইঁহার করণ ॥৭৭॥
verses.transliteration: śāstre yei dui dharma kairāche varjana\\nsei karma nirantara iṅhāra karaṇa
verses.translation: "The two kinds of activity rejected in the revealed scriptures constitute his daily affairs.

verses.devanagari: পরস্বভাবকর্মাণি ন প্রশংসেন্ন গর্হয়েৎ ।\\nবিশ্বমেকাত্মকং পশ্যন্ প্রকৃত্যা পুরুষেণ চ ॥৭৮॥
verses.transliteration: para-svabhāva-karmāṇi\\nna praśaṁsen na garhayet\\nviśvam ekātmakaṁ paśyan\\nprakṛtyā puruṣeṇa ca
verses.translation: "One should see that because of the meeting of material nature and the living entity, the universe is acting uniformly. Thus one should neither praise nor criticize the characteristics or activities of others.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(11.28.1) was spoken by Lord Kṛṣṇa to Uddhava.

verses.devanagari: তার মধ্যে পূর্ববিধি ‘প্রশংসা’ ছাড়িয়া ।\\nপরবিধি ‘নিন্দা’ করে ‘বলিষ্ঠ’ জানিয়া ॥৭৯॥
verses.transliteration: tāra madhye pūrva-vidhi 'praśaṁsā' chāḍiyā\\npara-vidhi 'nindā' kare 'baliṣṭha' jāniyā
verses.translation: "Of the two rules, Rāmacandra Purī obeys the first by abandoning praise, but although he knows that the second is more prominent, he neglects it by criticizing others.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The above-mentioned verse from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
gives two injunctions. The first, called
pūrva-vidhi,
is that one should not praise, and the second,
para-vidhi,
is that one should not criticize. As will be apparent from the following verse, the injunction against praise is less important than the injunction against blasphemy. One should carefully observe the
para-vidhi,
although one may neglect the
pūrva-vidhi.
Thus the actual injunction is that one may praise but should not criticize. This is called
śleṣokti,
or a statement having two meanings. Rāmacandra Purī, however, acted in just the opposite way, for he neglected the
para-vidhi
but strictly observed the
pūrva-vidhi.
Since he avoided following the principle of not criticizing, Rāmacandra Purī broke both the rules.

verses.devanagari: পূর্বপরয়োর্মধ্যে পববিধির্বলবান্ ॥৮০॥
verses.transliteration: pūrva-parayor madhye para-vidhir balavān
verses.translation: "Between the former rule and the latter rule, the latter is more important.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a verse from the
nyāya
literatures.

verses.devanagari: যাহাঁ গুণ শত আছে, তাহা না করে গ্রহণ ।\\nগুণমধ্যে ছলে করে দোষ-আরোপণ ॥৮১॥
verses.transliteration: yāhāṅ guṇa śata āche, tāhā nā kare grahaṇa\\nguṇa-madhye chale kare doṣa-āropaṇa
verses.translation: "Even where there are hundreds of good qualities, a critic does not consider them. Rather, he attempts by some trick to point out a fault in those attributes.

verses.devanagari: ইঁহার স্বভাব ইহাঁ করিতে না যুয়ায় ।\\nতথাপি কহিয়ে কিছু মর্ম-দুঃখ পায় ॥৮২॥
verses.transliteration: iṅhāra svabhāva ihāṅ karite nā yuyāya\\ntathāpi kahiye kichu marma-duḥkha pāya
verses.translation: "One should not, therefore, follow the principles of Rāmacandra Purī. Nevertheless, I have to say something against him because he is making our hearts unhappy.

verses.devanagari: ইঁহার বচনে কেনে অন্ন ত্যাগ কর ?\\nপূর্ববৎ নিমন্ত্রণ মান’, — সবার বোল ধর ।।” ॥ ৮৩ ॥
verses.transliteration: iṅhāra vacane kene anna tyāga kara?\\npūrvavat nimantraṇa māna',—sabāra bola dhara"
verses.translation: "Why have you given up proper eating due to the criticism of Rāmacandra Purī? Please accept invitations as before. This is the request of us all."

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহে, — “সবে কেনে পুরীরে কর রোষ ?\\n‘সহজ’ ধর্ম কহে তেঁহো, তাঁর কিবা দোষ? ॥৮৪॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahe,—"sabe kene purīre kara roṣa?\\n'sahaja' dharma kahe teṅho, tāṅra kibā doṣa?
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "Why are all of you angry at Rāmacandra Purī? He is expounding the natural principles of sannyāsa life. Why are you accusing him?

verses.devanagari: যতি হঞা জিহ্বা-লাম্পট্য, — অত্যন্ত অন্যায় ।\\nযতির ধর্ম, — প্রাণ রাখিতে আহারমাত্র খায় ।।” ॥ ৮৫ ॥
verses.transliteration: yati hañā jihvā-lāmpaṭya—atyanta anyāya\\nyatira dharma,—prāṇa rākhite āhāra-mātra khāya"
verses.translation: "For a sannyāsī to indulge in satisfying the tongue is a great offense. The duty of a sannyāsī is to eat only as much as needed to keep body and soul together."

verses.devanagari: তবে সবে মেলি’ প্রভুরে বহু যত্ন কৈলা ।\\nসবার আগ্রহে প্রভু অর্ধেক রাখিলা ॥৮৬॥
verses.transliteration: tabe sabe meli' prabhure bahu yatna kailā\\nsabāra āgrahe prabhu ardheka rākhilā
verses.translation: When they all requested very fervently that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu take a full meal, He still would not do so. Instead, He responded to their request by accepting half as much as usual.

verses.devanagari: দুইপণ কৌড়ি লাগে প্রভুর নিমন্ত্রণে ।\\nকভু দুইজন ভোক্তা, কভু তিনজনে ॥৮৭॥
verses.transliteration: dui-paṇa kauḍi lāge prabhura nimantraṇe\\nkabhu dui-jana bhoktā, kabhu tina-jane
verses.translation: The cost for the food needed to invite Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was fixed at two paṇas of kauḍis [160 conchshells], and that food would be taken by two men and sometimes three.

verses.devanagari: অভোজ্যান্ন বিপ্র যদি করেন নিমন্ত্রণ ।\\nপ্রসাদ-মূল্য লইতে লাগে কৌড়ি দুইপণ ॥৮৮॥
verses.transliteration: abhojyānna vipra yadi karena nimantraṇa\\nprasāda-mūlya la-ite lāge kauḍi dui-paṇa
verses.synonyms:
abhojya-anna vipra
—a
brāhmaṇa
at whose place an invitation cannot be accepted;
yadi
—if;
karena nimantraṇa
—he invites;
prasāda-mūlya
—the price of the
prasāda
;
la-ite
—to bear;
lāge
—costs;
kauḍi dui-paṇa
—two
paṇas
of
kauḍis.
verses.translation: When a brāhmaṇa at whose home an invitation could not be accepted invited the Lord, he would pay two paṇas of conchshells to purchase the prasāda.

verses.devanagari: ভোজ্যান্ন বিপ্র যদি নিমন্ত্রণ করে ।\\nকিছু ‘প্রসাদ’ আনে, কিছু পাক করে ঘরে ॥৮৯॥
verses.transliteration: bhojyānna vipra yadi nimantraṇa kare\\nkichu 'prasāda' āne, kichu pāka kare ghare
verses.translation: When a brāhmaṇa at whose home an invitation could be accepted invited Him, the brāhmaṇa would purchase part of the prasāda and cook the rest at home.

verses.devanagari: পণ্ডিত-গোসাঞি, ভগবান্-আচার্য, সার্বভৌম ।\\nনিমন্ত্রণের দিনে যদি করে নিমন্ত্রণ ॥৯০॥\\nতাঁ-সবার ইচ্ছায় প্রভু করেন ভোজন ।\\nতাহাঁ প্রভুর স্বাতন্ত্র্য নাই, যৈছে তাঁর মন ॥৯১॥
verses.transliteration: tāṅ-sabāra icchāya prabhu karena bhojana\\ntāhāṅ prabhura svātantrya nāi, yaiche tāṅra mana
verses.translation: Even on a day when Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was invited to dine by others, if Gadādhara Paṇḍita, Bhagavān Ācārya or Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya invited Him, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had no independence. He would accept their invitations as they desired.

verses.devanagari: ভক্তগণে সুখ দিতে প্রভুর ‘অবতার’ ।\\nযাহাঁ যৈছে যোগ্য, তাহাঁ করেন ব্যবহার ॥৯২॥
verses.transliteration: bhakta-gaṇe sukha dite prabhura 'avatāra'\\nyāhāṅ yaiche yogya, tāhāṅ karena vyavahāra
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu actually descended to give happiness to the devotees. Thus He behaved in whatever way fit the time and circumstances.

verses.devanagari: কভু লৌকিক রীতি, — যেন ‘ইতর’ জন ।\\nকভু স্বতন্ত্র, করেন ‘ঐশ্বর্য’ প্রকটন ॥৯৩॥
verses.transliteration: kabhu laukika rīti,—yena 'itara' jana\\nkabhu svatantra, karena 'aiśvarya' prakaṭana
verses.translation: Because of His full independence, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sometimes behaved like a common man and sometimes manifested His godly opulence.

verses.devanagari: কভু রামচন্দ্রপুরীর হয় ভৃত্যপ্রায় ।\\nকভু তারে নাহি মানে, দেখে তৃণ-প্রায় ॥৯৪॥
verses.transliteration: kabhu rāmacandra-purīra haya bhṛtya-prāya\\nkabhu tāre nāhi māne, dekhe tṛṇa-prāya
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sometimes accepted Rāmacandra Purī as His master and considered Himself a servant, and sometimes the Lord, not caring for him, would see him as being just like a straw.

verses.devanagari: ঈশ্বর-চরিত্র প্রভুর — বুদ্ধির অগোচর ।\\nযবে যেই করেন, সেই সব — মনোহর ॥৯৫॥
verses.transliteration: īśvara-caritra prabhura—buddhira agocara\\nyabe yei karena, sei saba—manohara
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu behaved exactly like the Supreme Personality of Godhead, beyond the restriction of anyone's intelligence. Whatever He liked He did, but all His activities were very beautiful.

verses.devanagari: এইমত রামচন্দ্রপুরী নীলাচলে ।\\nদিন কত রহি’ গেলা ‘তীর্থ’ করিবারে ॥৯৬॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata rāmacandra-purī nīlācale\\ndina kata rahi' gelā 'tīrtha' karibāre
verses.translation: Thus Rāmacandra Purī stayed for some days at Nīlācala [Jagannātha Purī]. Then he left to visit various holy places of pilgrimage.

verses.devanagari: তেঁহো গেলে প্রভুর গণ হৈল হরষিত ।\\nশিরের পাথর যেন পড়িল আচম্বিত ॥৯৭॥
verses.transliteration: teṅho gele prabhura gaṇa haila haraṣita\\nśirera pāthara yena paḍila ācambita
verses.translation: The devotees considered Rāmacandra Purī to be like a great burden on their heads. When he left Jagannātha Purī, everyone felt extremely happy, as if a great stone burden had suddenly fallen from their heads to the ground.

verses.devanagari: স্বচ্ছন্দে নিমন্ত্রণ, প্রভুর কীর্তন-নর্তন ।\\nস্বচ্ছন্দে করেন সবে প্রসাদ ভোজন ॥৯৮॥
verses.transliteration: svacchande nimantraṇa, prabhura kīrtana-nartana\\nsvacchande karena sabe prasāda bhojana
verses.translation: After his departure, everything was happy once again. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted invitations as usual and led congregational chanting and dancing. Everyone else also accepted prasāda without hindrances.

verses.devanagari: গুরু উপেক্ষা কৈলে, ঐছে ফল হয় ।\\nক্রমে ঈশ্বরপর্যন্ত অপরাধে ঠেকয় ॥৯৯॥
verses.transliteration: guru upekṣā kaile, aiche phala haya\\nkrame īśvara-paryanta aparādhe ṭhekaya
verses.translation: If one's spiritual master rejects him, one becomes so fallen that he, like Rāmacandra Purī, commits offenses even to the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

verses.devanagari: যদ্যপি গুরুবুদ্ধ্যে প্রভু তার দোষ না লইল ।\\nতার ফলদ্বারা লোকে শিক্ষা করাইল ॥১০০॥
verses.transliteration: yadyapi guru-buddhye prabhu tāra doṣa nā la-ila\\ntāra phala-dvārā loke śikṣā karāila
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not consider the offenses of Rāmacandra Purī, for the Lord considered him His spiritual master. However, his character instructed everyone about the result of offending the spiritual master.

verses.devanagari: চৈতন্যচরিত্র — যেন অমৃতের পূর ।\\nশুনিতে শ্রবণে মনে লাগয়ে মধুর ॥১০১॥
verses.transliteration: caitanya-caritra—yena amṛtera pūra\\nśunite śravaṇe mane lāgaye madhura
verses.translation: The character of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is full of nectar. Hearing about it is pleasing to the ear and mind.

verses.devanagari: চৈতন্যচরিত্র লিখি, শুন একমনে ।\\nঅনায়াসে পাবে প্রেম শ্রীকৃষ্ণচরণে ॥১০২॥
verses.transliteration: caitanya-caritra likhi, śuna eka-mane\\nanāyāse pābe prema śrī-kṛṣṇa-caraṇe
verses.translation: I write about the character of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. O readers, please hear with attention, for thus you will easily receive ecstatic love for the lotus feet of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: শ্রীরূপ-রঘুনাথ-পদে যার আশ ।\\nচৈতন্যচরিতামৃত কহে কৃষ্ণদাস ॥১০৩॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa\\ncaitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa
verses.translation: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThus end the Bhaktivedanta purports to Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā,  Eighth Chapter, describing how the Lord reduced His eating in fear of the criticism of Rāmacandra Purī.

sections.title: Chapter 9: The Deliverance of Gopīnātha Paṭṭanāyaka

verses.devanagari: অগণ্যধন্যচৈতন্যগণানাং প্রেমবন্যয়া ।\\nনিন্যেঽধন্যজনস্বান্তমরুঃ শশ্বদনূপতাম্ ॥১॥
verses.transliteration: agaṇya-dhanya-caitanya-\\ngaṇānāṁ prema-vanyayā\\nninye 'dhanya-jana-svānta-\\nmaruḥ śaśvad anūpatām
verses.translation: The innumerable, glorious followers of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu brought a constant flood to the desertlike hearts of the unfortunate with an inundation of ecstatic love.

verses.devanagari: জয় জয় শ্রীকৃষ্ণচৈতন্য দয়াময় ।\\nজয় জয় নিত্যানন্দ করুণ-হৃদয় ॥২॥
verses.transliteration: jaya jaya śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya dayāmaya\\njaya jaya nityānanda karuṇa-hṛdaya
verses.translation: All glories to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the most merciful incarnation! All glories to Lord Nityānanda, whose heart is always compassionate!

verses.devanagari: জয়াদ্বৈতাচার্য জয় জয় দয়াময় ।\\nজয় গৌরভক্তগণ সব রসময় ॥৩॥
verses.transliteration: jayādvaitācārya jaya jaya dayāmaya\\njaya gaura-bhakta-gaṇa saba rasamaya
verses.translation: All glories to Advaita Ācārya, who is very merciful! All glories to the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who are always overwhelmed by transcendental bliss!

verses.devanagari: এইমত মহাপ্রভু ভক্তগণ-সঙ্গে ।\\nনীলাচলে বাস করেন কৃষ্ণপ্রেমরঙ্গে ॥৪॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata mahāprabhu bhakta-gaṇa-saṅge\\nnīlācale vāsa karena kṛṣṇa-prema-raṅge
verses.translation: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu lived at Nīlācala [Jagannātha Purī] with His personal devotees, always merged in ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: অন্তরে-বাহিরে কৃষ্ণবিরহ-তরঙ্গ ।\\nনানা-ভাবে ব্যাকুল প্রভুর মন আর অঙ্গ ॥৫॥
verses.transliteration: antare-bāhire kṛṣṇa-viraha-taraṅga\\nnānā-bhāve vyākula prabhura mana āra aṅga
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu always felt waves of separation from Kṛṣṇa, externally and internally. His mind and body were agitated by various spiritual transformations.

verses.devanagari: দিনে নৃত্য-কীর্তন, জগন্নাথ-দরশন ।\\nরাত্র্যে রায়-স্বরূপ-সনে রস-আস্বাদন ॥৬॥
verses.transliteration: dine nṛtya-kīrtana, jagannātha-daraśana\\nrātrye rāya-svarūpa-sane rasa-āsvādana
verses.translation: During the day He chanted, danced and saw Lord Jagannātha in the temple. At night He tasted transcendental bliss in the company of Rāmānanda Rāya and Svarūpa Dāmodara.

verses.devanagari: ত্রিজগতের লোক আসি’ করেন দরশন ।\\nযেই দেখে, সেই পায় কৃষ্ণপ্রেম-ধন ॥৭॥
verses.transliteration: trijagatera loka āsi' karena daraśana\\nyei dekhe, sei pāya kṛṣṇa-prema-dhana
verses.translation: People from the three worlds used to come visit Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Anyone who saw Him received the transcendental treasure of love for Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: মনুষ্যের বেশে দেব-গন্ধর্ব-কিন্নর ।\\nসপ্তপাতালের যত দৈত্য বিষধর ॥৮॥
verses.transliteration: manuṣyera veśe deva-gandharva-kinnara\\nsapta-pātālera yata daitya viṣadhara
verses.translation: The inhabitants of the seven higher planetary systems-including the demigods, the Gandharvas and the Kinnaras-and the inhabitants of the seven lower planetary systems [Pātālaloka], including the demons and serpentine living entities, all visited Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in the dress of human beings.

verses.devanagari: সপ্তদীপে নবখণ্ডে বৈসে যত জন ।\\nনানা-বেশে আসি’ করে প্রভুর দরশন ॥৯॥
verses.transliteration: sapta-dvīpe nava-khaṇḍe vaise yata jana\\nnānā-veśe āsi' kare prabhura daraśana
verses.translation: Dressed in different ways, people from the seven islands and nine khaṇḍas visited Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: প্রহ্লাদ, বলি, ব্যাস, শুক আদি মুনিগণ ।\\nআসি’ প্রভু দেখি’ প্রেমে হয় অচেতন ॥১০॥
verses.transliteration: prahlāda, bali, vyāsa, śuka ādi muni-gaṇa\\nāsi' prabhu dekhi' preme haya acetana
verses.translation: Prahlāda Mahārāja, Bali Mahārāja, Vyāsadeva, Śukadeva Gosvāmī and other great sages came to visit Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Upon seeing Him, they became unconscious in ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
According to the opinion of some historians, Prahlāda Mahārāja was born in Tretā-yuga in the city of Mūlatāna in the state of Punjab. He was born of Hiraṇyakaśipu, a king of the dynasty of Kaśyapa. Prahlāda Mahārāja was a great devotee of Lord Viṣṇu, but his father was very much against Viṣṇu. Because the father and son thus differed in their consciousness, the demon father inflicted all kinds of bodily pain upon Prahlāda. When this torture became intolerable, the Supreme Lord appeared as Nṛsiṁhadeva and killed the great demon Hiraṇyakaśipu.
Bali Mahārāja was the grandson of Prahlāda Mahārāja. The son of Prahlāda Mahārāja was Virocana, and his son was known as Bali. Appearing as Vāmana and begging Bali Mahārāja for three feet of land, the Lord took possession of the entire three worlds. Thus Bali Mahārāja became a great devotee of Lord Vāmana. Bali Mahārāja had one hundred sons, of whom Mahārāja Bāṇa was the eldest and most famous.
Vyāsadeva was the son of the great sage Parāśara. Other names for him are Sātyavateya and Kṛṣṇa-dvaipāyana Bādarāyaṇa Muni. As one of the authorities on the
Vedas,
he divided the original
Veda,
for convenience, into four divisions—
Sāma, Yajur, Ṛg
and
Atharva.
He is the author of eighteen
Purāṇas
as well as the theosophical thesis
Brahma-sūtra
and its natural commentary,
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.
He belongs to the Brahma-sampradāya and is a direct disciple of Nārada Muni.
Śukadeva Gosvāmī is the son of Vyāsadeva. He was a
brahmacārī
fully conscious of Brahman realization, but later he became a great devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa. He narrated
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
to Mahārāja Parīkṣit.

verses.devanagari: বাহিরে ফুকারে লোক, দর্শন না পাঞা ।\\n‘কৃষ্ণ কহ’ বলেন প্রভু বাহিরে আসিয়া ॥১১॥
verses.transliteration: bāhire phukāre loka, darśana nā pāñā\\n'kṛṣṇa kaha' balena prabhu bāhire āsiyā
verses.translation: Being unable to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the populace outside His room would make a tumultuous sound. Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would go outside and tell them, "Chant Hare Kṛṣṇa."

verses.devanagari: প্রভুর দর্শনে সব লোক প্রেমে ভাসে ।\\nএইমত যায় প্রভুর রাত্রি-দিবসে ॥১২॥
verses.transliteration: prabhura darśane saba loka preme bhāse\\nei-mata yāya prabhura rātri-divase
verses.translation: All kinds of people would come to see the Lord, and upon seeing Him they would be overwhelmed with ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa. In this way Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed His days and nights.

verses.devanagari: একদিন লোক আসি’ প্রভুরে নিবেদিল ।\\nগোপীনাথেরে ‘বড় জানা’ চাঙ্গে চড়াইল ॥১৩॥
verses.transliteration: eka-dina loka āsi' prabhure nivedila\\ngopīnāthere 'baḍa jānā' cāṅge caḍāila
verses.translation: One day people suddenly came to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and informed Him, "Gopīnātha Paṭṭanāyaka, the son of Bhavānanda Rāya, has been condemned to death by the baḍa-jānā, the eldest son of the King, and has been raised on the cāṅga.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The
cāṅga
was a device for killing a condemned person. It consisted of a raised platform on which the condemned was made to stand. Underneath the platform, there were stationary upright swords. The condemned man would be pushed down onto the swords, and in this way he would die. For some reason, Gopīnātha Paṭṭanāyaka had been condemned to death and had therefore been raised upon the
cāṅga.

verses.devanagari: তলে খড়্গ পাতি’ তারে উপরে ডারিবে ।\\nপ্রভু রক্ষা করেন যবে, তবে নিস্তারিবে ॥১৪॥
verses.transliteration: tale khaḍga pāti' tāre upare ḍāribe\\nprabhu rakṣā karena yabe, tabe nistāribe
verses.translation: "He has placed swords beneath the platform," they said, "and will throw Gopīnātha upon them. O Lord, only if You protect him will he be saved.

verses.devanagari: সবংশে তোমার সেবক — ভবানন্দ-রায় ।\\nতাঁর পুত্র — তোমার সেবকে রাখিতে যুয়ায় ॥১৫॥
verses.transliteration: savaṁśe tomāra sevaka—bhavānanda-rāya\\ntāṅra putra—tomāra sevake rākhite yuyāya
verses.translation: "Bhavānanda Rāya and his entire family are your servants. Therefore it is quite fitting for You to save the son of Bhavānanda Rāya."

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহে, — ‘রাজা কেনে করয়ে তাড়ন ?’\\nতবে সেই লোক কহে সব বিবরণ ॥১৬॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahe,—'rājā kene karaye tāḍana?'\\ntabe sei loka kahe saba vivaraṇa
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu inquired, "Why is the King chastising him?" Thereupon the people described the entire incident.

verses.devanagari: “গোপীনাথ-পট্টনায়ক — রামানন্দ-ভাই ।\\nসর্বকাল হয় তেঁহ রাজবিষয়ী ॥১৭॥
verses.transliteration: "gopīnātha-paṭṭanāyaka—rāmānanda-bhāi\\nsarva-kāla haya teṅha rāja-viṣayī
verses.translation: They said, "Gopīnātha Paṭṭanāyaka, the brother of Rāmānanda Rāya, has always been a treasurer for the government.

verses.devanagari: ‘মালজাঠ্যা-দণ্ডপাটে’ তার অধিকার ।\\nসাধি’ পাড়ি’ আনি’ দ্রব্য দিল রাজদ্বার ॥১৮॥
verses.transliteration: 'mālajāṭhyā-daṇḍapāṭe' tāra adhikāra\\nsādhi' pāḍi' āni' dravya dila rāja-dvāra
verses.translation: "He served in the place known as Mālajāṭhyā Daṇḍapāta, soliciting and collecting money there and depositing it in the government treasury.

verses.devanagari: দুইলক্ষ কাহন তার ঠাঞি বাকী হইল ।\\nদুইলক্ষ কাহন কৌড়ি রাজা ত’ মাগিল ॥১৯॥
verses.transliteration: dui-lakṣa kāhana tāra ṭhāñi bākī ha-ila\\ndui-lakṣa kāhana kauḍi rājā ta' māgila
verses.translation: "Once when he deposited the collection, however, a balance of 200,000 kāhanas of conchshells was due from him. Therefore the King demanded this sum.

verses.devanagari: তেঁহ কহে, — “স্থূলদ্রব্য নাহি যে গণি’ দিব ।\\nক্রমে-ক্রমে বেচি’ কিনি’ দ্রব্য ভরিব ॥২০॥
verses.transliteration: teṅha kahe,—"sthūla-dravya nāhi ye gaṇi' diba\\nkrame-krame veci' kini' dravya bhariba
verses.translation: "Gopīnātha Paṭṭanāyaka replied,'There is no money I can immediately give you in cash. Please give me time. Gradually I shall purchase and sell my gross goods and in this way fill your treasury.

verses.devanagari: ঘোড়া দশ-বার হয়, লহ’ মূল্য করি’ ।\\nএত বলি’ ঘোড়া আনে রাজদ্বারে ধরি’ ॥২১॥
verses.transliteration: ghoḍā daśa-bāra haya, laha' mūlya kari' "\\neta bali' ghoḍā āne rāja-dvāre dhari'
verses.translation: "There are ten to twelve good horses. Take them immediately for a proper price.' After saying this, he brought all the horses to the door of the King.

verses.devanagari: এক রাজপুত্র ঘোড়ার মূল্য ভাল জানে ।\\nতারে পাঠাইল রাজা পাত্র-মিত্র সনে ॥২২॥
verses.transliteration: eka rāja-putra ghoḍāra mūlya bhāla jāne\\ntāre pāṭhāila rājā pātra-mitra sane
verses.translation: "One of the princes knew how to estimate the price of horses very well. Thus the King sent for him to come with his ministers and friends.

verses.devanagari: সেই রাজপুত্র মূল্য করে ঘাটাঞা ।\\nগোপীনাথের ক্রোধ হৈল মূল্য শুনিয়া ॥২৩॥
verses.transliteration: sei rāja-putra mūlya kare ghāṭāñā\\ngopīnāthera krodha haila mūlya śuniyā
verses.translation: "The prince, however, purposely gave a reduced estimate for the value of the horses. When Gopīnātha Paṭṭanāyaka heard the price quoted, he was very angry.

verses.devanagari: সেই রাজপুত্রের স্বভাব, — গ্রীবা ফিরায় ।\\nঊর্ধ্বমুখে বারবার ইতি-উতি চায় ॥২৪॥
verses.transliteration: sei rāja-putrera svabhāva,—grīvā phirāya\\nūrdhva-mukhe bāra-bāra iti-uti cāya
verses.translation: "That prince had a personal idiosyncrasy of turning his neck and facing the sky, looking here and there again and again.

verses.devanagari: তারে নিন্দা করি’ কহে সগর্ব বচনে  ।\\nরাজা কৃপা করে তাতে ভয় নাহি মানে ॥২৫॥
verses.transliteration: tāre nindā kari' kahe sagarva vacane\\nrājā kṛpā kare tāte bhaya nāhi māne
verses.translation: "Gopīnātha Paṭṭanāyaka criticized the prince. He was unafraid of the prince because the King was very kind toward him.

verses.devanagari: ‘আমার ঘোড়া গ্রীবা না ফিরায় ঊর্ধ্বে নাহি চায়  ।\\nতাতে ঘোড়ার মূল্য ঘাটি করিতে না যুয়ায় ।।’ ২৬ ॥২৬॥
verses.transliteration: 'āmāra ghoḍā grīvā nā phirāya ūrdhve nāhi cāya\\ntāte ghoḍāra mūlya ghāṭi karite nā yuyāya'
verses.translation: "Gopīnātha Paṭṭanāyaka said, 'My horses never turn their necks or look upward. Therefore the price for them should not be reduced.'

verses.devanagari: শুনি’ রাজপুত্র-মনে ক্রোধ উপজিল ।\\nরাজার ঠাঞি যাই’ বহু লাগানি করিল ॥২৭॥
verses.transliteration: śuni' rājaputra-mane krodha upajila\\nrājāra ṭhāñi yāi' bahu lāgāni karila
verses.translation: "Hearing this criticism, the prince became very angry. Going before the King, he made some false allegations against Gopīnātha Paṭṭanāyaka.

verses.devanagari: “কৌড়ি নাহি দিবে এই, বেড়ায় ছদ্ম করি’ ।\\nআজ্ঞা দেহ যদি, — ‘চাঙ্গে চড়াঞা লই কৌড়ি’ ॥২৮॥
verses.transliteration: "kauḍi nāhi dibe ei, beḍāya chadma kari'\\nājñā deha yadi,—'cāṅge caḍāñā la-i kauḍi'
verses.translation: "This Gopīnātha Paṭṭanāyaka,' he said,'is unwilling to pay the money due. Instead, he is squandering it under some pretext. If you issue an order, I can put him on the cāṅga and thus realize the money.'

verses.devanagari: রাজা বলে, — “যেই ভাল, সেই কর যায় ।\\nযে উপায়ে কৌড়ি পাই, কর সে উপায় ।।” ॥ ২৯ ॥
verses.transliteration: rājā bale,—"yei bhāla, sei kara yāya\\nye upāye kauḍi pāi, kara se upāya"
verses.translation: "The King replied, 'You can adopt whatever means you think best. Any device by which you can somehow or other realize the money is all right.'

verses.devanagari: রাজপুত্র আসি’ তারে চাঙ্গে চড়াইল ।\\nখড়্গ-উপরে ফেলাইতে তলে খড়্গ পাতিল ।।” ॥ ৩০ ॥
verses.transliteration: rāja-putra āsi' tāre cāṅge caḍāila\\nkhaḍaga-upare phelāite tale khaḍaga pātila"
verses.translation: "Thus the prince went back, raised Gopīnātha Paṭṭanāyaka onto the platform of the cāṅga and spread swords below upon which to throw him."

verses.devanagari: শুনি’ প্রভু কহে কিছু করি’ প্রণয়-রোষ ।\\n“রাজ-কৌড়ি দিতে নারে, রাজার কিবা দোষ ? ॥ ৩১ ॥
verses.transliteration: śuni' prabhu kahe kichu kari' praṇaya-roṣa\\n"rāja-kauḍi dite nāre, rājāra kibā doṣa?
verses.translation: After hearing this explanation, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied with affectionate anger. "Gopīnātha Paṭṭanāyaka does not want to pay dues to the King," the Lord said. "How then is the King at fault in punishing him?

verses.devanagari: রাজ-বিলাত্ সাধি’ খায়, নাহি রাজ-ভয় ।\\nদারী-নাটুয়ারে দিয়া করে নানা ব্যয় ॥৩২॥
verses.transliteration: rāja-bilāt sādhi' khāya, nāhi rāja-bhaya\\ndārī-nāṭuyāre diyā kare nānā vyaya
verses.translation: "Gopīnātha Paṭṭanāyaka is in charge of collecting money on behalf of the government, but he misappropriates it. Not fearing the King, he squanders it to see dancing girls.

verses.devanagari: যেই চতুর, সেই করুক রাজ-বিষয় ।\\nরাজ-দ্রব্য শোধি’ পায়, তার করুক ব্যয় ।।” ॥ ৩৩ ॥
verses.transliteration: yei catura, sei kuruka rāja-viṣaya\\nrāja-dravya śodhi' pāya, tāra karuka vyaya"
verses.translation: "If one is intelligent, let him perform service to the government, and after paying the government, he can spend whatever money is left."

verses.devanagari: হেন-কালে আর লোক আইল ধাঞা ।\\n‘বাণীনাথাদি সবংশে লঞা গেল বান্ধিয়া’ ॥৩৪॥
verses.transliteration: hena-kāle āra loka āila dhāñā\\n'vāṇīnāthādi savaṁśe lañā gela bāndhiyā'
verses.translation: At that time another person came there in great haste, bringing the news that Vāṇīnātha Rāya and his entire family had been arrested.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহে, — “রাজা আপনে লেখার দ্রব্য লইব ।\\nআমি — বিরক্ত সন্ন্যাসী, তাহে কি করিব ? ॥ ৩৫ ॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahe,—"rājā āpane lekhāra dravya la-iba\\nāmi—virakta sannyāsī, tāhe ki kariba?"
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "The King must personally realize the dues. I am but a sannyāsī, a member of the renounced order. What can I do?"

verses.devanagari: তবে স্বরূপাদি যত প্রভুর ভক্তগণ  ।\\nপ্রভুর চরণে সবে কৈলা নিবেদন ॥৩৬॥
verses.transliteration: tabe svarūpādi yata prabhura bhakta-gaṇa\\nprabhura caraṇe sabe kailā nivedana
verses.translation: Then all the devotees, headed by Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, fell at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and submitted the following plea.

verses.devanagari: “রামানন্দ-রায়ের গোষ্ঠী, সব — তোমার ‘দাস’  ।\\nতোমার উচিত নহে ঐছন উদাস ।।” ৩৭ ॥৩৭॥
verses.transliteration: "rāmānanda-rāyera goṣṭhī, saba—tomāra 'dāsa'\\ntomāra ucita nahe aichana udāsa"
verses.translation: "All the members of Rāmānanda Rāya's family are Your eternal servants. Now they are in danger. It is not befitting for You to be indifferent to them in this way."

verses.devanagari: শুনি’ মহাপ্রভু কহে সক্রোধ বচনে । “মোরে আজ্ঞা দেহ’ সবে, যাঙ রাজস্থানে ! ৩৮ ।। তোমা-সবার এই মত, — রাজ-ঠাঞি যাঞা  ।\\nকৌড়ি মাগি’ লঙ্ মুঞি আঁচল পাতিয়া ॥৩৮॥
verses.transliteration: śuni' mahāprabhu kahe sakrodha vacane\\n"more ājñā deha' sabe, yāṅa rāja-sthāne!
verses.translation: After hearing this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu spoke in an angry mood. "You want to order Me to go to the King," He said.

verses.devanagari: তোমাসবার এই মত, — রাজঠাঞি যাঞা ।\\nকৌডি মাগি' লঙ্ মুঞি আঙ্চল পাতিয়া ॥৩৯॥
verses.transliteration: tomā-sabāra ei mata,—rāja-ṭhāñi yāñā\\nkauḍi māgi' laṅ muñi āṅcala pātiyā
verses.translation: "Your opinion is that I should go to the King's palace and spread My cloth to beg money from him.

verses.devanagari: পাঁচগণ্ডার পাত্র হয় সন্ন্যাসী ব্রাহ্মণ ।\\nমাগিলে বা কেনে দিবে দুইলক্ষ কাহন ?” ॥ ৪০ ॥
verses.transliteration: pāṅca-gaṇḍāra pātra haya sannyāsī brāhmaṇa\\nmāgile vā kene dibe dui-lakṣa kāhana?"
verses.synonyms:
pāṅca-gaṇḍāra
—of five
gaṇḍās
;
pātra
—due recipients;
haya
—are;
sannyāsī brāhmaṇa
—
sannyāsīs
and
brāhmaṇas
;
māgile
—by begging;
vā
—or;
kene
—why;
dibe
—shall give;
dui-lakṣa kāhana
—200,000
kāhanas
of
kauḍis.
verses.translation: "Of course, a sannyāsī or brāhmaṇa may beg for up to five gaṇḍās, but why should he be granted the inappropriate sum of 200,000 kāhanas of conchshells?"

verses.devanagari: হেনকালে আর লোক আইল ধাঞা ।\\nখড়্গের উপরে গোপীনাথে দিতেছে ডারিয়া ॥৪১॥
verses.transliteration: hena-kāle āra loka āila dhāñā\\nkhaḍegara upare gopīnāthe diteche ḍāriyā
verses.translation: Then another person came with the news that Gopīnātha had already been set up to be thrown upon the points of the swords.

verses.devanagari: শুনি’ প্রভুর গণ প্রভুরে করে অনুনয় ।\\nপ্রভু কহে, — “আমি ভিক্ষুক, আমা হৈতে কিছু নয় ॥৪২॥
verses.transliteration: śuni' prabhura gaṇa prabhure kare anunaya\\nprabhu kahe,—"āmi bhikṣuka, āmā haite kichu naya
verses.translation: Hearing this news, all the devotees again appealed to the Lord, but the Lord replied, "I am a beggar. It is impossible for Me to do anything about this.

verses.devanagari: তাতে রক্ষা করিতে যদি হয় সবার মনে ।\\nসবে মেলি’ জানাহ জগন্নাথের চরণে ॥৪৩॥
verses.transliteration: tāte rakṣā karite yadi haya sabāra mane\\nsabe meli' jānāha jagannāthera caraṇe
verses.translation: "Therefore if you want to save him, you should all pray together at the lotus feet of Jagannātha.

verses.devanagari: ঈশ্বর জগন্নাথ, — যাঁর হাতে সর্ব ‘অর্থ’ ।\\nকর্তুমকর্তুমন্যথা করিতে সমর্থ ।।” ॥ ৪৪ ॥
verses.transliteration: īśvara jagannātha,—yāṅra hāte sarva 'artha'\\nkartum akartum anyathā karite samartha"
verses.translation: "Lord Jagannātha is the Supreme Personality of Godhead. He possesses all potencies. Therefore He is able to act freely and can do and undo whatever He likes."

verses.devanagari: ইহাঁ যদি মহাপ্রভু এতেক কহিলা  ।\\nহরিচন্দন-পাত্র যাই’ রাজারে কহিলা ॥৪৫॥
verses.transliteration: ihāṅ yadi mahāprabhu eteka kahilā\\nharicandana-pātra yāi' rājāre kahilā
verses.translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied in this way, an officer named Haricandana Pātra went to the King and spoke with him.

verses.devanagari: “গোপীনাথ-পট্টনায়ক — সেবক তোমার  ।\\nসেবকের প্রাণদণ্ড নহে ব্যবহার ॥৪৬॥
verses.transliteration: "gopīnātha-paṭṭanāyaka—sevaka tomāra\\nsevakera prāṇa-daṇḍa nahe vyavahāra
verses.translation: "After all," he said, "Gopīnātha Paṭṭanāyaka is your faithful servant. To condemn a servant to death is not good behavior.

verses.devanagari: বিশেষ তাহার ঠাঞি কৌড়ি বাকী হয় ।\\nপ্রাণ নিলে কিবা লাভ? নিজ ধনক্ষয় ॥৪৭॥
verses.transliteration: viśeṣa tāhāra ṭhāñi kauḍi bākī haya\\nprāṇa nile kibā lābha? nija dhana-kṣaya
verses.translation: "His only fault is that he owes some money to the government. If he is killed, however, what profit will there be? The government will be the loser, for it will not get the money.

verses.devanagari: যথার্থ মূল্যে ঘোড়া লহ, যেবা বাকী হয় ।\\nক্রমে ক্রমে দিবে, ব্যর্থ প্রাণ কেনে লয় ।।” ॥ ৪৮ ॥
verses.transliteration: yathārtha mūlye ghoḍā laha, yebā bākī haya\\nkrame krame dibe, vyartha prāṇa kene laya"
verses.translation: "It would be better to take the horses for a proper price and let him gradually repay the balance. Why are you killing him unnecessarily?"

verses.devanagari: রাজা কহে, — “এই বাত্ আমি নাহি জানি ।\\nপ্রাণ কেনে লইব, তার দ্রব্য চাহি আমি ॥৪৯॥
verses.transliteration: rājā kahe,—"ei vāt āmi nāhi jāni\\nprāṇa kene la-iba, tāra dravya cāhi āmi
verses.translation: The King answered in surprise, "I did not know about all this. Why should his life be taken? I only want the money from him.

verses.devanagari: তুমি যাই’ কর তাহাঁ সর্ব সমাধান ।\\nদ্রব্য যৈছে আইসে, আর রহে তার প্রাণ ।।” ॥ ৫০ ॥
verses.transliteration: tumi yāi' kara tāhāṅ sarva samādhāna\\ndravya yaiche āise, āra rahe tāra prāṇa"
verses.translation: "Go there and adjust everything. I want only the payment, not his life."

verses.devanagari: তবে হরিচন্দন আসি’ জানারে কহিল ।\\nচাঙ্গে হৈতে গোপীনাথে শীঘ্র নামাইল ॥৫১॥
verses.transliteration: tabe haricandana āsi' jānāre kahila\\ncāṅge haite gopīnāthe śīghra nāmāila
verses.translation: Haricandana then returned and informed the prince of the King's desire, and immediately Gopīnātha Paṭṭanāyaka was taken down from the cāṅga.

verses.devanagari: ‘দ্রব্য দেহ’ রাজা মাগে — উপায় পুছিল  ।\\n‘যথার্থ-মূল্যে ঘোড়া লহ’, তেঁহ ত’ কহিল ॥৫২॥
verses.transliteration: 'dravya deha' rājā māge—upāya puchila\\n'yathārtha-mūlye ghoḍā laha', teṅha ta' kahila
verses.translation: Then he was told that the King demanded the money due him and asked what means he would adopt to pay it. "Kindly take my horses," he replied, "for a proper price.

verses.devanagari: ‘ক্রমে ক্রমে দিমু, আর যত কিছু পারি  ।\\nঅবিচারে প্রাণ লহ, — কি বলিতে পারি ?’ ৫৩ ॥৫৩॥
verses.transliteration: 'krame krame dimu, āra yata kichu pāri\\navicāre prāṇa laha,—ki balite pāri?'
verses.translation: "I shall gradually pay the balance as I can. Without consideration, however, you were going to take my life. What can I say?"

verses.devanagari: যথার্থ মূল্য করি’ তবে সব ঘোড়া লইল ।\\nআর দ্রব্যের মুদ্দতী করি’ ঘরে পাঠাইল ॥৫৪॥
verses.transliteration: yathārtha mūlya kari' tabe saba ghoḍā la-ila\\nāra dravyera muddatī kari' ghare pāṭhāila
verses.translation: Then the government took all the horses for a proper price, a time was set for payment of the balance, and Gopīnātha Paṭṭanāyaka was released.

verses.devanagari: এথা প্রভু সেই মনুষ্যেরে প্রশ্ন কৈল ।\\n“বাণীনাথ কি করে, যবে বান্ধিয়া আনিল ?” ॥ ৫৫ ॥
verses.transliteration: ethā prabhu sei manuṣyere praśna kaila\\n"vāṇīnātha ki kare, yabe bāndhiyā ānila?"
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu inquired from the messenger, "What was Vāṇīnātha doing when he was arrested and brought there?"

verses.devanagari: সে কহে — “বাণীনাথ নির্ভয়ে লয় কৃষ্ণনাম ।\\n‘হরে কৃষ্ণ, হরে কৃষ্ণ’ কহে অবিশ্রাম ॥৫৬॥
verses.transliteration: se kahe—"vāṇīnātha nirbhaye laya kṛṣṇa-nāma\\n'hare kṛṣṇa, hare kṛṣṇa' kahe aviśrāma
verses.translation: The messenger replied, "He was fearlessly, incessantly chanting the mahā-mantra-Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare Hare Rāma, Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma, Hare Hare.

verses.devanagari: সংখ্যা লাগি’ দুই-হাতে অঙ্গুলীতে লেখা ।\\nসহস্রাদি পূর্ণ হৈলে, অঙ্গে কাটে রেখা ।।” ॥ ৫৭ ॥
verses.transliteration: saṅkhyā lāgi' dui-hāte aṅgulīte lekhā\\nsahasrādi pūrṇa haile, aṅge kāṭe rekhā"
verses.translation: "He counted the chants on the fingers of both hands, and after he had finished chanting one thousand times, he would make a mark on his body."

verses.devanagari: শুনি’ মহাপ্রভু হইলা পরম আনন্দ ।\\nকে বুঝিতে পারে গৌরের কৃপা-ছন্দবন্ধ ? ॥ ৫৮ ॥
verses.transliteration: śuni' mahāprabhu ha-ilā parama ānanda\\nke bujhite pāre gaurera kṛpā-chanda-bandha?
verses.translation: Hearing this news, the Lord was very pleased. Who can understand the mercy of the Lord upon His devotee?

verses.devanagari: হেনকালে কাশীমিশ্র আইলা প্রভু-স্থানে ।\\nপ্রভু তাঁরে কহে কিছু সোদ্বেগ-বচনে ॥৫৯॥
verses.transliteration: hena-kāle kāśī-miśra āilā prabhu-sthāne\\nprabhu tāṅre kahe kichu sodvega-vacane
verses.translation: At that time Kāśī Miśra came to the residence of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and the Lord talked with him with some agitation.

verses.devanagari: “ইহাঁ রহিতে নারি, যামু আলালনাথ ।\\nনানা উপদ্রব ইহাঁ, না পাই সোয়াথ ।।” ॥ ৬০ ॥
verses.transliteration: "ihāṅ rahite nāri, yāmu ālālanātha\\nnānā upadrava ihāṅ, nā pāi soyātha"
verses.translation: "I cannot stay here any longer," the Lord said. "I shall go to Ālālanātha. There are too many disturbances here, and I cannot get any rest.

verses.devanagari: ভবানন্দ-রায়ের গোষ্ঠী করে রাজবিষয় ।\\nনানা-প্রকারে করে তারা রাজদ্রব্য ব্যয় ॥৬১॥
verses.transliteration: bhavānanda-rāyera goṣṭhī kare rāja-viṣaya\\nnānā-prakāre kare tārā rāja-dravya vyaya
verses.translation: "All the family members of Bhavānanda Rāya are engaged in government service, but they spend the government's revenue in various ways.

verses.devanagari: রাজার কি দোষ? রাজা নিজ-দ্রব্য চায় ।\\nদিতে নারে দ্রব্য, দণ্ড আমারে জানায় ॥৬২॥
verses.transliteration: rājāra ki doṣa rājā nija-dravya cāya\\ndite nāre dravya, daṇḍa āmāre jānāya
verses.translation: "What is the fault on the part of the King? He wants the government's money. However, when they are punished for failing to pay the government its due, they come to Me to release them.

verses.devanagari: রাজা গোপীনাথে যদি চাঙ্গে চড়াইল ।\\nচারিবারে লোকে আসি’ মোরে জানাইল ॥৬৩॥
verses.transliteration: rājā gopīnāthe yadi cāṅge caḍāila\\ncāri-bāre loke āsi' more jānāila
verses.translation: "When the King put Gopīnātha Paṭṭanāyaka on the cāṅga, messengers came four times to inform Me about the incident.

verses.devanagari: ভিক্ষুক সন্ন্যাসী আমি নির্জনবাসী ।\\nআমায় দুঃখ দেয়, নিজ-দুঃখ কহি’ আসি’ ॥৬৪॥
verses.transliteration: bhikṣuka sannyāsī āmi nirjana-vāsī\\nāmāya duḥkha deya, nija-duḥkha kahi' āsi'
verses.translation: "As a beggar sannyāsī, a mendicant, I wish to live alone in a solitary place, but these people come to tell Me about their unhappiness and disturb Me.

verses.devanagari: আজি তারে জগন্নাথ করিলা রক্ষণ ।\\nকালি কে রাখিবে, যদি না দিবে রাজধন ? ॥ ৬৫ ॥
verses.transliteration: āji tāre jagannātha karilā rakṣaṇa\\nkāli ke rākhibe, yadi nā dibe rāja-dhana?
verses.translation: "Jagannātha has saved him once from death today, but if tomorrow he again does not pay what he owes the treasury, who will give him protection?
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The Supreme Personality of Godhead will certainly protect a devotee who does something sinful accidentally. As the Lord says in
Bhagavad-gītā
(9.30-31):
api cet sudurācāro
bhajate mām ananya-bhāk
sādhur eva sa mantavyaḥ
saṁyag vyavasito hi saḥ
kṣipraṁ bhavati dharmātmā
śaśvac-chāntiṁ nigacchati
kaunteya pratijānīhi
na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati
"Even if one commits the most abominable actions, if he is engaged in devotional service, he is to be considered saintly because he is properly situated. He quickly becomes righteous and attains lasting peace. O son of Kuntī, declare it boldly that My devotee never perishes." However, if a devotee or so-called devotee purposefully commits sinful activities continually in the hope that Kṛṣṇa will give him protection, Kṛṣṇa will not protect him. Therefore Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said,
kāli ke rākhibe, yadi nā dibe rāja-dhana?:
"Jagannātha has saved Gopīnātha Paṭṭanāyaka from being killed by the King today, but if he commits the same offense again, who will give him protection?" Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thus warns all such foolish devotees that Jagannātha will not protect them if they continue to commit offenses.

verses.devanagari: বিষয়ীর বার্তা শুনি’ ক্ষুব্ধ হয় মন ।\\nতাতে ইঁহা রহি’ মোর নাহি প্রয়োজন ।।” ॥ ৬৬ ॥
verses.transliteration: viṣayīra vārtā śuni' kṣubdha haya mana\\ntāte ihāṅ rahi' mora nāhi prayojana"
verses.translation: "If we hear about the activities of materialistic persons, our minds become agitated. There is no need for Me to stay here and be disturbed in that way."

verses.devanagari: কাশীমিশ্র কহে প্রভুর ধরিয়া চরণে ।\\n“তুমি কেনে এই বাতে ক্ষোভ কর মনে ? ॥ ৬৭ ॥
verses.transliteration: kāśī-miśra kahe prabhura dhariyā caraṇe\\n"tumi kene ei vāte kṣobha kara mane?
verses.translation: Kāśī Miśra caught hold of the Lord's lotus feet and said, "Why should You be agitated by these affairs?

verses.devanagari: সন্ন্যাসী বিরক্ত তোমার কা-সনে সম্বন্ধ ?\\nব্যবহার লাগি’ তোমা ভজে, সেই জ্ঞান-অন্ধ ॥৬৮॥
verses.transliteration: sannyāsī virakta tomāra kā-sane sambandha?\\nvyavahāra lāgi' tomā bhaje, sei jñāna-andha
verses.translation: "You are a renounced sannyāsī. What connections do You have? One who worships You for some material purpose is blind to all knowledge."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Becoming a devotee of the Lord to serve material purposes is a great mistake. Many people become showbottle devotees for material profits. indeed materialistic persons sometimes take to professional devotional service and keep Viṣṇu, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, as a means of livelihood. None of this, however, is approved. In the book known as
Sapta-śatī,
as mentioned by Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura, one can discover how a person worshiping the goddess Durgā begs her for different varieties of material profit. Such activities are very popular among people in general, but they are the attempts of foolish, blind people (
sei jñāna-andha).
A materialist does not actually know why one should become a devotee. A devotee's only concern is to satisfy the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Pure devotional service is defined by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī:
anyābhilāṣitā-śūnyaṁ
jñāna-karmādy-anāvṛtam
ānukūlyena kṛṣṇānu-
śīlanaṁ bhaktir uttamā
One should be completely free from all material desires and should serve Kṛṣṇa simply to please Him. When people become interested in their own sense gratification (
bhukti mukti siddhi kāmī),
some of them desire to enjoy the material world to the fullest extent, some of them desire to be liberated and merge into the existence of Brahman, and others want to perform magic through mystic power and thus become incarnations of God. These are all against the principles of devotional service. One must be free from all material desires. The desire of the impersonalist to merge into the existence of Brahman is also material because such an impersonalist wants to gratify his senses by merging into the existence of Kṛṣṇa instead of serving His lotus feet. Even if such a person merges into the Brahman effulgence, he falls down again into material existence. As stated in
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(10.2.32):
āruhya kṛcchreṇa paraṁ padaṁ tataḥ
patanty adho 'nādṛta-yuṣmad-aṅghrayaḥ
Because Māyāvādī philosophers have no information regarding the transcendental service of the Lord, even after attaining liberation from material activities and merging in the Brahman effulgence, they must come down again to this material world.

verses.devanagari: তোমার ভজন-ফলে তোমাতে ‘প্রেমধন’ ।\\nবিষয় লাগি’ তোমায় ভজে, সেই মূর্খ জন ॥৬৯॥
verses.transliteration: tomāra bhajana-phale tomāte 'prema-dhana'\\nviṣaya lāgi' tomāya bhaje, sei mūrkha jana
verses.translation: Kāśī Miśra continued, "If one engages in devotional service for Your satisfaction, this will result in his increasingly awakening his dormant love for You. But if one engages in Your devotional service for material purposes, he should be considered a number-one fool.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura comments that there are many materialistic persons who become preachers,
gurus,
religionists or philosophers only for the sake of maintaining a high standard of living and sense gratification for themselves and their families. Sometimes they adopt the dress of a
sannyāsī
or preacher. They train some of their family members as lawyers and continually seek help from a high court to acquire riches on the plea of maintaining temples.
